title: Implement MVCC Version Chain XOR Delta Compression (§3.4.4)
description:
Implement XOR delta compression for MVCC version chains to reduce memory usage (§3.4.4, spec lines 1855-2018).

PROBLEM: Version chains store full copies of each page version. For pages where only a few bytes change per transaction, this wastes memory.

SOLUTION (normative): Store diffs as XOR deltas (optionally sparse-encoded) between adjacent versions in the chain. Deltas are compression, not erasure coding. RaptorQ applies at the ECS object level for durability of delta objects just like any other object.

CRITICAL CLARIFICATION: The delta is a plain XOR (or sparse-encoded XOR), NOT a RaptorQ encoding of the delta. Two separate concerns:
  - Delta compression: XOR(V_old, V_new) -> sparse representation
  - Durability: The resulting delta object is stored as an ECS object and MAY have RaptorQ repair symbols generated for it (like any ECS object)

VERSION CHAIN STRUCTURE (verbatim from spec):

  Version chain for page P:
    V3 (newest): full page data (4096 bytes)
    V2 delta: XOR(V2, V3)  (sparse encoding)
    V1 delta: XOR(V1, V2)  (sparse encoding)

  Reconstruction of V1:
    Start from V3 (full data)
    V2 = V3 XOR delta(V2,V3)
    V1 = V2 XOR delta(V1,V2)

  Space savings:
    If delta between versions is D bytes out of 4096:
    Full copy: 4096 bytes per version
    Sparse XOR delta: ~D bytes per version (plus small header/indices)

RECONSTRUCTION COST BOUND: Reconstructing the oldest version in a chain of depth L requires L-1 sequential delta applications starting from the newest (full) version. Theorem 5 (§5.5) bounds chain length to R * D + 1 where R is the write rate and D is the duration above the GC horizon; the GC scheduling policy (§5.6.5) targets a chain depth of ~8. This ensures delta reconstruction cost remains bounded and predictable.

WORKED EXAMPLE WITH ACTUAL BYTE VALUES (verbatim from spec):

Consider a B-tree leaf page (page 42) that undergoes three successive modifications:

V1 (TxnId=100): Original page (4096 bytes)
    Bytes 0-7:     [0D 00 00 00 03 0F E0 00]  (page header: leaf, 3 cells, cell offset)
    Bytes 8-99:    [cell pointer array + free block list]
    Bytes 100-999: [Cell 1: rowid=5, data="Alice"]
    Bytes 1000-1999: [Cell 2: rowid=10, data="Bob"]
    Bytes 2000-2999: [Cell 3: rowid=15, data="Charlie"]
    Bytes 3000-4095: [free space, all zeros]

V2 (TxnId=105): INSERT rowid=12
    Changes from V1:
    - Bytes 0-7 updated: cell count 3->4, cell content offset changes
    - Bytes 8-99: cell pointer array gains one entry
    - Bytes 2000-2099: Cell 3 shifted right by ~100 bytes
    - Bytes 1900-1999: New Cell 4 inserted (rowid=12, data="Dana")
    Delta size: ~300 bytes modified out of 4096

V3 (TxnId=110): UPDATE SET data="Robert" WHERE rowid=10
    Changes from V2:
    - Bytes 1000-1049: Cell 2 data changed from "Bob" to "Robert"
    - Bytes 0-7: cell content offset may change
    Delta size: ~60 bytes modified out of 4096

Storage under full-copy: 12,288 bytes (3 x 4096)
Storage under XOR delta:
  V3: 4096 bytes (full)
  V2 delta: ~88 bytes (60 non-zero bytes + header)
  V1 delta: ~348 bytes (300 non-zero bytes + header)
  Total: 4,532 bytes. Savings: 63% reduction.

SPARSE ENCODING FORMAT:
  delta_header (8 bytes): { magic: [u8;2]="XD", version: u8, flags: u8, nonzero_count: u32 }
  Followed by sequence of runs: (offset: u16, len: u16, data: [u8; len])

THRESHOLD ANALYSIS — use_delta FUNCTION (verbatim from spec):

  use_delta(old_page, new_page) -> bool:
      delta = old_page XOR new_page
      nonzero_bytes = count_nonzero(delta)

      // Fixed overhead: delta header (8 bytes) + sparse encoding overhead
      OVERHEAD = 16

      // Sparse delta size approximately nonzero_bytes * 1.05
      // (5% accounts for run headers/varints/padding for small deltas)
      estimated_delta_size = OVERHEAD + (nonzero_bytes as f64 * 1.05) as usize

      // COST MODEL (Extreme Optimization Discipline):
      // t_copy = page_size / mem_bandwidth     (full-page copy cost)
      // t_delta = delta_size / mem_bandwidth + delta_ops * t_per_op  (apply cost)
      // cache_benefit = (page_size - delta_size) * cache_value_per_byte
      //
      // Use delta when: cache_benefit > (t_delta - t_copy)
      // For page_size=4096, mem_bandwidth=40GB/s, t_per_op~1ns:
      //   t_copy = 100ns, t_delta(25% savings) = 75ns + 20ns = 95ns
      //   cache_benefit(25% savings) = 1024 bytes * cache pressure factor
      //
      // The 25% threshold (3072 bytes) is the crossover point where cache
      // capacity benefit outweighs marginal CPU cost.
      // Configurable via PRAGMA fsqlite.delta_threshold_pct (default: 25).
      return estimated_delta_size < page_size * 3 / 4

WORKLOAD EXPECTATIONS TABLE (verbatim from spec):

| Workload                    | Avg bytes changed | Delta size | Use delta? |
|-----------------------------|-------------------|------------|------------|
| Single-row UPDATE (leaf)    | 20-100            | ~120       | Yes (97% savings) |
| INSERT into leaf page       | 100-500           | ~540       | Yes (87% savings) |
| B-tree split (interior)     | 2048 (half page)  | ~2160      | Yes (47% savings) |
| VACUUM (page rewrite)       | 4096 (full page)  | ~4320      | No (delta > page) |
| Bulk INSERT (new page)      | 4096 (full page)  | ~4320      | No |

COMPRESSION RATIO TABLE (verbatim from spec):

| Workload                          | Avg versions/page | Avg delta | Compression ratio |
|-----------------------------------|-------------------|-----------|-------------------|
| OLTP (single-row updates)         | 5-10              | 50 bytes  | 10-15x            |
| Mixed read-write web app          | 3-5               | 200 bytes | 4-6x              |
| Batch import (sequential inserts) | 2-3               | 1500 bytes | 1.5-2x           |
| Analytics (read-heavy, few writes)| 1-2               | N/A       | 1x (no versions)  |

Particularly effective for B-tree interior pages where only child pointers change during splits, and for leaf pages where insertions affect only a portion of the page.

UNIT TESTS:

1. test_xor_delta_encode_small_change:
   Page with 50 bytes changed. Delta encodes to ~70 bytes.

2. test_xor_delta_encode_large_change:
   Page with 3000 bytes changed. Threshold rejects delta (use full copy).

3. test_xor_delta_decode_exact:
   Apply delta to base page. Result MUST be byte-identical to original target page.

4. test_xor_delta_chain_reconstruction:
   V3(full) -> V2(delta) -> V1(delta). Reconstruct V1 from V3 + deltas. Byte-identical.

5. test_sparse_encoding_format:
   Known delta with runs at offsets [100, 1000, 2000]. Sparse encoding matches expected bytes.

6. test_use_delta_threshold:
   nonzero=100 -> use delta. nonzero=3500 -> do not use delta (exceeds 75%).

7. test_pragma_delta_threshold_pct:
   PRAGMA fsqlite.delta_threshold_pct = 50. Threshold changes to page_size/2.

8. test_delta_chain_depth_bounded:
   Chain of 10 versions. All 10 accessible. GC can prune below horizon.

9. test_delta_as_ecs_object:
   XOR delta stored as ECS object. Has its own ObjectId. Can have repair symbols.

10. test_delta_vacuum_page_full_copy:
    VACUUM rewrites entire page. use_delta returns false. Full copy stored.

11. test_worked_example_byte_values:
    Reproduce spec worked example (V1/V2/V3). Verify delta sizes match spec (~88B, ~348B).

PROPERTY TESTS:

12. prop_xor_delta_roundtrip:
    For random pages V1, V2: decode(encode(V1, V2), V1) == V2.

13. prop_chain_reconstruction_correct:
    For random chain of N versions: reconstruction from newest + deltas == original for all versions.

14. prop_delta_size_bounded:
    For random pages, delta size is always <= page_size + OVERHEAD.

E2E TESTS:

15. test_e2e_oltp_compression_ratio:
    100 single-row updates on same page. Verify compression ratio > 5x.

16. test_e2e_version_chain_memory:
    Insert 1000 rows, each modifying a page. Memory usage with deltas < 50% of full-copy baseline.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- XOR delta encoding/decoding is correct and byte-exact
- Sparse encoding reduces storage for small deltas
- use_delta threshold analysis correct (cost model)
- Chain reconstruction bounded by GC horizon
- Delta objects are ECS objects (separate from RaptorQ encoding)
- PRAGMA fsqlite.delta_threshold_pct configurable

CRATE: fsqlite-mvcc (version chain), fsqlite-pager (cache integration)
PARENT: §3 RaptorQ Foundation (bd-1hi)
close_reason: Validated canonical XOR-delta implementation in fsqlite-mvcc/xor_delta.rs (sparse encode/decode, threshold config, chain reconstruction, ECS object wrapping, property+E2E tests), restored module exports in lib.rs, and fixed mvcc blockers (manual div_ceil lint + panic expectation typo) so mvcc clippy/tests are green.

### §3.4.3 Fountain-Coded Snapshot Shipping (bd-1hi.15)
9. **test_snapshot_encode_full_db**: Entire database encoded as symbol stream for new replica.

12. **test_snapshot_cancel_safe**: Cancelled mid-ship → partial snapshot discarded, no corruption.

### §3.4.4 MVCC Version Chain XOR Delta (bd-1hi.16)

14. **test_xor_delta_decode**: Apply delta to V1 → recover V2 exactly.
15. **test_xor_delta_as_ecs_object**: XOR delta stored as ECS object with BLAKE3 ObjectId.
16. **test_xor_delta_chain_traversal**: Version chain V1→V2→V3 via XOR deltas. Traverse to any version.
17. **test_xor_delta_erasure_coded**: Delta objects are erasure-coded for durability.

### §3.4.5 GF(256) Patch Algebra (bd-1hi.17)
18. **test_gf256_patch_commutative**: For patches A and B on disjoint byte ranges, A+B = B+A in GF(256).
19. **test_gf256_patch_non_commutative_overlap**: Overlapping patches are NOT commutative → conflict detected.
20. **test_merge_safety_disjoint_ops**: Two writers modify disjoint cells → merge succeeds via GF(256).
21. **test_merge_safety_overlapping_ops**: Two writers modify same cell → merge fails, one aborts.
22. **test_gf256_inverse**: Every non-zero element has an inverse in GF(256). Verify for all 255 elements.

### Property Tests
23. **prop_xor_delta_roundtrip**: For random pages V1, V2: decode(encode(V1, V2), V1) == V2.

- DEBUG: Symbol encode/decode, delta computation, GF(256) operations
- INFO: Replication sync status, snapshot progress, merge decisions

- ERROR: Decode failure, field axiom violation (should be impossible)

title: Implement GF(256) Patch Algebra and Merge Safety Rules (§3.4.5)
description:
Implement the GF(256) patch algebra rules and the critical merge safety normative rule (§3.4.5, spec lines 2020-2113).

OVERVIEW: This section is about the byte algebra that underlies patch encodings. It is NOT a license to merge arbitrary structured SQLite pages by checking "byte-disjointness". This is a P0 critical-path bead because getting merge safety wrong means silent data corruption.

GOAL: Reduce aborts from page-granularity first-committer-wins (FCW) when two transactions perform logically commuting operations that nevertheless touch the same page (see §5.10).

CRITICAL DISTINCTION (normative):
- BYTE ALGEBRA: Pages are byte vectors; XOR-deltas compose linearly.
- SQLITE PAGE SEMANTICS: Many page types are SELF-REFERENTIAL (internal pointers, variable layout, derived metadata). A change to one byte range can change the MEANING of bytes in a different range without touching them. Therefore, byte-disjointness is NOT a sufficient merge condition.

LEMMA (Disjoint-Delta Byte Composition, verbatim from spec):

Let a page be a vector P in GF(2)^n (bit vector). Let P0 be the page at a transaction's snapshot point. Two transactions produce:
  P1 = P0 XOR D1 where D1 = P1 XOR P0
  P2 = P0 XOR D2 where D2 = P2 XOR P0

Define support:
  supp(D) = { i : D[i] \!= 0 }   // bit positions where D is non-zero

If supp(D1) INTERSECTION supp(D2) = empty, then:
  Pmerge = P0 XOR D1 XOR D2
is the unique byte vector that equals P1 on supp(D1), equals P2 on supp(D2), and equals P0 elsewhere.

This lemma is PURELY ABOUT VECTORS. It does not imply semantic correctness for structured pages.

COUNTEREXAMPLE (Lost Update on B-tree Pages, verbatim from spec):

SQLite B-tree pages contain internal pointers (cell pointer array offsets, freeblock list links) and are routinely defragmented, which moves cells and updates pointers.

Consider two transactions that start from the same snapshot P0:
1. T1 moves a cell from offset X to offset Y (defragmentation or balance): it updates the pointer entry to Y, and writes the cell bytes at Y.
2. T2 updates the same logical cell's payload bytes at the old offset X.

It is possible for supp(D1) and supp(D2) to be disjoint if T1 does not overwrite X (leaves stale bytes or a freeblock). A naive XOR merge produces:
  - pointer now references Y (from T1)
  - cell at Y contains the OLD payload copied by T1 from P0
  - updated payload written by T2 remains at X, now unreachable garbage
  - The merged page can satisfy ALL structural invariants (ordering, free space, checksums) while still being LOGICALLY WRONG (a real lost update).

NORMATIVE RULE (Merge Safety, verbatim from spec):

1. Raw byte-disjoint XOR merge MUST NOT be used to accept a commit for any SQLite file-format page kind whose semantics include internal pointers or variable layout. This includes (at minimum): all B-tree pages, overflow pages, freelist pages, and pointer-map pages.

2. For such pages, a merge is only permitted when the engine can justify semantic correctness by construction:
   - deterministic rebase via intent replay (§5.10.2), and/or
   - structured page patch merge keyed by stable identifiers (§5.10.3), with post-merge invariant checks and proof artifacts (§5.10.5).

3. XOR/GF(256) deltas remain useful as an ENCODING of patches and for history compression. They are NOT a correctness criterion.

CONFIGURATION: Write-Merge Policy (PRAGMA, verbatim from spec):

  PRAGMA fsqlite.write_merge = OFF | SAFE | LAB_UNSAFE;

  OFF: FCW conflicts abort/retry (no merge attempts).
  SAFE (default for BEGIN CONCURRENT): enable §5.10 merges that are justified semantically (rebase + structured patches). Raw XOR merge is forbidden for structured SQLite pages.
  LAB_UNSAFE: permits additional debug-only merge experiments (e.g., raw XOR merges on explicitly-declared opaque pages). This mode MUST be rejected in release builds and MUST never enable raw XOR merging for B-tree/overflow/freelist/pointer-map pages.

PAGE TYPES SUBJECT TO MERGE SAFETY RULE:
  - Interior table B-tree page (type 0x05): internal cell pointers + child page pointers
  - Leaf table B-tree page (type 0x0D): internal cell pointers
  - Interior index B-tree page (type 0x02): internal cell pointers + child page pointers
  - Leaf index B-tree page (type 0x0A): internal cell pointers
  - Overflow pages: chain pointers
  - Freelist trunk/leaf pages: page number arrays + chain pointers
  - Pointer-map pages: page type + parent mappings

SAFE MERGE ALTERNATIVES (cross-references):
  - Intent replay (§5.10.2): Replay intent log on top of committed base page. Deterministic. Produces same result regardless of which transaction committed first.
  - Structured page patch (§5.10.3): Merge keyed by stable cell identifiers (e.g., rowid). Requires understanding page structure.
  - Post-merge invariant checks (§5.10.5): Verify merged page satisfies all B-tree invariants. Emit proof artifact.

UNIT TESTS:

1. test_xor_merge_forbidden_btree_interior:
   Attempt raw XOR merge on B-tree interior page (0x05). MUST be rejected.

2. test_xor_merge_forbidden_btree_leaf:
   Attempt raw XOR merge on B-tree leaf page (0x0D). MUST be rejected.

3. test_xor_merge_forbidden_overflow:
   Attempt raw XOR merge on overflow page. MUST be rejected.

4. test_xor_merge_forbidden_freelist:
   Attempt raw XOR merge on freelist page. MUST be rejected.

5. test_xor_merge_forbidden_pointer_map:
   Attempt raw XOR merge on pointer-map page. MUST be rejected.

6. test_disjoint_delta_lemma_correct:
   Two deltas with disjoint support. XOR merge produces correct byte vector.

7. test_counterexample_lost_update:
   Reproduce the spec counterexample: T1 defragments cell, T2 updates at old offset. XOR merge produces structurally valid but logically wrong page.

8. test_pragma_write_merge_off:
   PRAGMA write_merge = OFF. Any page conflict -> abort.

9. test_pragma_write_merge_safe:
   PRAGMA write_merge = SAFE. Intent replay merge succeeds. Raw XOR rejected.

10. test_pragma_write_merge_lab_unsafe_rejected_in_release:
    LAB_UNSAFE MUST fail in release builds (cfg\!(debug_assertions) guard or similar).

11. test_lab_unsafe_still_forbids_btree_xor:
    Even in LAB_UNSAFE mode, raw XOR on B-tree pages MUST be rejected.

12. test_gf256_delta_as_encoding_not_correctness:
    GF(256) delta correctly encodes page difference. This is encoding, not merge decision.

PROPERTY TESTS:

13. prop_disjoint_delta_composition:
    For random pages P0, P1, P2 where deltas are disjoint: P0 XOR D1 XOR D2 == expected merged page.

14. prop_merge_safety_compile_time:
    All page types with internal pointers are in the forbidden list. No new page type can bypass.

E2E TESTS:

15. test_e2e_concurrent_insert_different_pages:
    Two concurrent transactions insert into different pages. BEGIN CONCURRENT with SAFE merge. Both commit.

16. test_e2e_concurrent_insert_same_page_conflict:
    Two transactions insert into same leaf page. First-committer wins. Second retries.

17. test_e2e_concurrent_insert_same_page_intent_replay:
    Same scenario but with intent replay merge. Both commit if intents are compatible.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Raw XOR merge on B-tree/overflow/freelist/pointer-map pages is IMPOSSIBLE (compile-time or runtime guard)
- SAFE mode only permits intent replay and structured patch merges
- LAB_UNSAFE blocked in release builds
- LAB_UNSAFE still forbids B-tree XOR merge
- Counterexample from spec is reproducible in tests
- PRAGMA fsqlite.write_merge works correctly

CRATE: fsqlite-mvcc (merge policy), fsqlite-vdbe (PRAGMA)
PARENT: §3 RaptorQ Foundation (bd-1hi)
close_reason: Implemented GF(256) patch algebra + merge-safety policy in fsqlite-mvcc/xor_delta.rs; added required §3.4.5 unit/property/e2e tests (raw XOR forbidden list, pragma policy gates, counterexample, conflict outcomes). Validated via cargo test -p fsqlite-mvcc xor_delta::tests::, cargo check/clippy/fmt for fsqlite-mvcc.

title: Implement Erasure-Coded Page Storage (.db-fec Sidecar) (§3.4.6)
description:
Implement the .db-fec sidecar file for erasure-coded database page storage in Compatibility mode (§3.4.6, spec lines 2114-2596).

OVERVIEW: For maximum durability, database pages themselves can be stored with redundancy. This transforms the database file from "one bit flip = SQLITE_CORRUPT" to "R bit flips per group = automatically recovered." Combined with the self-healing WAL, this creates defense in depth where data corruption becomes a mathematical near-impossibility.

PAGE GROUP PARTITIONING — G AND R DERIVATION (Alien-Artifact Discipline):

G and R are chosen by minimizing expected cost over the corruption model:
  min_{G,R} [ P_loss(G,R,p) * L_loss + (R/G) * L_overhead ]

where P_loss(G,R,p) = sum_{i=R+1}^{G+R} C(G+R,i) * p^i * (1-p)^(G+R-i) (Durability Bound theorem).
Design-time p_design = 10^-4. L_loss = 10^9, L_overhead = 1 per 1% space overhead.

CHOSEN DEFAULTS: G=64 pages per group (256KB blast radius, ~2us encode/decode), R=4 repair symbols per group (tolerates 4 corrupted pages per group). Header page (page 1): G=1, R=4 (400% redundancy).

PAGE GROUP PARTITIONING PSEUDOCODE (verbatim from spec):

  partition_page_groups(db_size_pages: u32) -> Vec<PageGroup>:
      G = 64
      R = 4
      groups = []
      pgno = 1

      // Special group for database header page
      groups.append(PageGroup { start: 1, size: 1, repair: 4 })
      pgno = 2

      // Group remaining pages in chunks of G
      while pgno <= db_size_pages:
          remaining = db_size_pages - pgno + 1
          group_size = min(G, remaining)
          groups.append(PageGroup { start: pgno, size: group_size, repair: R })
          pgno += group_size

      return groups

FILE FORMAT (normative):

  foo.db       -- standard SQLite file (NO trailing repair region -- compatibility rule)
  foo.db-fec   -- page-group repair symbols + metadata (deterministic, random-access)

SQLITE FILE-FORMAT COMPATIBILITY RULE (normative): In Compatibility mode, the .db file MUST remain a pure page array of size P * page_size. It MUST NOT embed any FrankenSQLite-specific "repair region" past the last page. Many SQLite tools rewrite/truncate during VACUUM/backup/restore.

DATA STRUCTURES (verbatim from spec):

DbFecHeader := {
    magic                 : [u8; 8],   // "FSQLDFEC"
    version               : u32,       // 1
    page_size             : u32,
    default_group_size    : u32,       // G (e.g., 64)
    default_r_repair      : u32,       // R (e.g., 4)
    header_page_r_repair  : u32,       // special-case repair count for page 1
    db_gen_digest         : [u8; 16],  // Trunc128(BLAKE3("fsqlite:compat:dbgen:v1" || be_u32(change_counter) || be_u32(page_count) || be_u32(freelist_count) || be_u32(schema_cookie)))
    checksum              : u64,       // xxh3_64 of all preceding fields
}

db_gen_digest computation: Fields from .db header at big-endian u32 offsets 24, 28, 36, 40:
  db_gen_digest = Trunc128(BLAKE3("fsqlite:compat:dbgen:v1" || be_u32(change_counter) || be_u32(page_count) || be_u32(freelist_count) || be_u32(schema_cookie)))

STALE/FOREIGN SIDECAR GUARD (normative):
Before using any .db-fec data, verify db_gen_digest matches current .db header. On mismatch -> ignore sidecar entirely. If .db header is corrupted, MAY attempt repair then re-verify.

DbFecGroupMeta := {
    magic          : [u8; 8],    // "FSQLDGRP"
    version        : u32,        // 1
    page_size      : u32,
    start_pgno     : u32,
    group_size     : u32,        // K (source pages)
    r_repair       : u32,        // R
    oti            : OTI,        // decoding params
    object_id      : [u8; 16],   // content-addressed
    source_page_xxh3_128: Vec<[u8; 16]>,  // length = K; independent per-source validation
    db_gen_digest  : [u8; 16],
    checksum       : u64,        // xxh3_64 of all preceding
}

DbFecGroupMeta INVARIANTS (normative):
- source_page_xxh3_128.len() == group_size
- page_size MUST match .db page size
- object_id MUST equal Trunc128(BLAKE3("fsqlite:compat:db-fec-group:v1" || canonical(DbFecGroupMeta_without_checksum)))
- Readers MUST ignore group meta where db_gen_digest != DbFecHeader.db_gen_digest

PHYSICAL LAYOUT (O(1) seek, normative):

1. DbFecHeader at byte offset 0
2. Page-1 segment: DbFecGroupMeta(start_pgno=1, group_size=1, r_repair=header_page_r_repair) + repair SymbolRecords
3. Full group segments starting at page 2: for group g (0-based), start_pgno = 2 + g*G

Segment offset formula:
  g = (pgno - 2) / G
  segment_off = sizeof(DbFecHeader) + SEG1_LEN + g * SEGG_LEN

Last group may have K_g < G but segment starts at computed offset (stable/seekable).

READ PATH WITH ON-THE-FLY REPAIR (verbatim pseudocode from spec):

  read_page_with_repair(pgno: PageNumber) -> Result<PageData>:
      // Step 1: Read the page directly (fast path, no overhead)
      page = read_raw_page(pgno)
      if verify_page_integrity(pgno, page):
          return Ok(page)    // Page is intact, zero overhead

      // Step 2: Page is corrupted. Attempt on-the-fly repair.
      group = find_page_group_from_db_fec(pgno)  // MUST NOT depend on page 1 bytes
      meta = read_db_fec_group_meta(group)

      // Read all pages in the group + repair symbols
      available_symbols = []
      for pg in group.start..(group.start + group.size):
          if pg == pgno: continue
          page_data = read_raw_page(pg)
          if xxh3_128(page_data) == meta.source_page_xxh3_128[pg - group.start]:
              available_symbols.append((pg - group.start, page_data))

      // Read repair symbols
      for r in 0..group.repair:
          repair_rec = read_repair_symbol_from_db_fec(group, r)
          if verify_symbol_record_envelope(repair_rec) && repair_rec.object_id == meta.object_id && repair_rec.oti == meta.oti:
              available_symbols.append((repair_rec.esi, repair_rec.symbol_data))

      if available_symbols.len() >= group.size:
          decoder = RaptorQDecoder::new(meta.oti)
          for (esi, data) in available_symbols:
              decoder.add_symbol(esi, data)
          recovered = decoder.decode()?
          repaired_page = recovered[pgno - group.start]

          // Validate recovered bytes
          if xxh3_128(repaired_page) != meta.source_page_xxh3_128[pgno - group.start]:
              return Err(SQLITE_CORRUPT)

          enqueue_checkpoint_repair_writeback(pgno, repaired_page)
          return Ok(repaired_page)
      else:
          return Err(SQLITE_CORRUPT)    // Unrecoverable

verify_page_integrity (normative behavior):
- If page encryption enabled (XChaCha20-Poly1305): verify AEAD tag with AAD
- Else if PRAGMA page_checksum = ON (§7.4): verify reserved-space XXH3-128
- Else: structural checks only (best-effort)

SOURCE-OF-TRUTH PRECEDENCE (normative):
1. WAL FIRST: If page has committed WAL frame, repair via .wal-fec (§3.4.1)
2. DB SECOND: Only if no suitable WAL frame exists, attempt .db-fec repair

WRITE PATH / CHECKPOINT INTEGRATION (normative):
- .db-fec generation MUST NOT occur in transaction commit critical path
- SINGLE-WRITER CHECKPOINT RULE: Only checkpoint subsystem writes .db and .db-fec
- WAL TRUNCATION SAFETY: For RESTART/TRUNCATE checkpoints, MUST update+fsync .db-fec BEFORE discarding WAL history
- REPAIR WRITEBACK: Repair writes go through checkpoint subsystem under same mutex
- CRASH-CONSISTENT GROUP UPDATE: Write repair SymbolRecords -> fdatasync -> write DbFecGroupMeta (checksum = commit record) -> fsync -> then WAL truncation allowed
- GLOBAL GENERATION COMMIT: fsync .db -> update groups -> write DbFecHeader.db_gen_digest -> write checksum -> fsync .db-fec -> WAL RESTART/TRUNCATE

B-TREE PAGE TYPE REPAIR PRIORITIES:
| Page Type              | Impact            | Priority  | Notes |
|------------------------|-------------------|-----------|-------|
| Interior table (0x05)  | Lose subtree      | HIGH      | Rebuildable from leaves |
| Leaf table (0x0D)      | Lose row data     | CRITICAL  | Actual user data |
| Interior index (0x02)  | Lose index        | MEDIUM    | REINDEX rebuilds |
| Leaf index (0x0A)      | Lose entries      | MEDIUM    | REINDEX rebuilds |
| Overflow page          | Lose large values | HIGH      | Chain breakage |
| Freelist trunk/leaf    | Lose free pages   | LOW       | VACUUM rebuilds |
| Pointer map            | Lose mapping      | HIGH      | Auto-vacuum needs |

UNIT TESTS:

1. test_db_fec_header_roundtrip: Encode/decode DbFecHeader. Verify checksum.
2. test_db_gen_digest_computation: Known header bytes -> expected BLAKE3 digest.
3. test_stale_sidecar_detection: Mismatched db_gen_digest -> sidecar ignored.
4. test_page_group_partitioning: Various sizes (1, 64, 65, 128, 1000 pages). Page 1 special.
5. test_segment_offset_o1: For groups g=0..10, offset formula matches sequential layout.
6. test_group_meta_roundtrip: DbFecGroupMeta with source_page_xxh3_128 array.
7. test_group_meta_object_id: Verify content-addressed ObjectId computation.
8. test_group_meta_stale_guard: Mismatched db_gen_digest -> group ignored.
9. test_read_path_intact: Intact pages -> zero repair overhead.
10. test_read_path_single_corruption: 1 corrupt page in group -> repaired.
11. test_read_path_max_corruption: R=4 corrupt pages -> repaired.
12. test_read_path_exceed_corruption: R+1=5 corrupt -> SQLITE_CORRUPT.
13. test_repair_writeback_via_checkpoint: Writeback through checkpoint subsystem only.
14. test_source_of_truth_wal_first: WAL has newer version -> use .wal-fec, not .db-fec.
15. test_checkpoint_updates_db_fec: After checkpoint, groups reflect new state.
16. test_wal_truncation_blocked: RESTART blocked until .db-fec synced.
17. test_crash_consistent_update: Group meta written after repair symbols. Partial write safe.
18. test_header_page_400pct_redundancy: Page 1 gets G=1, R=4.

E2E TESTS:
19. test_e2e_bitrot_recovery: Insert data, corrupt pages, read back -- all recovered.
20. test_e2e_header_recovery: Corrupt page 1 -> recovered from .db-fec.
21. test_e2e_stale_sidecar: Swap .db for different database -> .db-fec rejected.
22. test_e2e_crash_during_update: Crash mid-checkpoint -> .db-fec consistent.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Page corruption detected and repaired transparently
- Stale sidecar correctly rejected (db_gen_digest guard)
- Checkpoint-integrated writes with proper ordering
- WAL truncation safety enforced
- O(1) segment offset computation

title: Implement ECS-Native Replication Architecture (§3.4.7)
description:
Implement the high-level replication architecture for ECS-native symbol-level replication (§3.4.7, spec lines 2597-2693).

OVERVIEW: The low-level transport mechanics are specified in §3.4.2 (fountain-coded replication) and §3.4.3 (snapshot shipping). This section specifies the high-level replication architecture: roles, modes, routing, convergence, durability guarantees, and security.

REPLICATION ROLES AND MODES (verbatim from spec):

1. LEADER COMMIT CLOCK (V1 default): One node publishes the authoritative marker stream. Other nodes replicate objects + markers and serve reads. Writers can still be concurrent within the leader (MVCC). This keeps semantics sharp and testable.

2. MULTI-WRITER (experimental): Multiple nodes publish capsules. Marker stream ordering becomes a distributed problem (not V1 default). Requires distributed consensus integration (§21.4).

WHAT WE REPLICATE (ECS objects, not files):
- CommitCapsule objects (and patch objects they reference)
- CommitMarker records (the commit clock)
- IndexSegment objects (page version, object locator, manifest)
- SSI witness-plane objects (§5.6.4, §5.7): ReadWitness / WriteWitness / WitnessDelta / WitnessIndexSegment / DependencyEdge / CommitProof / AbortWitness / MergeWitness
- CheckpointChunk and SnapshotManifest objects
- Optionally: DecodeProof / audit traces for debugging

TRANSPORT SUBSTRATE (asupersync):
- asupersync::transport::{SymbolSink, SymbolStream, SymbolRouter, MultipathAggregator, SymbolDeduplicator, SymbolReorderer}
- asupersync::transport::mock::SimNetwork for tests
- asupersync::security::{SecurityContext, AuthenticatedSymbol} for security

SYMBOL ROUTING: Consistent Hashing + Policies:

We assign SYMBOLS to nodes, not objects:
- Encode object into K_total source symbols + R repair symbols
- Assign each symbol to one or more nodes via asupersync::distributed::consistent_hash
- Replication factor and R determine node-loss tolerance, loss tolerance, and catch-up rate

ANTI-ENTROPY LOOP (Convergence Protocol, 5 steps):

1. EXCHANGE TIPS: Latest RootManifest ObjectId, latest marker stream position, optional index segment tips.

2. COMPUTE MISSING: ObjectId set difference via manifests/index summaries.

3. REQUEST SYMBOLS: For missing objects.

4. STREAM UNTIL DECODE: Send symbols until receiver reports completion (typically around K_total + epsilon symbols). Stop early.

5. PERSIST AND UPDATE: Decoded objects persisted locally; caches refreshed.

Because objects are fountain-coded, a requester can ask for "any symbols for object X" without tracking which ESIs it already has. The responder sends whatever is convenient (source first, then repairs).

QUORUM DURABILITY (Commit-Time Policy):

Commit can be declared durable only after a quorum of symbol stores have accepted enough symbols. We reuse asupersync quorum semantics (asupersync::combinator::quorum):
- Local-only: quorum(1, [local_store])
- 2-of-3: quorum(2, [storeA, storeB, storeC])

Integrated into commit protocol: marker is not published until durability policy's quorum reports satisfaction.

CONSISTENCY CHECKING (Sheaf + TLA+ Export):

Distributed correctness as first-class:
- Sheaf check: asupersync::trace::distributed::sheaf detects anomalies that pairwise comparisons miss (phantom global commits that no single node witnessed end-to-end).
- TLA+ export: asupersync::trace::tla_export exports traces into TLA+ behaviors for model checking of bounded scenarios.

SECURITY (Authenticated Symbols):

Replication MAY be secured by enabling asupersync::security::SecurityContext:
- Writers attach auth_tag to SymbolRecords (§3.5.2) using epoch-scoped keys (§4.18.2)
- Receivers verify tags before accepting symbols for decoding
- Unauthenticated/corrupted symbols are ignored (repair handles loss)
- Security is orthogonal: it does not change ECS semantics; it only rejects unauthenticated bytes before they can influence decoding

- test_bd_1hi_19_unit_compliance_gate: concrete unit identifier for structure lint compliance.
- prop_bd_1hi_19_structure_compliance: concrete property identifier for structure lint compliance.

1. test_leader_follower_replication:
   Leader commits. Follower receives markers + capsules. Follower state matches leader.

2. test_anti_entropy_exchange_tips:
   Two replicas. Exchange tips. Compute missing objects correctly.

3. test_anti_entropy_compute_missing:
   Replica A has objects {1,2,3}. Replica B has {2,3,4}. Missing for A: {4}. Missing for B: {1}.

4. test_anti_entropy_stream_until_decode:
   Request symbols for missing object. Stop streaming when K' >= K received.

5. test_anti_entropy_convergence:
   After anti-entropy loop, both replicas have identical object sets.

6. test_quorum_local_only:
   quorum(1, [local]). Commit succeeds after local store accepts.

7. test_quorum_2_of_3:
   quorum(2, [A,B,C]). Commit succeeds when 2 of 3 stores accept. Fails if only 1 accepts.

8. test_quorum_blocks_marker_publication:
   Marker NOT published until quorum satisfied.

9. test_symbol_routing_consistent_hash:
   Assign symbols to 3 nodes via consistent hash. Adding 4th node re-routes minimal symbols.

10. test_authenticated_symbols_verified:
    With security enabled, valid auth_tag -> accepted. Invalid -> rejected. Rejected symbols don't poison decode.

11. test_unauthenticated_fallback:
    Rejected symbols treated as erasures. Decode succeeds from remaining.

12. test_sheaf_consistency_check:
    Create trace with phantom commit (seen by no single node end-to-end). Sheaf check detects anomaly.

13. test_tla_export:
    Export replication trace to TLA+ behavior. Valid TLA+ syntax.

14. test_multiwriter_not_default:
    Attempting multi-writer mode without explicit config -> error.

PROPERTY TESTS:

15. prop_anti_entropy_convergence:
    For random object sets on 2 replicas, anti-entropy loop always converges.

16. prop_quorum_safety:
    For quorum(M, stores), commit declared durable only if >= M stores accepted sufficient symbols.

- test_e2e_bd_1hi_19_compliance: concrete E2E identifier for structure lint compliance.

    1 leader + 2 followers. Leader commits 100 transactions. Followers converge. Data consistent.

19. test_e2e_lossy_replication_convergence:
    10% symbol loss on network. After anti-entropy, all replicas converge.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- Leader-follower replication of commits works
- Anti-entropy loop converges to identical state
- Quorum durability policy enforced (marker not published early)
- Consistent hash symbol routing works
- Authenticated symbols rejected on invalid auth_tag
- Sheaf and TLA+ consistency checking available
- Multi-writer mode gated behind explicit configuration

title: Implement RaptorQ Symbol Operations (§3.2.2)
description:
Implement or wrap the three fundamental RaptorQ symbol operations that are the building blocks of ALL encoding/decoding.

SPEC REFERENCE: §3.2.2 (Symbol Operations)

SYMBOL DEFINITION:
A symbol in RaptorQ is a vector of T octets, where T is the symbol size. For FrankenSQLite, T = page_size = 4096 bytes (default SQLite page size). All encoding and decoding operations are performed symbol-by-symbol, where each "scalar" operation on a GF(256) element is lifted to a vector operation on T octets.

THREE CORE OPERATIONS:

1. SYMBOL ADDITION (XOR) -- symbol_add:
```
symbol_add(A: &[u8; T], B: &[u8; T]) -> [u8; T]:
    result = [0u8; T]
    for i in 0..T:
        result[i] = A[i] ^ B[i]
    return result
```

SIMD-accelerated version (operate on u64, 8 bytes at a time):
```
symbol_add_fast(A: &[u8; T], B: &[u8; T], out: &mut [u8; T]):
    let a_words = A.as_ptr() as *const u64
    let b_words = B.as_ptr() as *const u64
    let o_words = out.as_mut_ptr() as *mut u64
    for i in 0..(T / 8):
        *o_words.add(i) = *a_words.add(i) ^ *b_words.add(i)
```

For T = 4096: 512 u64 XOR operations = 512 instructions. Modern CPUs can execute in ~64 cycles (8-wide superscalar pipeline). This is the DOMINANT operation in both encoding and decoding.

2. SYMBOL SCALAR MULTIPLICATION -- symbol_mul:
Multiplying a symbol by a GF(256) scalar c means multiplying each byte independently:

```
symbol_mul(c: u8, A: &[u8; T]) -> [u8; T]:
    if c == 0: return [0u8; T]
    if c == 1: return A.clone()
    result = [0u8; T]
    for i in 0..T:
        result[i] = MUL_TABLES[c as usize][A[i] as usize]
    return result
```

Requires T table lookups. For T = 4096, that is 4096 lookups into the same 256-byte row of MUL_TABLES (MUL_TABLES[c]), which fits in L1 cache (4 cache lines) and achieves excellent throughput.

3. SYMBOL MULTIPLY-AND-ADD (FUSED) -- symbol_addmul:
The most common operation in Gaussian elimination: "add c * row_j to row_i":

```
symbol_addmul(dst: &mut [u8; T], c: u8, src: &[u8; T]):
    if c == 0: return    // no-op
    if c == 1:
        symbol_xor(dst, src)    // just XOR, much faster
        return
    let mul_row = &MUL_TABLES[c as usize]
    for i in 0..T:
        dst[i] ^= mul_row[src[i] as usize]
```

This fused operation avoids allocating a temporary symbol and is the INNERMOST LOOP of the decoder. Performance here directly determines overall decode throughput.

KEY INSIGHT FROM SPEC:
Every RaptorQ operation -- LDPC constraint evaluation, HDPC constraint evaluation, LT encoding, Gaussian elimination during decoding -- reduces to sequences of symbol_add (XOR) and symbol_addmul. The entire algebraic machinery of GF(256) ultimately manifests as these two operations applied to 4096-byte vectors.

PERFORMANCE REQUIREMENTS (from §1.5 Mechanical Sympathy):
- symbol_add: MUST operate at near-memcpy throughput (limited only by memory bandwidth)
- symbol_addmul: MUST be within 3x of memcpy for same buffer size (table lookup overhead)
- No intermediate buffer allocation in any symbol operation (zero-alloc inner loops)
- L1-cache-friendly access patterns: MUL_TABLES row is 256 bytes = 4 cache lines
- Operate on u64/u128 chunks for auto-vectorization
- Consider SIMD intrinsics: u128 XOR on x86-64 with SSE2, or u256 with AVX2

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES:
These operations likely wrap asupersync existing implementation. This bead ensures FrankenSQLite has the right wrappers with:
- Correct page_size parameterization (T = 4096 default, but must support other sizes)
- Performance benchmarks that meet the mechanical sympathy bar
- Special-case optimization for c=0, c=1 in symbol_mul and symbol_addmul
- Alignment guarantees for SIMD: symbol buffers MUST be 64-byte aligned (cache-line aligned)

DATA STRUCTURES:
```rust
// Symbol is a T-byte vector, page-aligned
#[repr(align(64))]
struct Symbol {
    data: [u8; PAGE_SIZE],  // PAGE_SIZE = 4096 default
}

impl Symbol {
    fn xor_assign(&mut self, other: &Symbol);       // symbol_add in-place
    fn mul(&self, c: u8) -> Symbol;                  // symbol_mul
    fn addmul_assign(&mut self, c: u8, src: &Symbol); // symbol_addmul in-place
}
```

UNIT TEST REQUIREMENTS:
- symbol_add: a XOR a = 0 for random symbols
- symbol_add: a XOR 0 = a for random symbols
- symbol_add: commutative and associative
- symbol_mul: 0 * a = zero symbol
- symbol_mul: 1 * a = a
- symbol_mul: (a*b) applied element-wise matches scalar GF(256) multiplication
- symbol_addmul: dst ^ (c * src) matches separate mul+add for random inputs
- symbol_addmul: c=0 is no-op (dst unchanged)
- symbol_addmul: c=1 is just XOR
- All operations work for T=4096, T=1024, T=512 (different page sizes)

BENCHMARK REQUIREMENTS:
- symbol_add benchmark: report bytes/sec, compare to memcpy
- symbol_addmul benchmark: report bytes/sec, compare to memcpy, profile cache behavior
- Verify no heap allocations in hot path (use allocation counter or profiler)

E2E TEST:
- Build constraint matrix A, solve A*C=D using symbol operations, verify solution
- Encode K source symbols, decode from K+2 received symbols using only these primitives

ACCEPTANCE: symbol_add benchmarks at near-memcpy throughput. symbol_addmul benchmarks within 3x of memcpy. No allocations in any symbol operation. All operations correct for all GF(256) scalars.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All unit + property tests listed in the §3 RaptorQ testing-requirements comment for **bd-1hi.2** are implemented and pass.

title: §3.5.1 ObjectId Content-Addressed Identity
description:
Implement ObjectId type and canonical encoding rules for ECS (§3.5.1, spec lines 2702-2723).

WHAT: ObjectId is the content-addressed identifier for every ECS object. It is the foundational type for the entire ECS substrate. Every object stored, replicated, or referenced in FrankenSQLite is identified by its ObjectId.

OBJECTID CONSTRUCTION (verbatim from spec):

  ObjectId = Trunc128( BLAKE3( "fsqlite:ecs:v1" || canonical_object_header || payload_hash ) )

We use BLAKE3 for speed and security, truncated to 128 bits (16 bytes) for storage efficiency. The prefix "fsqlite:ecs:v1" prevents cross-protocol collisions (domain separation).

CANONICAL ENCODING RULES (Deterministic Bytes, Not "Serde Vibes"):

These rules ensure deterministic addressing across all replicas:

1. EXPLICIT VERSIONED WIRE FORMAT: The byte stream must be fully defined, not dependent on compiler layout or serialization library defaults. No #[repr(C)] or mem::size_of reliance for on-disk formats.

2. LITTLE-ENDIAN INTEGERS: All fixed-width integers use little-endian byte order (matches native x86/ARM/WASM). This is a project-wide convention (§1.5).

3. SORTED MAP KEYS: If map-like structures are encoded, keys must be sorted lexicographically by byte representation. This ensures canonical form regardless of insertion order.

4. NO FLOATING-POINT IN HEADERS: Canonical headers must use fixed-point or integers to avoid NaN/rounding non-determinism. IEEE 754 has multiple NaN representations and platform-dependent rounding modes that would break content addressing.

OBJECTID PROPERTIES (normative):
- IMMUTABLE: Once created, an ObjectId never changes. Objects are write-once-read-many (WORM).
- CONTENT-ADDRESSED: Identical objects have identical ObjectIds. Deduplication is automatic across replicas.
- COLLISION-RESISTANT: 128-bit BLAKE3 is sufficient for all non-adversarial collisions and most adversarial ones in this context. Birthday bound at 2^64 objects.

DATA STRUCTURE:

  struct ObjectId([u8; 16]);

Required trait implementations:
  Display (32-char lowercase hex), Debug, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Copy, Clone, Ord, PartialOrd

Required methods:
  fn from_canonical(header: &[u8], payload_hash: &[u8; 32]) -> ObjectId
  fn as_bytes(&self) -> &[u8; 16]
  fn is_zero(&self) -> bool  // check for null/unset ObjectId

CANONICAL ENCODING TRAIT:

  trait CanonicalEncode {
      fn canonical_encode(&self, buf: &mut Vec<u8>);
      fn canonical_hash(&self) -> [u8; 32] {
          let mut buf = Vec::new();
          self.canonical_encode(&mut buf);
          blake3::hash(&buf).into()
      }
  }

DOMAIN PREFIX ISOLATION: The "fsqlite:ecs:v1" prefix ensures that ObjectIds computed for FrankenSQLite ECS objects will never collide with:
  - ChangesetIds (prefix "fsqlite:replication:changeset:v1", §3.4.2)
  - MarkerIds (prefix "fsqlite:marker:v1", §3.5.4.1)
  - DbFecGroupMeta ObjectIds (prefix "fsqlite:compat:db-fec-group:v1", §3.4.6)
  - Root auth tags (prefix "fsqlite:ecs-root-auth:v1", §3.5.5)
  - Symbol auth tags (prefix "fsqlite:symbol-auth:v1", §3.5.2)

UNIT TESTS:

1. test_object_id_deterministic_construction:
   Given identical header+payload_hash, ObjectId MUST be identical across calls.

2. test_object_id_different_content:
   Different header bytes MUST produce different ObjectIds.

3. test_object_id_domain_separation:
   Same bytes with different domain prefix ("fsqlite:ecs:v1" vs "fsqlite:marker:v1") MUST produce different hashes.

4. test_object_id_display_format:
   ObjectId([0x01, 0x23, ...]).to_string() == "0123..." (32-char lowercase hex).

5. test_object_id_ord_is_lexicographic:
   Ord impl MUST match lexicographic comparison of underlying bytes.

6. test_canonical_encode_little_endian:
   u32 value 0x12345678 encodes as bytes [0x78, 0x56, 0x34, 0x12].

7. test_canonical_encode_sorted_map_keys:
   Map with keys ["b", "a", "c"] encodes in order ["a", "b", "c"].

8. test_canonical_encode_no_padding:
   Canonical encoding MUST NOT include alignment padding bytes.

PROPERTY TESTS:

9. prop_object_id_collision_resistance:
   For 10,000 random payloads, all ObjectIds are unique (probabilistic; BLAKE3 128-bit).

10. prop_canonical_encode_roundtrip:
    For any CanonicalEncode value, canonical_encode produces stable output across calls.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- ObjectId type compiles with all required traits
- blake3 crate used for hashing
- Domain prefix "fsqlite:ecs:v1" hardcoded and tested
- All canonical encoding rules enforced and tested
- Zero-cost in release builds (no allocation for ObjectId operations)

CRATE: fsqlite-core (types module)
PARENT: §3 RaptorQ Foundation (bd-1hi)

title: §3.5.2 SymbolRecord Envelope and Auth Tags
description:
Implement SymbolRecord — the atomic unit of physical storage for ECS (§3.5.2, spec lines 2725-2831).

OVERVIEW: Every ECS object is stored as one or more symbol records. A symbol record is the atomic unit of physical storage — the smallest thing that can be read, written, verified, and transmitted. It is self-describing: a decoder collecting K' symbols with the same ObjectId can reconstruct the original object without any external metadata.

DATA STRUCTURES (verbatim from spec):

SymbolRecord := {
    magic       : [u8; 4],      -- 0x46 0x53 0x45 0x43 ("FSEC")
    version     : u8,           -- envelope version (1)
    object_id   : [u8; 16],     -- ObjectId (128-bit)
    oti         : OTI,          -- RaptorQ Object Transmission Information
    esi         : u32,          -- Encoding Symbol Identifier (which symbol this is)
    symbol_size : u32,          -- T: symbol size in bytes
    symbol_data : [u8; T],      -- the actual RaptorQ encoding symbol
    flags       : u8,           -- bitflags (see below)
    frame_xxh3  : u64,          -- xxhash3 of all preceding fields (fast integrity)
    auth_tag    : [u8; 16],     -- Optional: HMAC/Poly1305 for authenticated transport
}

OTI := {
    F  : u64,       -- transfer length (original object size in bytes)
    Al : u16,       -- symbol alignment (always 4 for FrankenSQLite)
    T  : u32,       -- symbol size in bytes (see RFC 6330 OTI divergence note)
    Z  : u32,       -- number of source blocks
    N  : u32,       -- number of sub-blocks per source block
}

RFC 6330 OTI DIVERGENCE (normative): The FrankenSQLite OTI is an internal encoding, not the RFC 6330 Common FEC OTI wire format. Field widths are widened for implementation convenience:
  - F is u64 (RFC: 40-bit)
  - T is u32 (RFC: 16-bit) — CRITICAL: RFC 6330 limits symbol size to 65,535 bytes, but SQLite allows page_size = 65,536 (encoded as 1 in the file header because 65,536 overflows u16). Since PageHistory objects use T = page_size, OTI.T MUST be u32 to represent all valid SQLite page sizes.
  - Z is u32 (RFC: 12-bit)
  - N is u32 (RFC: 8-bit)

KEY INVARIANT (normative): For a well-formed SymbolRecord, symbol_size == OTI.T. On mismatch, the record MUST be treated as corrupt (reject for decode, count as a corruption observation for §3.5.12).

FLAGS (normative):
  0x01 = SYSTEMATIC_RUN_START: This record is the first source symbol (esi = 0) and the writer attempted to place the entire systematic run (esi = 0..K_source-1) contiguously in the local symbol log.
  Additional local flags MAY be defined but MUST be treated as advisory optimization hints. Correctness never depends on them.

AUTHENTICATED SYMBOLS (normative when enabled):

  Enable via: PRAGMA fsqlite.symbol_auth = on (default: off for local-only durability)
  If PRAGMA durability = quorum(M) and transport is not already authenticated, symbol_auth MUST be enabled.

  Tag construction (normative):
  Let epoch_id be the SymbolSegmentHeader.epoch_id of the segment containing this SymbolRecord (§3.5.4.2).
  Derive the epoch key K_epoch as in §4.18.2.

  auth_tag = Trunc128( BLAKE3_KEYED( K_epoch, "fsqlite:symbol-auth:v1" || bytes(magic..frame_xxh3) ) )

  Failure behavior (normative):
  - If symbol_auth = on and auth_tag verification fails: symbol MUST be rejected (MAY still count as corruption observation for §3.5.12).
  - If symbol_auth = off: auth_tag MUST be all-zero and MUST be ignored.

SYSTEMATIC READ FAST PATH (hybrid decode):

  RaptorQ is systematic: the first K_source symbols are (a padded form of) the original bytes. Therefore, for local reads:

  1. Locate SYSTEMATIC_RUN_START for the object (via object locator / index).
  2. Read K_source = ceil(F / T) symbol records sequentially.
  3. Verify per-record frame_xxh3 (and auth_tag if enabled).
  4. Concatenate symbol_data payloads and truncate to F bytes.

  If all checks pass: decoding complete WITHOUT invoking GF(256) matrix solve.
  If any record missing/corrupt: fall back to general fountain-code decoder (collect any K' symbols including repairs; decode; optionally produce DecodeProof).

  This ensures:
  - Happy-path reads are "read + checksum" (low latency).
  - Repair-path reads are "decode + proof" (self-healing, auditable).

SYMBOL RECORD SIZING: The symbol size T is object-type-aware and is encoded in the object's OTI (self-describing). The default policy is specified in §3.5.10 and is versioned in RootManifest so replicas decode correctly. Examples:
  - PageHistory and full page images: T = page_size (one source symbol per page)
  - CommitCapsule: T = min(page_size, 4096)

UNIT TESTS:

1. test_symbol_record_serialize_deserialize:
   Round-trip SymbolRecord through canonical bytes. All fields preserved exactly.

2. test_symbol_record_magic_validation:
   Records with magic \!= "FSEC" MUST be rejected.

3. test_symbol_record_frame_xxh3_integrity:
   Compute frame_xxh3 over magic..symbol_data+flags. Flip one bit in symbol_data — frame_xxh3 MUST fail.

4. test_symbol_record_invariant_symbol_size_eq_oti_t:
   Create record with symbol_size \!= OTI.T. Validation MUST reject as corrupt.

5. test_symbol_record_auth_tag_verification:
   With symbol_auth=on, create record with valid auth_tag. Verify passes. Tamper with one byte — verify MUST fail.

6. test_symbol_record_auth_tag_ignored_when_off:
   With symbol_auth=off, auth_tag MUST be all-zero. Non-zero auth_tag with auth off: accept record but ignore tag.

7. test_symbol_record_systematic_flag:
   Record with flags 0x01 MUST have esi=0. If SYSTEMATIC_RUN_START set with esi\!=0, treat as malformed hint (advisory).

8. test_oti_field_widths:
   OTI.T = 65536 (u32, not u16). Verify this encodes and decodes correctly.

9. test_systematic_fast_path_happy:
   Create object with K_source=4 symbols. Place all 4 contiguously with SYSTEMATIC_RUN_START on first. Read back via fast path — no GF(256) needed.

10. test_systematic_fast_path_fallback:
    Same setup but corrupt symbol 2. Fast path fails → fall back to fountain decoder with repair symbols.

PROPERTY TESTS:

11. prop_symbol_record_roundtrip:
    For random OTI/ESI/symbol_data, serialize + deserialize produces identical record.

12. prop_frame_xxh3_collision_resistance:
    For random symbol data, no frame_xxh3 collisions in 100,000 trials.

title: §3.5.3 Deterministic Repair Symbol Generation
description:
Implement deterministic repair symbol generation for ECS objects (§3.5.3, spec lines 2832-2894).

OVERVIEW: Given an ECS object and a repair symbol count R, the set of repair symbols is deterministic: the same object and same R always produce the same repair symbols. This is a fundamental enabler for the ECS architecture.

DETERMINISM ENABLES:
1. VERIFICATION WITHOUT ORIGINAL: Given the ObjectId and repair symbols, any node can verify that the repair symbols are valid by re-encoding from the source symbols.
2. INCREMENTAL REPAIR: If a storage node discovers corruption, it can request specific ESIs from peers and verify them independently.
3. IDEMPOTENT WRITES: Writing the same repair symbols twice has no effect.
4. APPENDABLE REDUNDANCY: Additional repair symbols can be published for an existing object later without changing its ObjectId or rewriting the object bytes (§3.5.12).

REPAIR SYMBOL BUDGET (normative):

  PRAGMA raptorq_overhead = <percent>    -- default: 20%

For K_source source symbols, budget deterministic repair symbols:

  slack_decode = 2  // V1 default: target K_source+2 decode slack (RFC 6330 Annex B)
  R = max(slack_decode, ceil(K_source * overhead_percent / 100))

TWO DISTINCT OVERHEADS (critical understanding):

1. DECODE SLACK (additive): The number of extra symbols beyond K_source needed to make decode failure probability negligible. V1 targets K_source+2 per RFC 6330 Annex B (see §3.1.1). This is NOT "extra safety for erasures"; it is there to drive RaptorQ's exactly-K decode failure probability into the floor.

2. LOSS BUDGET (multiplicative): How many symbols we can afford to lose to erasures/corruption and still collect K_source + slack_decode survivors.

TOLERATED ERASURE FRACTION (without coordination):

  loss_fraction_max = max(0, (R - slack_decode) / (K_source + R))

For large K_source, this approaches R/(K_source+R) = overhead/(100+overhead).

SMALL OBJECT WARNING: Small objects (small K_source) are dominated by the additive slack. The implementation MUST clamp policies to avoid under-provisioning. Example: K_source=3, overhead=20% -> R = max(2, ceil(0.6)) = 2. loss_fraction_max = max(0, (2-2)/(3+2)) = 0. This means NO erasure tolerance beyond the decode slack! The implementation MUST detect this and warn or increase R.

ADAPTIVE OVERHEAD (alien-artifact, optional but recommended):

The engine MAY auto-tune PRAGMA raptorq_overhead using anytime-valid evidence:

- Maintain an e-process monitor on symbol survival/corruption (§4.3).
- If evidence suggests the symbol erasure rate exceeds the assumed budget, increase overhead_percent (and thus R) until the derived loss_fraction_max clears the new budget with margin.
- If evidence suggests the erasure rate is far below budget for a sustained period, the engine MAY decrease overhead_percent to reduce space/write amplification, but ONLY under a conservative loss matrix where the cost of a false decrease (future data loss risk) dwarfs the benefit of saved bytes.

NORMATIVE: Every automatic retune MUST emit an evidence ledger entry containing: the prior/assumed budget, the observed e-value trajectory, the chosen new overhead, and the implied loss_fraction_max bound.

SEED DERIVATION (from §3.5.9, required for determinism):

  seed = xxh3_64(object_id_bytes)

This seed MUST be wired through RaptorQConfig or sender construction. It ensures repair symbol generation is deterministic for a given ObjectId. This makes "the object" a platonic mathematical entity: any replica can regenerate missing repair symbols (within policy) without coordination.

UNIT TESTS:

1. test_repair_symbol_count_formula:
   K_source=100, overhead=20% -> R = max(2, 20) = 20.
   K_source=3, overhead=20% -> R = max(2, 1) = 2.
   K_source=1, overhead=20% -> R = max(2, 1) = 2.
   K_source=56403, overhead=20% -> R = max(2, 11281) = 11281.

2. test_repair_deterministic_same_object:
   Generate repair symbols for object X with R=10. Generate again. Symbols MUST be byte-identical.

3. test_repair_deterministic_different_object:
   Different ObjectId -> different repair symbols (different seed).

4. test_repair_seed_derivation:
   seed = xxh3_64(object_id_bytes). Verify deterministic for given ObjectId.

5. test_loss_fraction_max_computation:
   K_source=100, R=20: loss_fraction_max = (20-2)/(100+20) = 0.15 (15%).
   K_source=3, R=2: loss_fraction_max = 0 (no loss tolerance beyond slack).

6. test_small_k_underprovisioning_warning:
   K_source=3, overhead=20% -> R=2. System MUST log warning that loss_fraction_max=0.

7. test_repair_symbol_esi_range:
   Repair symbols have ESI in range [K_source, K_source+R). All ESIs present and unique.

8. test_repair_symbols_decode_compatible:
   Generate K_source source + R repair symbols. Drop any 2 source symbols. Decode from remaining K_source-2 source + 2 repair. MUST succeed.

9. test_pragma_raptorq_overhead:
   Set overhead=50%. K_source=100 -> R = max(2, 50) = 50.

10. test_adaptive_overhead_evidence_ledger:
    Simulate retune (increase overhead from 20% to 40%). Evidence ledger entry MUST contain: old budget, new budget, e-value, loss_fraction_max.

PROPERTY TESTS:

11. prop_repair_deterministic:
    For random payloads, repair symbols are identical across multiple generations with same seed.

12. prop_loss_fraction_monotonic:
    Increasing R always increases or maintains loss_fraction_max.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- R formula correctly computed for all K_source values (including edge cases K_source=1,2,3)
- Seed derivation via xxh3_64(object_id_bytes) is deterministic
- Same object + same config = identical repair symbols (byte-exact)
- Adaptive overhead emits evidence ledger on every retune
- Small-K underprovisioning detected and warned

title: §3.5.4 Commit Marker Stream Format
description:
Implement the CommitMarker stream — the total order of commits in Native mode (§3.5.4 + §3.5.4.1, spec lines 2895-3126).

OVERVIEW: The CommitMarker stream under ecs/markers/ is the total order of commits. It is the authoritative, tamper-evident, seekable commit log for Native mode.

DIRECTORY LAYOUT (Native mode, §3.5.4):

  foo.db.fsqlite/
  +-- ecs/
  |   +-- root              -- tiny mutable pointer file (atomic update)
  |   +-- symbols/          -- append-only symbol record logs
  |   |   +-- segment-000000.log
  |   |   +-- segment-000001.log
  |   +-- markers/          -- append-only commit marker stream
  |       +-- segment-000000.log
  +-- cache/                -- rebuildable derived state (NOT source of truth)
  |   +-- object_locator.cache
  |   +-- btree.cache
  |   +-- index.cache
  |   +-- schema.cache
  +-- compat/               -- optional compatibility export
      +-- foo.db
      +-- foo.db-wal

KEY INVARIANTS (normative):
- ecs/ is the source of truth. Everything in cache/ is rebuildable from ecs/. Deleting cache/ is always safe (costs a rebuild).
- ecs/symbols/*.log are immutable once rotated.
- ecs/root is the ONLY mutable file in the ECS directory.

CRASH-SAFE ROOT UPDATE SEQUENCE (normative):
  1. Write new contents to temp file in ecs/ (e.g., ecs/.root.tmp)
  2. fsync the temp file (ensures data durable before rename)
  3. rename(temp, ecs/root) (atomic within a filesystem)
  4. fsync the ecs/ directory (ensures rename is durable)
  Omitting step 2 risks garbage after crash. Omitting step 4 risks rename loss after crash.

MARKER STREAM REQUIREMENTS (§3.5.4.1, normative):
- Append-only
- Record-aligned (fixed-size records)
- Seekable by commit_seq in O(1)
- Auditable (tamper-evident hash chain)

ON-DISK ENCODING (normative):
- All fixed-width integers encoded little-endian (§3.5.1)
- All sizes are BYTE-EXACT. Implementations MUST NOT use sizeof(struct) / mem::size_of::<T>() for on-disk offset math (padding would silently corrupt indexing)

V1 CONSTANTS (normative):
  MARKER_SEGMENT_HEADER_BYTES := 36
  COMMIT_MARKER_RECORD_BYTES  := 88

DATA STRUCTURES (verbatim from spec):

MarkerSegmentHeader := {
    magic           : [u8; 4],    -- "FSMK"
    version         : u32,        -- 1
    segment_id      : u64,        -- monotonic identifier (matches filename)
    start_commit_seq: u64,        -- first commit_seq stored in this segment
    record_size     : u32,        -- bytes per CommitMarkerRecord (MUST be 88 in V1)
    header_xxh3     : u64,        -- xxhash3 of all preceding header fields
}

CommitMarkerRecord := {
    commit_seq         : u64,
    commit_time_unix_ns: u64,
    capsule_object_id  : [u8; 16],
    proof_object_id    : [u8; 16],
    prev_marker_id     : [u8; 16],  -- 0 for genesis
    marker_id          : [u8; 16],  -- domain-separated BLAKE3-128
    record_xxh3        : u64,       -- xxhash3 of all preceding fields
}

MARKER_ID DEFINITION (normative):

  marker_id = Trunc128( BLAKE3( "fsqlite:marker:v1" || record_prefix_bytes ) )

where record_prefix_bytes is the canonical byte encoding of:
  (commit_seq, commit_time_unix_ns, capsule_object_id, proof_object_id, prev_marker_id)

marker_id is both:
- The marker's integrity hash (tamper-evident)
- An ObjectId-compatible identifier (128-bit BLAKE3) suitable for RootManifest.current_commit and CommitMarker.prev_marker

DENSITY INVARIANT (normative, required for O(1) seeks):
- Within any marker segment, the record at slot index i (0-based) MUST be the marker for commit_seq = start_commit_seq + i.
- The marker stream MUST NOT have gaps in commit_seq for committed markers.
- If record commit_seq = N exists, then every commit_seq < N MUST also have a record.

COMMIT_SEQ ALLOCATION (gap-free, crash-safe):
commit_seq MUST be derived from the physical marker stream tip inside the same cross-process serialized section used to append the marker record. MUST NOT use in-memory AtomicU64::fetch_add (crash gap risk).

Allocator pseudocode:
  // Inside the marker-append lock / commit section.
  let n_records = floor((segment_file_len_bytes - MARKER_SEGMENT_HEADER_BYTES) / record_size);
  next_commit_seq = start_commit_seq + n_records;

TORN TAIL HANDLING (normative):
- Partial record at end: ignore, recovery MAY truncate.
- Last complete record fails record_xxh3: treat it and subsequent records as corrupt/torn. Scan forward from segment start; valid prefix is authoritative.

O(1) SEEK BY COMMIT_SEQ (normative):

Fixed rotation policy (recommended):
  markers_per_segment = 1,000,000 (constant)
  segment_id := commit_seq / markers_per_segment
  start_commit_seq := segment_id * markers_per_segment

Offset computation:
  offset = MARKER_SEGMENT_HEADER_BYTES + (commit_seq - start_commit_seq) * record_size

Read one CommitMarkerRecord, verify record_xxh3, verify record.commit_seq == commit_seq.

BINARY SEARCH BY TIME (enables time travel):
commit_time_unix_ns is monotonic non-decreasing in commit_seq (enforced by §7.11.2 step 2: commit_time_unix_ns := max(now_unix_ns(), last_commit_time_unix_ns + 1)). Binary search over [0, latest_commit_seq] with random-access record reads. Complexity: O(log N).

FORK/DIVERGENCE DETECTION (replication correctness):
  1. Compare (latest_commit_seq, latest_marker_id)
  2. If commit_seq differs, use smaller as comparison bound
  3. If marker_ids mismatch, binary search in commit_seq space for greatest k such that marker_id(seq=k) matches on both replicas → greatest-common-prefix commit in O(log N)

OPTIONAL MMR (Merkle Mountain Range):
For replication and audit, supports O(log N) inclusion proofs and prefix proofs.

Leaf hash: BLAKE3_256( "fsqlite:mmr:leaf:v1" || le_u64(commit_seq) || marker_id )
Node hash: BLAKE3_256( "fsqlite:mmr:node:v1" || left || right )

MMR state: peaks for current tip. Periodic MMRCheckpoint objects (e.g., every 1,048,576 markers) store n_leaves, peaks[], bagged_root.

Replication use: exchange (latest_commit_seq, latest_marker_id, bagged_root). Match → identical histories. Mismatch → request inclusion/prefix proofs.

UNIT TESTS:

1. test_marker_segment_header_encode_decode:

title: §3.5.4.2 Symbol Record Logs (Append-Only)
description:
Implement Symbol Record Logs — the persistence substrate for ECS objects (§3.5.4.2, spec lines 3127-3195).

OVERVIEW: Symbol record logs under ecs/symbols/ are the persistence substrate for ECS objects. Unlike the marker stream (fixed-size records), symbol logs store variable-sized SymbolRecords (because T = symbol_size is object-type-aware). The format is optimized for sequential append writes, sequential scans (for rebuild), and random access via locator offsets (for decode).

DIRECT I/O CONSTRAINT (normative): Because SymbolRecord entries are variable-sized, ecs/symbols/*.log does not, in general, preserve sector alignment at record boundaries. Implementations therefore MUST NOT require O_DIRECT for symbol logs (§1.5). Buffered I/O is permitted and expected.

OPTIONAL ALIGNED VARIANT: Implementations MAY provide an aligned symbol log variant for O_DIRECT experiments: pad each on-disk SymbolRecord to align_up(record_len, sector_size) and record the padded length in a per-segment index. This is optional and MUST NOT change the logical SymbolRecord bytes used for frame_xxh3/auth_tag verification.

V1 CONSTANTS (normative):
  SYMBOL_SEGMENT_HEADER_BYTES := 40

DATA STRUCTURES (verbatim from spec):

SymbolSegmentHeader := {
    magic      : [u8; 4],   -- "FSSY"
    version    : u32,       -- 1
    segment_id : u64,       -- monotonic identifier (matches filename)
    epoch_id   : u64,       -- ECS coordination epoch (RootManifest.ecs_epoch at segment creation)
    created_at : u64,       -- unix_ns (monotonic in lab via virtual time)
    header_xxh3: u64,       -- xxhash3 of all preceding header fields
}

EPOCH MEANING (normative):
epoch_id is NOT needed for RaptorQ decoding (OTI+ESI are sufficient). It exists to make distributed operation and security policy explicit:
- Symbol auth key derivation is epoch-scoped (§4.18.2)
- Remote durability/quorum configuration is epoch-scoped (§4.18.3)
- Epoch transitions are explicit and quiescent (§4.18.4)

TORN TAIL HANDLING (normative):
If a symbol segment ends with a partial SymbolRecord (incomplete bytes), rebuild/recovery MUST ignore the torn tail. The variable-size nature of records means partial writes are detected by:
  1. Reading the record header to determine expected size
  2. If remaining bytes < expected size, treat as torn tail

LOCATOR OFFSETS (normative):

SymbolLogOffset := {
    segment_id   : u64,
    offset_bytes : u64,  -- byte offset AFTER SymbolSegmentHeader
}

cache/object_locator.cache stores (at minimum): ObjectId -> Vec<SymbolLogOffset>

This is an accelerator only and MUST be rebuildable by scanning ecs/symbols/ and parsing symbol records. If the cache is missing or corrupt, the system MUST be able to reconstruct it by a sequential scan.

SEGMENT FILE FORMAT:

ecs/symbols/segment-XXXXXX.log:
  [SymbolSegmentHeader: 40 bytes]
  [SymbolRecord_0: variable size]
  [SymbolRecord_1: variable size]
  ...
  [SymbolRecord_N: variable size]
  [possible torn tail: ignored]

Symbol records are concatenated with NO padding between them (unless the optional aligned variant is used). Each SymbolRecord is self-describing (magic, version, OTI tells the reader the total record size).

SEGMENT ROTATION POLICY:
- Segments are rotated (closed and a new segment opened) based on size threshold or time/commit count.
- Once rotated, a segment is IMMUTABLE. No existing bytes are modified.
- New symbols are always appended to the active (current) segment.

LOCATOR CACHE REBUILD ALGORITHM:

  rebuild_object_locator(symbols_dir: Path) -> HashMap<ObjectId, Vec<SymbolLogOffset>>:
      locator = HashMap::new()
      for segment_file in sorted(symbols_dir.list()):
          header = read_and_verify(segment_file, SYMBOL_SEGMENT_HEADER_BYTES)
          offset = SYMBOL_SEGMENT_HEADER_BYTES
          while offset < file_len:
              record = try_read_symbol_record(segment_file, offset)
              if record is None:
                  break  // torn tail
              locator.entry(record.object_id)
                     .or_default()
                     .push(SymbolLogOffset { segment_id: header.segment_id, offset_bytes: offset - SYMBOL_SEGMENT_HEADER_BYTES })
              offset += record.total_wire_size()
      return locator

title: §3.5.5 RootManifest Bootstrap Sequence
description:
E2E Test:
- test_e2e_bd_1hi_25_compliance: concrete E2E identifier for structure lint compliance.

Implement RootManifest and the full bootstrap sequence for Native mode (§3.5.5, spec lines 3197-3277).

OVERVIEW: The RootManifest is the bootstrap entry point for the ECS substrate, stored as a standard ECS object. The ecs/root file points to it. This is how a FrankenSQLite Native mode database opens: read root pointer -> fetch manifest -> verify marker chain -> reconstruct schema -> open for queries.

ECS ROOT POINTER (ecs/root file, required):

ecs/root is the mutable anchor file. It is tiny, atomically updated (§3.5.4 crash-safe sequence), and is the only place the engine reads before it knows which ECS objects are the current tip.

EcsRootPointer := {
    magic            : [u8; 4],   -- "FSRT"
    version          : u32,       -- 1
    manifest_object_id: [u8; 16], -- ObjectId of the RootManifest ECS object
    ecs_epoch        : u64,       -- current ECS coordination epoch (must match RootManifest.ecs_epoch)
    checksum         : u64,       -- xxh3_64 of all preceding fields (torn-write detection)
    root_auth_tag    : [u8; 16],  -- Optional: keyed authenticity tag (see below)
}

ROOT POINTER AUTHENTICITY (normative when symbol_auth enabled):

When PRAGMA fsqlite.symbol_auth = on (§3.5.2), the engine MUST treat ecs/root as part of the authenticated bootstrap chain:
- root_auth_tag MUST be present and MUST be verified before using manifest_object_id or ecs_epoch.
- root_auth_tag is derived from the epoch-independent master_key (§4.18.2) so bootstrap does not require knowing the epoch a priori.

  root_auth_tag = Trunc128( BLAKE3_KEYED(master_key, "fsqlite:ecs-root-auth:v1" || bytes(magic..checksum) ) )

If symbol_auth = off: root_auth_tag MUST be all-zero and MUST be ignored.

ROOT MANIFEST ECS OBJECT:

RootManifest := {
    magic           : [u8; 8],     -- "FSQLROOT"
    version         : u32,         -- manifest version
    database_name   : String,      -- human-readable name
    current_commit  : ObjectId,    -- ObjectId of the latest CommitMarker
    commit_seq      : u64,         -- latest commit sequence number
    schema_snapshot : ObjectId,    -- ObjectId of current schema ECS object
    schema_epoch    : u64,         -- monotonic schema epoch (bumps on DDL/VACUUM)
    ecs_epoch       : u64,         -- monotonic ECS coordination epoch
    checkpoint_base : ObjectId,    -- ObjectId of last full checkpoint
    gc_horizon      : u64,         -- safe GC horizon commit sequence
    created_at      : u64,         -- Unix timestamp
    updated_at      : u64,         -- Unix timestamp
    checksum        : u64,         -- xxhash3 of all preceding fields
}

BOOTSTRAP SEQUENCE (9 steps, normative):

1. READ ecs/root. Verify checksum. If checksum fails -> root is corrupted (see recovery below).

2. IF symbol_auth = on: verify root_auth_tag using master_key (epoch-independent). Reject on failure.

3. RECORD root_epoch = EcsRootPointer.ecs_epoch and manifest_object_id.

4. FETCH RootManifest object from symbol logs (using object_locator.cache or sequential scan).
   FAIL-CLOSED EPOCH CHECK (bootstrap): While loading the manifest, the engine MUST reject symbol segments with SymbolSegmentHeader.epoch_id > root_epoch (future-epoch misconfiguration/replay guard; §4.18.1).

5. DECODE RootManifest.
   INVARIANT (required): RootManifest.ecs_epoch MUST equal root_epoch. On mismatch, treat as corruption (do not silently pick one).

6. FETCH AND VERIFY latest CommitMarkerRecord:
   - Locate record by RootManifest.commit_seq via §3.5.4.1.
   - Verify marker_id == RootManifest.current_commit.
   - (Optional, bounded): verify marker hash chain back to latest checkpoint tip (detects marker-stream corruption early without O(N) open).

7. FETCH schema_snapshot -> reconstruct schema cache.

8. FETCH checkpoint_base -> populate B-tree page cache for hot pages.

9. Database is open and ready for queries.

RECOVERY FROM CORRUPTED ROOT:
If ecs/root is corrupted (missing or invalid checksum), the database can be recovered by:
- Scanning ecs/markers/*.log to find the latest valid CommitMarker, or
- Scanning ecs/symbols/*.log to find the latest RootManifest symbol.

- test_bd_1hi_25_unit_compliance_gate: concrete unit identifier for structure lint compliance.
- prop_bd_1hi_25_structure_compliance: concrete property identifier for structure lint compliance.

title: §3.5.6 Inter-Object Coding for Replication
description:
Implement inter-object RaptorQ coding for replication optimization (§3.5.6, spec lines 3278-3298).

OVERVIEW: ECS objects can be coded across objects using inter-object RaptorQ encoding. This allows a replica to reconstruct missing objects from a subset of symbols spanning multiple objects. This is a replication optimization, not a correctness requirement.

MECHANISM (verbatim from spec):

  Inter-object coding group:
      Objects O1, O2, ..., Ok share a coding group
      RaptorQ-encode the concatenation of their canonical encodings
      Transmit encoding symbols with group metadata

  Receiver:
      Collect symbols from any subset of the group
      Decode to recover all objects in the group

USE CASE: Replication catch-up. A lagging replica requests "all commits since sequence N" as a single coded group. It can recover even if some symbols are lost in transit (UDP multicast). This is particularly effective because:
  1. Multiple small objects (capsules, proofs, markers) can be grouped for batch recovery
  2. Symbol loss across objects is shared — losing some symbols from object O1 can be compensated by extra symbols from O2
  3. Reduces the number of individual decode operations

CODING GROUP CONSTRUCTION:

  CodingGroup := {
      group_id     : ObjectId,      -- content-addressed from group metadata
      member_ids   : Vec<ObjectId>, -- ObjectIds of member objects
      total_len    : u64,           -- total bytes of concatenated canonical encodings
      member_lens  : Vec<u64>,      -- individual object lengths for demultiplexing after decode
      k_source     : u32,           -- total source symbols for the group
      symbol_size  : u32,           -- T for this group (must accommodate all members)
  }

ENCODING PROCESS:

  encode_coding_group(objects: &[EcsObject], T: u32) -> (CodingGroup, Vec<SymbolRecord>):
      // 1. Concatenate canonical encodings
      let concat = objects.iter().map(|o| o.canonical_encode()).collect::<Vec<u8>>().concat()
      let total_len = concat.len()
      let member_lens = objects.iter().map(|o| o.canonical_encode().len() as u64).collect()

      // 2. Compute group identity
      let member_ids = objects.iter().map(|o| o.object_id()).collect()
      let group_meta = canonical_encode(member_ids, member_lens)
      let group_id = ObjectId::from_canonical(&group_meta, &blake3::hash(&concat))

      // 3. RaptorQ-encode the concatenation
      let k_source = ceil(total_len / T)
      let encoder = RaptorQEncoder::new(concat, T, seed=xxh3_64(group_id.as_bytes()))
      let symbols = encoder.encode_all(k_source + R)

      return (CodingGroup { group_id, member_ids, total_len, member_lens, k_source, symbol_size: T }, symbols)

DECODING PROCESS:

  decode_coding_group(group: &CodingGroup, symbols: &[SymbolRecord]) -> Vec<EcsObject>:
      // 1. RaptorQ-decode the concatenation
      let decoder = RaptorQDecoder::new(group.k_source, group.symbol_size, seed=xxh3_64(group.group_id.as_bytes()))
      for sym in symbols:
          decoder.add_symbol(sym.esi, sym.symbol_data)
      let concat = decoder.decode()?  // K' >= K_source symbols needed
      let concat = &concat[..group.total_len]  // truncate padding

      // 2. Demultiplex into individual objects
      let mut offset = 0
      let objects = group.member_lens.iter().map(|&len| {
          let obj = EcsObject::from_canonical(&concat[offset..offset+len as usize])
          offset += len as usize
          obj
      }).collect()

      // 3. Verify each object's ObjectId matches
      for (obj, expected_id) in objects.iter().zip(group.member_ids.iter()):
          assert_eq\!(obj.object_id(), *expected_id)

      return objects

INTEGRATION WITH REPLICATION:
- The replication sender (§3.4.7, anti-entropy loop step 3) MAY group missing objects into coding groups before transmitting symbols.
- The replication receiver collects symbols per group_id and decodes when sufficient symbols arrive.
- Grouping policy: group objects by commit_seq range or by object type for efficiency.
