title: §3.5.7 RaptorQ Permeation Map Audit
description:
Implement and enforce the RaptorQ Permeation Map — every subsystem that persists/ships bytes MUST declare its ECS object type, symbol policy, and repair story (§3.5.7, spec lines 3299-3367).

OVERVIEW: This is the "no excuses" mapping from subsystem to ECS/RaptorQ role. If a subsystem persists or ships bytes, it MUST declare its ECS object type, symbol policy (K/R), and repair story. This is an audit checklist and enforcement mechanism.

DURABILITY PLANE (disk) — verbatim from spec:

| Subsystem     | ECS Object Type | Symbol Policy | Repair Story |
|---------------|-----------------|---------------|--------------|
| Commits       | CommitCapsule + CommitProof (coded) + CommitMarkerRecord (marker stream) | Capsule/Proof: T = min(page_size, 4096), R = 20% default; Marker: 88B fixed records | Capsule/Proof: decode from surviving symbols; Marker: torn-tail ignore + record_xxh3 + hash-chain audit |
| Checkpoints   | CheckpointChunk | T = 1024-4096B, R = policy-driven | Chunked snapshot objects; rebuild from marker stream if lost |
| Indices       | IndexSegment (Page, Object, Manifest) | T = 1280-4096B, R = 20% default | Decode or rebuild-from-marker-scan |
| Page storage  | PageHistory | T = page_size, R = per-group | Decode from group symbols; on-the-fly repair on read |

CONCURRENCY PLANE (memory) — verbatim from spec:

| Subsystem          | ECS Role | Notes |
|--------------------|----------|-------|
| MVCC page history  | PageHistory objects (patch chains) | Bounded by GC horizon; compressed via intent log + structured patches |
| Conflict reduction | Intent logs as small ECS objects | Replayed deterministically for rebase merge |
| SSI witness plane  | ReadWitness / WriteWitness / WitnessIndexSegment / DependencyEdge / CommitProof | The serialization graph is itself a fountain-coded stream (§5.6.4, §5.7) |

REPLICATION PLANE (network) — verbatim from spec:

| Subsystem        | Transport Primitive | Notes |
|------------------|-------------------|-------|
| Symbol streaming | SymbolSink/SymbolStream | Symbol-native, not file-native |
| Anti-entropy     | ObjectId set reconciliation (IBLT) | O(delta) reconciliation; fallback to segment hash scan |
| Bootstrap        | CheckpointChunk symbol streaming | Late-join = collect K symbols |
| Multipath        | MultipathAggregator | Any K symbols from any path suffice |

ANTI-ENTROPY VIA IBLT (recommended):

Naive set reconciliation ("send me your ObjectIds") is O(|A|) bandwidth. Use an Invertible Bloom Lookup Table (IBLT) to reconcile the symmetric difference in O(delta) where delta = |A symmetric_diff B|.

Protocol sketch:
1. Replica A builds IBLT over its ObjectId set in reconciliation scope
2. A sends IBLT to replica B
3. B subtracts its own ObjectIds from received IBLT and attempts to peel (decode)
4. On success: B obtains missing ObjectIds and requests needed symbols
5. If peeling fails (delta too large): B requests larger IBLT or falls back to segment-hash scan

Correctness-preserving: failure to peel is not silent; it degrades to slower fallback.

OBSERVABILITY PLANE (alien-artifact explainability):

| Subsystem             | Mechanism | Notes |
|-----------------------|-----------|-------|
| Repair auditing       | DecodeProof artifacts | Attached to lab traces when repair occurs |
| Schedule exploration  | LabRuntime deterministic trace | Reproducible concurrency bugs from a single seed |
| Invariant monitoring  | e-process monitors | MVCC invariants, memory bounds, replication divergence |
| Model checking        | TLA+ export of traces | Bounded model checking of commit/replication/recovery |

WILD BUT ALIGNED EXPERIMENTS (encouraged, feature-gated):
- Symbol-level RAID on single machine: Distribute symbols across multiple local devices/paths; any K reconstructs. RAID-like redundancy without strict striping constraints.
- Integrity sweeps as information theory: Periodically sample symbols and attempt partial decodes; use e-process monitors to detect elevated corruption rates early.

ENFORCEMENT RULE (normative): If a new feature persists bytes or ships bytes, it MUST declare its ECS object type, symbol policy, and repair story BEFORE implementation begins. This rule applies to all development, not just V1.

AUDIT CHECKLIST IMPLEMENTATION:

  struct PermeationEntry {
      subsystem: &'static str,
      object_type: &'static str,
      symbol_size_policy: &'static str,  // formula or range
      repair_story: &'static str,
      plane: Plane,  // Durability | Concurrency | Replication | Observability
  }

  enum Plane { Durability, Concurrency, Replication, Observability }

  static PERMEATION_MAP: &[PermeationEntry] = &[
      PermeationEntry { subsystem: "Commits", object_type: "CommitCapsule", symbol_size_policy: "T=min(page_size,4096), R=20%", repair_story: "decode from surviving symbols", plane: Durability },
      // ... all entries from tables above
  ];

  fn audit_permeation_map() -> Vec<AuditFailure> {
      // Verify every registered subsystem has a valid entry
      // Verify no subsystem is missing from the map
      // Return any gaps or inconsistencies
  }

title: §3.5.8-3.5.10 Decode Proofs + Deterministic Encoding + Symbol Size Policy
description:
Implement DecodeProofs, deterministic encoding seed derivation, and symbol size policy (§3.5.8-3.5.10, spec lines 3368-3422).

NOTE: This bead covers THREE distinct spec subsections (§3.5.8, §3.5.9, §3.5.10). Each is relatively small and closely related, so they are tracked together. If any subsection grows in scope during implementation, consider splitting into separate beads.

=== §3.5.8 DECODE PROOFS (Auditable Repair) ===

Asupersync includes a DecodeProof facility (asupersync::raptorq::proof). We exploit this in two critical ways:

1. IN LAB RUNTIME: Every decode that repairs corruption MUST produce a proof artifact attached to the test trace. This makes repair operations auditable and reproducible.

2. IN REPLICATION: A replica MAY demand proof artifacts for suspicious objects (e.g., repeated decode failures), enabling explainable "why did we reject this commit?" answers.

DecodeProof records:
- The set of symbol ESIs received
- Which symbols were repair vs source
- The intermediate decoder state at success/failure
- Timing metadata under LabRuntime (deterministic virtual time)

This is the "alien artifact" stance on repair: we do not merely fix things; we produce a mathematical witness that the fix is correct.

DecodeProof STRUCT:

  DecodeProof := {
      object_id       : ObjectId,
      k_source        : u32,
      symbols_received: Vec<u32>,    // ESIs of all symbols fed to decoder
      source_esis     : Vec<u32>,    // subset that were source symbols
      repair_esis     : Vec<u32>,    // subset that were repair symbols
      decode_success  : bool,
      intermediate_rank: Option<u32>, // decoder matrix rank at success/failure
      timing_ns       : u64,         // wall-clock or virtual time (LabRuntime)
      seed            : u64,         // RaptorQ seed used
  }

=== §3.5.9 DETERMINISTIC ENCODING (Seed Derivation from ObjectId) ===

If ObjectId is content-derived, symbol generation MUST be deterministic:
- The set of source symbols is deterministic by definition (payload chunking).
- Repair symbol generation MUST be deterministic for a given ObjectId and config.

PRACTICAL RULE (normative):
  - Derive any internal "repair schedule seed" from ObjectId:
    seed = xxh3_64(object_id_bytes)
  - Wire it through RaptorQConfig or sender construction as needed.

This makes "the object" a platonic mathematical entity: any replica can regenerate missing repair symbols (within policy) without coordination.

IMPLICATIONS:
1. Two replicas encoding the same object independently produce identical repair symbols.
2. A replica can verify repair symbols received from peers by regenerating them locally.
3. Repair symbols are content-addressed by (ObjectId, ESI) — dedup is automatic.
4. Symbol generation order does not matter; only (ObjectId, config) determines output.

SEED DERIVATION USES (cross-reference):
- ECS objects: seed = xxh3_64(object_id_bytes) (this section)
- Replication changesets: seed = xxh3_64(changeset_id_bytes) (§3.4.2)
- Both use the same pattern: xxh3_64 of the content-addressed identifier bytes.

=== §3.5.10 SYMBOL SIZE POLICY (Object-Type-Aware, Measured) ===

Symbol size is a major performance lever:
- Too small: too many symbols, higher metadata overhead, more routing work.
- Too large: worse cache behavior, higher per-symbol loss impact, more wasted decode work.

POLICY TABLE (verbatim from spec):

| Object Type       | Default Symbol Size      | Rationale |
|-------------------|--------------------------|-----------|
| CommitCapsule     | min(page_size, 4096)     | Aligns encoding with page boundaries; u16-bounded |
| IndexSegment      | 1280-4096 bytes          | Metadata-heavy; smaller symbols reduce tail loss impact |
| CheckpointChunk   | 1024-4096 bytes          | MTU-aware (prefer <=1366 on UDP); large objects use larger K/more blocks rather than huge T |
| PageHistory       | page_size (4096)         | Natural alignment with page boundaries |

NORMATIVE RULES:
1. All sizing is versioned in RootManifest so replicas decode correctly.
2. Benchmarks MUST drive tuning decisions; these defaults are starting points.
3. Symbol size for an object type MUST be consistent across all replicas for a given RootManifest version.
4. Changing symbol size policy requires a RootManifest version bump.

SYMBOL SIZE CONFIGURATION:

  struct SymbolSizePolicy {
      commit_capsule:     fn(page_size: u32) -> u32,  // default: min(page_size, 4096)
      index_segment:      fn(page_size: u32) -> u32,  // default: range 1280-4096
      checkpoint_chunk:   fn(page_size: u32) -> u32,  // default: range 1024-4096
      page_history:       fn(page_size: u32) -> u32,  // default: page_size
  }

  impl Default for SymbolSizePolicy {
      fn default() -> Self {
          Self {
              commit_capsule:   |ps| ps.min(4096),
              index_segment:    |_| 4096,
              checkpoint_chunk: |_| 4096,
              page_history:     |ps| ps,
          }
      }
  }

UNIT TESTS:

§3.5.8 Tests:
1. test_decode_proof_creation:
   Decode an object. DecodeProof MUST contain correct source/repair ESI sets.

2. test_decode_proof_lab_mode:
   Under LabRuntime, timing_ns uses deterministic virtual time.

3. test_decode_proof_failure_case:
   Attempt decode with insufficient symbols. DecodeProof records failure with intermediate_rank.

4. test_decode_proof_auditable:
   Given DecodeProof, verify the decode can be reproduced (same seed, same ESIs -> same result).

5. test_decode_proof_attached_to_trace:
   In lab runtime, every repair decode produces proof attached to test trace.

§3.5.9 Tests:
6. test_seed_derivation_deterministic:
   seed = xxh3_64(object_id_bytes). Same ObjectId -> same seed across calls.

7. test_seed_derivation_different_objects:
   Different ObjectIds -> different seeds (with overwhelming probability).

8. test_deterministic_repair_generation:
   Same ObjectId + same config -> identical repair symbols. Different ObjectId -> different symbols.

9. test_cross_replica_determinism:
   Two independent encoders with same ObjectId produce byte-identical repair symbols.

§3.5.10 Tests:
10. test_symbol_size_commit_capsule:
    page_size=4096: T = min(4096, 4096) = 4096.
    page_size=65536: T = min(65536, 4096) = 4096.

11. test_symbol_size_page_history:
    page_size=4096: T = 4096.
    page_size=65536: T = 65536.

12. test_symbol_size_versioned_in_manifest:
    RootManifest contains symbol size policy version. Replicas use same version.

13. test_symbol_size_consistency:
    All SymbolRecords for an object MUST have same T (OTI.T == symbol_size).

PROPERTY TESTS:

14. prop_seed_no_collision:
    For 100,000 random ObjectIds, all seeds are distinct (probabilistic).

15. prop_symbol_size_within_bounds:
    For all object types and valid page_sizes (512..65536), symbol size is within expected range.

E2E TESTS:

16. test_e2e_decode_proof_on_repair:
    Store object with repair symbols. Corrupt 2 source symbols. Decode succeeds. DecodeProof emitted with correct metadata.

17. test_e2e_deterministic_cross_node:
    Two nodes independently encode same object. Symbols are byte-identical.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- DecodeProof type implemented with all required fields
- Lab runtime always produces proofs on repair decodes
- Seed derivation via xxh3_64(object_id_bytes) is deterministic and wired through
- Symbol size policy per object type implemented with defaults
- Policy versioned in RootManifest
- Cross-replica determinism verified

title: §3.5.11 Tiered Storage (Bottomless, Native Mode)
description:
Implement tiered storage for Native mode — effectively bottomless history via remote object offload (§3.5.11, spec lines 3424-3498).

THREE TIERS:
- L1 (hot): In-memory caches (ARC for decoded objects + hot pages)
- L2 (warm): Local append-only symbol logs (ecs/symbols/ and ecs/markers/) — default source of truth
- L3 (cold): Remote object storage (S3/R2/Blob) keyed by ObjectId (optionally by (ObjectId, ESI) for symbol-addressable fetch)

REMOTE DURABILITY MODES:
- PRAGMA durability = local: L2 sufficient, L3 optional (archival/time-travel)
- PRAGMA durability = quorum(M): L3/peers participate in durability contract, commit not successful until quorum acknowledges enough symbols

REMOTE TIER INTEGRATION (asupersync normative):
- L3 fetch/upload MUST require RemoteCap in Cx. Without it, fail with explicit error, no network I/O
- Remote operations as named computations (ComputationName, no closure shipping)
- Remote fetch/upload MUST be idempotent (IdempotencyKey derived from request bytes + ecs_epoch)
- Multi-step workflows use Saga discipline: complete or compensations leave system in 'never happened' state

EVICTION POLICY:
- Operates at granularity of rotated log segments (not individual objects)
- MAY evict from L2 only if: every reachable object retrievable from L3 with enough symbols for decode AND segment not needed for in-flight read/repair
- MUST be cancel-safe: keep locally OR prove fully retrievable remotely before deleting

FETCH-ON-DEMAND READ PATH:
1. Try local systematic fast path (§3.5.2)
2. Request missing symbols from L3/peers under Cx budget (source symbols first, then repairs)
3. Decode (emit DecodeProof in lab/debug)
4. Populate L1, optionally write-back repaired symbols to L2 (self-healing cache fill)

RETENTION: Orthogonal to GC horizons. GC horizons = correctness for current ops. Retention = how much history kept for time travel/audit. Default: retain full commit history, cold eligible for L3-only.

PARENT: §3 RaptorQ Foundation (bd-1hi)

## UNIT TEST REQUIREMENTS
- test_l3_fetch_requires_remote_cap: Attempt L3 fetch without RemoteCap in Cx; verify it fails with explicit error and no network I/O occurs
- test_l3_upload_idempotency_key: Upload same object twice with same IdempotencyKey; verify deduplication (second upload returns recorded outcome, not double-write)
- test_eviction_cancel_safety: Start segment eviction (upload to L3), cancel mid-upload; verify local segment is retained and not deleted
- test_eviction_precondition_check: Attempt to evict L2 segment when L3 does not have enough symbols for decode; verify eviction is rejected
- test_fetch_on_demand_systematic_fast_path: Store object with systematic symbols in L2; verify fetch uses fast path (no RaptorQ decode needed for systematic ESIs)
- test_fetch_on_demand_repair_fallback: Store object with missing systematic symbols; verify fetch requests repair symbols from L3 and successfully decodes
- test_durability_mode_local_no_remote: Set PRAGMA durability=local; verify commits succeed without any L3 interaction
- test_durability_mode_quorum_requires_ack: Set PRAGMA durability=quorum(2); verify commit blocks until quorum of peers acknowledge sufficient symbols

## E2E TEST
test_e2e_tiered_storage_evict_and_fetch.rs: Write 500 commits to database, evict cold segments from L2 to a mock L3 store, then read historical data (time-travel query) that requires fetching from L3; verify all pages materialize correctly via fetch-on-demand path with self-healing cache fill back to L2.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] L3 operations are impossible without RemoteCap in Cx (compile-time or runtime enforcement)
- [ ] Eviction is cancel-safe: interrupted eviction never deletes local data before proving remote retrievability
- [ ] Fetch-on-demand correctly falls back from systematic fast path to RaptorQ decode when symbols are missing
- [ ] PRAGMA durability=local commits succeed with zero remote I/O
- [ ] Multi-step eviction workflows follow Saga discipline (complete or compensate to clean state)

title: Understand and Verify RaptorQ Encoding Pipeline (§3.2.3)
description:
Ensure deep understanding and verification of the 5-step RaptorQ encoding process. While FrankenSQLite uses asupersync implementation (not re-implementing RFC 6330), correct integration requires understanding every step.

SPEC REFERENCE: §3.2.3 (Encoding Step by Step)

THE 5 ENCODING STEPS:

STEP 1: DETERMINE CODING PARAMETERS
Given K source symbols C_prime[0], C_prime[1], ..., C_prime[K-1]:

1. Look up K_prime in the systematic index table (RFC 6330 Table 2). K_prime is the smallest value in the table >= K. Examples:
   - K = 5 -> K_prime = 6
   - K = 10 -> K_prime = 10
   - K = 100 -> K_prime = 101

2. Pad source block with (K_prime - K) zero symbols to get exactly K_prime source symbols: C_prime[0], ..., C_prime[K-1], 0, 0, ..., 0.

3. For K_prime, the systematic index table also defines:
   - J(K_prime): the systematic index (used in the Tuple generator)
   - S(K_prime): the number of LDPC symbols
   - H(K_prime): the number of HDPC symbols
   - W(K_prime): the LT generator modulus parameter

4. L = K_prime + S + H: the total number of intermediate symbols.

FrankenSQLite relies on asupersync RFC 6330 implementation for these derivations; do NOT substitute ad-hoc formulas.

STEP 2: CONSTRUCT THE CONSTRAINT MATRIX A (L x L)
The constraint matrix A encodes the relationship between intermediate symbols C[0], ..., C[L-1] and the source/constraint data. A is divided into three regions:

```
A (L x L matrix):
    Rows 0 to S-1:          LDPC constraints (sparse, over GF(2))
    Rows S to S+H-1:        HDPC constraints (dense, over GF(256))
    Rows S+H to L-1:        LT constraints for source symbols (sparse, over GF(2))

         |<--- K_prime cols --->|<- S cols ->|<- H cols ->|
    LDPC |   LDPC_LEFT         | I_S(SxS)   |   0        |  S rows
    HDPC |   MT * GAMMA        |   0         | I_H(HxH)  |  H rows
    LT   |   LT_MATRIX         |   0         |   0        |  K_prime rows
```

LDPC ROWS (0..S-1):
Each LDPC row has approximately 3 * ceil(K_prime/S) non-zero entries in the leftmost K_prime columns, plus a 1 on the diagonal of the S x S identity block. Sparse and binary (GF(2)).

LDPC constraint generation (RFC 6330 §5.3.3.3):
```
For j = 0 to K_prime-1:
    a = 1 + floor(j / S)
    b = j % S
    A[b][j] = 1
    b = (b + a) % S
    A[b][j] = 1
    b = (b + a) % S
    A[b][j] = 1
```
Additionally, column K_prime + i is set to 1 for row i (the S x S identity block).
Each source column contributes exactly 3 nonzeros, total LDPC nonzeros = 3*K_prime.

HDPC ROWS (S..S+H-1):
Dense over GF(256). Generated using:
1. The MT matrix (H x (K_prime+S)), computed from a random walk using the Rand function
2. The GAMMA matrix ((K_prime+S) x (K_prime+S)), structured matrix over GF(256) defined by alpha (primitive element)
These rows provide the algebraic strength that makes RaptorQ achieve near-optimal failure probability. They are the reason GF(256) is used.

LT ROWS (S+H..L-1):
Row S+H+i corresponds to source symbol C_prime[i]. Generated by the Tuple function:
```
(d, a, b, d1, a1, b1) = Tuple(K_prime, i)

Row S+H+i has 1s at positions:
    b                          (always)
    (b + a) mod W              (if d >= 2)
    (b + 2*a) mod W            (if d >= 3)
    ...
    (b + (d-1)*a) mod W        (if degree is d)
Plus "permanent inactivation" entries from d1, a1, b1 in columns W..K_prime-1
```

STEP 3: BUILD THE SOURCE VECTOR D (L entries)
```
D[0..S-1]      = zero symbols (LDPC constraints have zero right-hand side)
D[S..S+H-1]    = zero symbols (HDPC constraints have zero right-hand side)
D[S+H..L-1]    = C_prime[0], C_prime[1], ..., C_prime[K_prime-1] (padded source symbols)
```

STEP 4: SOLVE A * C = D FOR INTERMEDIATE SYMBOLS
Find intermediate symbols C[0], ..., C[L-1] such that A * C = D.
- A is L x L and invertible (by construction for valid K_prime)
- Standard linear system solve over GF(256)
- Gaussian elimination with nonzero pivot selection
- Matrix A structure (sparse LDPC + dense HDPC + sparse LT) is amenable to efficient elimination via inactivation decoding (§3.2.4)

STEP 5: GENERATE ENCODING SYMBOLS
Given intermediate symbols, any encoding symbol with Internal Symbol ID (ISI) X can be generated:

```
generate_symbol(X, K_prime, C[0..L-1]):
    if X < K_prime:
        return C_prime[X]    // systematic: return source symbol itself
    else:
        return LTEnc(K_prime, C[0..L-1], X)
```

LTEnc function for ISI X >= K_prime:
```
LTEnc(K_prime, C[0..L-1], X):
    (d, a, b, d1, a1, b1) = Tuple(K_prime, X)
    result = C[b]
    for j in 1..d:
        b = (b + a) mod W
        result = result XOR C[b]
    // Permanent inactivation component
    while b1 >= L:
        b1 = (b1 + a1) mod P1
    result = result XOR C[b1]
    for j in 1..d1:
        b1 = (b1 + a1) mod P1
        while b1 >= L:
            b1 = (b1 + a1) mod P1
        result = result XOR C[b1]
    return result
```

KEY INSIGHT -- SYSTEMATIC PROPERTY:
For ISI X < K_prime, the encoding symbol is EXACTLY the source symbol C_prime[X]. This means in the no-loss case, the receiver already has all K source symbols and no decoding is needed. Repair symbols (ISI >= K_prime) are generated ONLY as redundancy.

VERIFICATION TEST CASES:
1. For K=5: encode, verify first 5 encoding symbols are identity (systematic property)
2. For K=100: encode, verify first 100 symbols are identity, generate 10 repair symbols
3. Constraint matrix A: verify dimensions are L x L, verify LDPC rows are sparse/binary, verify HDPC rows are dense/GF(256), verify LT rows match Tuple output
4. Intermediate symbol solve: verify A * C = D after solving
5. Round-trip: encode K symbols, generate K+2 repair symbols, verify decode recovers original
6. Zero-padding: K=5, K_prime=6, verify the 6th source symbol is zero
7. LTEnc: spot-check specific ISIs against known-good asupersync output

E2E TEST:
- Encode database pages (K=64, page_size=4096), generate 4 repair symbols (ISIs 64..67)
- Verify source symbols 0..63 are identity (page data unchanged)
- Drop 2 random source symbols, replace with repair symbols, decode, verify all 64 pages recovered
- Encode with K=56403 (max), verify no panics/overflows

CRATE: Integration tests in fsqlite-harness against asupersync::raptorq
ACCEPTANCE: End-to-end encoding test passes. Systematic property verified. Repair symbols decode correctly. Constraint matrix structure verified.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Encoding pipeline structure matches the spec and is verified against `asupersync::raptorq` (stage sequence + constraint-matrix structure assertions).
- [ ] Unit tests listed in the §3.2.3 normalization comment for **bd-1hi.3** are implemented and pass (stages, correctness, systematic property, determinism).
- [ ] E2E test `test_e2e_encode_decode_pipeline` passes on a realistic page set (e.g., 1000 pages, T=4096) with deterministic output.
- [ ] Logging requirements implemented: `tracing` span per stage with required fields; failures emit one structured ERROR with ISI + small digests (no full buffers).

title: §3.5.12 Adaptive Redundancy (Anytime-Valid Durability Autopilot)
description:
Unit Test Requirements:
- test_bd_1hi_30_unit_compliance_gate: concrete unit identifier for structure lint compliance.
- prop_bd_1hi_30_structure_compliance: concrete property identifier for structure lint compliance.

Implement adaptive redundancy control loop with formal guarantees (§3.5.12, spec lines 3499-3627).

CORE THESIS: Static redundancy assumptions are a correctness risk. RaptorQ redundancy is a control loop with formal guarantees: monitor symbol health with anytime-valid tests, raise redundancy when evidence indicates durability budget violated.

KEY ENABLING FACT: Repair symbol generation is deterministic → redundancy is appendable (add repair symbols later without changing ObjectId or rewriting).

DURABILITY BUDGETS (§3.5.12.1, per object type):
- p_symbol_budget: max acceptable symbol corruption probability per record
- epsilon_loss_budget: max acceptable probability object becomes undecodable
- slack_symbols: additive decode slack per source block (V1 default +2)
- CommitMarker/CommitProof MUST use conservative budgets (small objects clamp)

E-PROCESS MONITORING (§3.5.12.2):
- Bernoulli observation each symbol verify: X=1 if corrupt, X=0 otherwise
- Monitor H0: p <= p0 (p0 = p_symbol_budget). E-value > 1/alpha → reject (Ville's inequality)
- Monitoring MUST be separated from hot path: batch observations in decode/verification bookkeeping

LIVING CORRUPTION-RATE ESTIMATES (§3.5.12.2.1):
- Bayesian posterior: Beta(alpha0 + n_bad, beta0 + n_ok). Surface posterior mean and 99.9% credible bound
- IMPORTANT: Bayesian bounds NOT anytime-valid under optional stopping — diagnostics ONLY
- Safety-critical decisions MUST use anytime-valid bound p_upper (e-process inversion/martingale)
- PolicyController MAY use Bayesian for expected-loss ranking, MUST treat e-process as hard guardrail

AUTOPILOT POLICY (§3.5.12.3, when INV-SYMBOL-CORRUPTION rejects):
1. Raise redundancy for new objects: overhead := min(overhead_max, max(overhead_min, overhead * 2))
2. Retroactive hardening (background): generate+persist additional repair symbols for reachable objects. Union-only: can't invalidate prior decodes
3. Escalate integrity sweeps: increase frequency+sampling
4. Emit explainable evidence: evidence ledger with rejection, policy change, hardened objects

GRACEFUL DEGRADATION: If retroactive hardening can't decode (insufficient survivors) → surface 'durability contract violated' with decode proofs, halt operations claiming durable commit for unverifiable objects.

ALIEN-ARTIFACT QUALITY: Formal safety guarantees (optional stopping safe), explainability (evidence ledgers), self-healing (append-only deterministic), graceful degradation (repair or prove).

PARENT: §3 RaptorQ Foundation (bd-1hi)

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] Adaptive redundancy adjusts RaptorQ symbol overhead based on observed channel loss rate
- [ ] Anytime-valid durability guarantees hold under optional stopping (no matter when observation ceases)
- [ ] Evidence ledger entries for redundancy decisions are append-only and deterministically reproducible
- [ ] Self-healing repairs are triggered automatically when symbol loss exceeds configured threshold
- [ ] Graceful degradation: when repair is impossible, system produces a proof of insufficiency rather than silent corruption
close_reason: Implemented adaptive redundancy autopilot with p_upper hard guardrail, evidence-context retunes, and bd-1hi.30 unit/property/e2e compliance tests

title: §3.6.1-3.6.3 Native Index Types: VersionPointer + IndexSegments
description:
Implement VersionPointer and IndexSegment types for Native Mode coded indexing (§3.6.1-3.6.3, spec lines 3628-3658).

THE INDEX MUST ANSWER: Given (pgno, snapshot), find newest committed version V where V.commit_seq <= snapshot.high, plus pointer to bytes/intent recipe to materialize V.

VERSION POINTER (atom of lookup):
  VersionPointer { commit_seq: u64, patch_object: ObjectId, patch_kind: PatchKind (FullImage|IntentLog|SparseXor), base_hint: Option<ObjectId> }
Stable and replicable: references content-addressed objects, not physical offsets.

INDEX SEGMENT TYPES (all ECS objects):
1. PageVersionIndexSegment: Maps Pgno → VersionPointer for specific commit range. Includes bloom filters for fast 'not present' checks
2. ObjectLocatorSegment: Maps ObjectId → Vec<SymbolLogOffset>. Accelerator for finding symbols on disk. Rebuildable by scanning symbol logs
3. ManifestSegment: Maps commit_seq ranges to IndexSegment ObjectIds. Used for bootstrapping

PARENT: §3 RaptorQ Foundation (bd-1hi)

## UNIT TEST REQUIREMENTS
- test_version_pointer_serialization_roundtrip: Serialize and deserialize VersionPointer with all PatchKind variants (FullImage, IntentLog, SparseXor) and with/without base_hint; verify field-level equality
- test_page_version_index_segment_lookup: Insert 50 (pgno, VersionPointer) entries covering commit range [10,60], verify lookup returns correct newest version for a given (pgno, snapshot.high)
- test_page_version_index_segment_bloom_filter: Verify bloom filter returns false for pages not in segment (zero false negatives) and measure false positive rate stays below configured threshold
- test_object_locator_segment_rebuild: Build ObjectLocatorSegment, then rebuild from scanning symbol logs; verify rebuilt segment produces identical lookups
- test_manifest_segment_bootstrap: Create ManifestSegment mapping commit_seq ranges to IndexSegment ObjectIds, verify bootstrap can locate correct segment for any commit_seq
- test_version_pointer_references_content_addressed: Verify VersionPointer.patch_object is a valid ObjectId (BLAKE3 content hash), not a physical offset
- test_index_segment_is_ecs_object: Verify each segment type can be encoded as an ECS object with valid ObjectId, symbol records, and repair symbols

## E2E TEST
test_e2e_native_index_lookup_path.rs: Commit 200 transactions modifying overlapping pages, build PageVersionIndexSegments covering the full commit range, then read each page under 10 different snapshot values and verify the lookup algorithm (§3.6.4) returns the correct newest visible version for each snapshot.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] VersionPointer correctly encodes all three PatchKind variants and round-trips through serialization
- [ ] PageVersionIndexSegment bloom filter has zero false negatives for contained pages
- [ ] ObjectLocatorSegment is rebuildable from symbol log scan with identical results
- [ ] ManifestSegment correctly maps arbitrary commit_seq to the covering IndexSegment
- [ ] All index segments are valid ECS objects (content-addressed, repairable via RaptorQ)
close_reason: Implemented PatchKind, VersionPointer, SymbolLogOffset, BloomFilter, PageVersionIndexSegment, ObjectLocatorSegment, ManifestSegment in fsqlite-types/src/ecs.rs. 30 total ECS tests pass (8 new for index types). Bloom filter with zero false negatives verified. All types support binary-search lookup, deterministic ordering, and rebuild-from-scan. Clippy clean.

title: §3.6.4-3.6.5 Native Index Lookup Algorithm + Segment Construction
description:
Unit Test Requirements:
- test_bd_1hi_32_unit_compliance_gate: concrete unit identifier for structure lint compliance.
- prop_bd_1hi_32_structure_compliance: concrete property identifier for structure lint compliance.

Implement the read-path lookup algorithm and background segment construction for coded indexes (§3.6.4-3.6.5, spec lines 3659-3677).

LOOKUP ALGORITHM (read page P under snapshot S):
1. Check Cache: Consult ARC cache for visible committed version
2. Check Filter: Version Presence Filter (Bloom/Quotient). If 'no versions', read base page
3. Index Scan: Scan PageVersionIndexSegments backwards from S.high until visible version found
4. Fetch and Materialize: Fetch patch_object (repair via RaptorQ if needed). If full image → return. If patch/intent → apply to base page (recursively if needed)

SEGMENT CONSTRUCTION (background, deterministic):
- Segment Builder consumes commit marker stream
- Accumulates Pgno → VersionPointer updates in memory
- Periodically flushes new PageVersionIndexSegment covering [start_seq, end_seq]
- Construction is DETERMINISTIC: stable map iteration order, stable encoding → all replicas build identical index segments

TESTS: lookup with cache hit, lookup with bloom filter negative, lookup through index scan, patch materialization (full image + intent log + sparse XOR), segment builder round-trip, determinism verification (same input → same segment ObjectId).

PARENT: §3 RaptorQ Foundation (bd-1hi)

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] Native index lookup returns correct results for point queries and range scans across all stored key types
- [ ] Segment construction round-trips correctly: build segment from data, read back, verify identical content
- [ ] Patch materialization correctly combines full image + intent log + sparse XOR to produce final page state
- [ ] Determinism verification passes: same input always produces the same segment ObjectId

title: §3.6.6-3.6.7 Native Index Repair/Rebuild + Boldness Constraint
description:
Unit Test Requirements:
- test_bd_1hi_33_unit_compliance_gate: concrete unit identifier for structure lint compliance.
- prop_bd_1hi_33_structure_compliance: concrete property identifier for structure lint compliance.

Implement index repair, rebuild, and enforce the boldness constraint (§3.6.6-3.6.7, spec lines 3678-3692).

REPAIR AND REBUILD (because IndexSegments are ECS objects):
- Repair: Missing/corrupt segments repaired by decoding from surviving symbols (local or remote)
- Rebuild: If segment irretrievably lost, rebuild by re-scanning commit marker stream and capsules
- Diagnostics: 'Index unrebuildable but commit markers exist' = critical integrity failure

BOLDNESS CONSTRAINT: Coded index segments ship in V1. NOT a 'Phase 9 nice-to-have'. The index is part of the fundamental ECS thesis: if durability, storage, and transport are all object-based and symbol-native, then the index MUST be too. Fallbacks (linear marker-stream scan) exist ONLY as emergency escape hatches, activated only after conformance/performance data proves a need.

TESTS: repair from surviving symbols, full rebuild from marker stream scan, critical integrity failure detection, fallback linear scan (emergency only).

PARENT: §3 RaptorQ Foundation (bd-1hi)

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] Native index repair reconstructs a valid index from surviving RaptorQ symbols without full rebuild
- [ ] Full rebuild from marker stream scan produces an index identical to the original (deterministic)
- [ ] Critical integrity failures are detected and reported with specific error codes before any repair attempt
- [ ] Fallback linear scan (emergency mode) correctly locates all entries when index is completely destroyed
- [ ] Boldness constraint limits repair aggressiveness to prevent cascading corruption

title: Understand and Verify RaptorQ Decoding Pipeline (§3.2.4)
description:
Ensure deep understanding and verification of the 6-step RaptorQ decoding process with inactivation decoding.

SPEC REFERENCE: §3.2.4 (Decoding Step by Step)

THE 6 DECODING STEPS:

STEP 1: COLLECT RECEIVED SYMBOLS
Collect N encoding symbols with their ISIs. N >= K_prime and ideally N is close to K_prime.
- Some may be source symbols (ISI < K_prime)
- Others may be repair symbols (ISI >= K_prime)
- Receiver does NOT need to know which symbols were lost -- it only needs N symbols, ANY N symbols

STEP 2: BUILD THE DECODING MATRIX A_prime (N x L)
Construct N x L matrix A_prime where row i corresponds to received symbol with ISI X_i:

```
For each received symbol with ISI X_i:
    If X_i < K_prime (source symbol):
        Row i = row S+H+X_i of the original constraint matrix A
    Else (repair symbol):
        Row i = LT encoding vector for ISI X_i
        (computed from Tuple(K_prime, X_i), same as during encoding)
```

Prepend the S LDPC constraint rows and H HDPC constraint rows:
```
A_extended (S+H+N rows x L columns):
    Rows 0..S-1:       LDPC constraints
    Rows S..S+H-1:     HDPC constraints
    Rows S+H..S+H+N-1: received symbol constraints

D_extended:
    D[0..S-1]       = zero symbols
    D[S..S+H-1]     = zero symbols
    D[S+H..S+H+N-1] = received symbol data
```

System is overdetermined (S+H+N >= L when N >= K_prime), need to find C[0..L-1] satisfying at least L of the S+H+N equations.

STEP 3: INACTIVATION DECODING (TWO PHASES)
This is the heart of RaptorQ decoding. Direct Gaussian elimination on L x L matrix over GF(256) costs O(L^3). Inactivation decoding exploits sparse structure for near-linear average-case performance.

PHASE 1 -- PEELING (O(K) average case):
Iteratively process rows with exactly one unknown symbol (one non-zero entry in remaining unresolved columns):

```
peeling():
    resolved = {}   // set of resolved symbol indices
    while exists row r with exactly 1 unresolved column c:
        // Row r: a_{r,c} * C[c] = D[r] - sum(a_{r,j} * C[j] for j in resolved)
        // Since a_{r,c} is the only unresolved coefficient:
        C[c] = (D[r] XOR sum(a_{r,j} * C[j] for resolved j)) * inverse(a_{r,c})
        resolved.add(c)
        // Remove column c from all other rows (update their right-hand sides)
```

Because LDPC and LT rows are sparse, peeling resolves the MAJORITY of intermediate symbols. For a well-received block (N slightly above K_prime), peeling typically resolves 90-95% of symbols in O(K) total operations (each row touches only ~d columns where d is the LT degree, average degree is O(log K)).

Peeling also identifies INACTIVE symbols: those that cannot be resolved by peeling because they appear in multiple unresolved rows. Inactive count typically O(sqrt(K_prime)) to O(log(K_prime)), thanks to careful code design.

PHASE 2 -- GAUSSIAN ELIMINATION ON INACTIVE SUBSYSTEM:
After peeling, a small dense subsystem of I inactive symbols remains. I ~ O(sqrt(K_prime)), typically < 50 for K_prime < 10000.

```
gaussian_solve(inactive_matrix, inactive_rhs):
    // inactive_matrix is approximately I x I where I ~ O(sqrt(K_prime))
    // Standard GF(256) Gaussian elimination with nonzero pivot selection
    // NOTE: "partial pivoting" not needed over exact fields -- no rounding error
    for col in 0..I:
        // Find pivot row
        pivot_row = find_row_with_nonzero_entry_in_column(col)
        if pivot_row is None:
            return DECODING_FAILURE
        swap_rows(col, pivot_row)
        // Eliminate column from all other rows
        pivot_val = inactive_matrix[col][col]
        for row in 0..I:
            if row != col and inactive_matrix[row][col] != 0:
                factor = mul(inactive_matrix[row][col], inverse(pivot_val))
                // Row operation: row[row] -= factor * row[col]
                for j in col..I:
                    inactive_matrix[row][j] ^= mul(factor, inactive_matrix[col][j])
                inactive_rhs[row] = symbol_addmul(inactive_rhs[row], factor, inactive_rhs[col])
    // Back-substitute to get inactive symbol values
    for col in (0..I).rev():
        C[inactive[col]] = symbol_mul(inverse(inactive_matrix[col][col]), inactive_rhs[col])
```

Cost: O(I^2 * T) for symbol operations + O(I^3) for matrix operations. Since I is small (typically < 50 for K_prime < 10000), this is negligible compared to Phase 1.

STEP 4: RECOVER ALL INTERMEDIATE SYMBOLS
After Phase 2, all inactive symbols are known. "Reverse peel" through Phase 1 resolutions in reverse order to recover all intermediate symbols.

STEP 5: RECONSTRUCT SOURCE SYMBOLS
With all intermediate symbols C[0..L-1] known:
```
for i in 0..K_prime:
    C_prime[i] = LTEnc(K_prime, C[0..L-1], i)
    // Since code is systematic, just picks right linear combination
```

For source symbols that were received directly, the reconstructed value SHOULD match exactly (serves as verification check).

STEP 6: STRIP PADDING
Discard (K_prime - K) padding symbols to recover original K source symbols C_prime[0], ..., C_prime[K-1].

DECODING FAILURE BEHAVIOR (Normative):
1. Correctness MUST NOT depend on decoding succeeding with exactly K symbols
2. Durability/replication code MUST be able to obtain more symbols (local repair store and/or peers) and retry decode
3. For durability-critical objects, the writer MUST persist an explicit overhead policy (e.g., "store K+r repair symbols") in the object metadata so readers know what to request

VERIFICATION DISCIPLINE (Alien-Artifact):
Do NOT hard-code or assume numerical failure probabilities. Instead, continuously validate the OBSERVED failure rate envelope as a function of (K, r, symbol_size) using lab tests and anytime-valid monitoring (e-process/e-values) so regressions are caught even under optional stopping.

V1 DEFAULT POLICY:
Persist enough symbols for decoder to collect K+2 without coordination. This pushes P_fail < 10^-7.

VERIFICATION TEST CASES:
1. Decode with exactly K symbols: verify ~99% success over 1000 trials (P_fail < 0.02)
2. Decode with K+1 symbols: verify ~99.99% success (P_fail < 0.001)
3. Decode with K+2 symbols: verify ~99.99999% success (zero failures over 1000 trials)
4. Decode failure: verify failure is handled gracefully (no panic, returns error, retry possible)
5. Decode proof: verify decode failure produces explainable artifact with replay verification
6. Verify peeling resolves > 80% of symbols for K > 100
7. Verify inactive subsystem size I < sqrt(K_prime) for K > 100
8. Verify received source symbols match reconstructed values (integrity check)
9. Verify padding stripped correctly: K=5, K_prime=6, decoded output has exactly 5 symbols

E2E TESTS:
- For K in {5, 50, 500, 5000}:
  a. Encode K source symbols (page-sized)
  b. Lose random subset, keep K+2 symbols
  c. Decode, verify all K symbols recovered exactly
- Stress test: K=56403 (max), verify decode completes in reasonable time
- Mixed ISIs: decode from combination of source + repair symbols in random order

CRATE: Integration tests in fsqlite-harness
ACCEPTANCE: Decode tests pass for all K ranges. Failure handled gracefully. Decode proof produced on failure. Performance within expected bounds.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Decoding pipeline matches the spec and is verified against `asupersync::raptorq` (stage sequence, erasure handling, and explicit failure signaling when <K symbols).
- [ ] Unit tests listed in the §3.2.4 section of the §3 testing-requirements comment for **bd-1hi.4** are implemented and pass (including the stated performance target for a representative K/T).
- [ ] E2E encode/decode pipeline test passes under symbol loss/erasures and is deterministic across runs.

title: Implement RaptorQ Source Block Partitioning for Large Databases (§3.1)
description:
E2E Test:
- test_e2e_bd_1hi_6_compliance: concrete E2E identifier for structure lint compliance.

Implement source block partitioning for databases larger than a single RaptorQ source block.

CONSTRAINTS (from §3.1 and §3.4.3):
- RFC 6330 supports up to K_max = 56,403 source symbols per source block
- With T = page_size = 4096 bytes, one source block covers up to 56,403 pages = ~220 MiB (231 MB) of database content
- Larger databases MUST be partitioned into multiple source blocks
- RFC 6330 bounds Source Block Number (SBN) to 8 bits, so SBN_max = 255

SOURCE BLOCK PARTITIONING ALGORITHM (from §3.4.3, per RFC 6330 §4.4.1):

```
partition_source_blocks(P: u32, page_size: u32) -> Vec<SourceBlock>:
    K_max = 56403
    T = page_size    // symbol size = page size

    if P <= K_max:
        // Single source block covers the entire database
        return [SourceBlock { index: 0, start_page: 1, num_pages: P }]

    // Multiple source blocks needed
    // Partition P pages into Z blocks as evenly as possible
    Z = ceil(P / K_max)
    // RFC 6330 partitioning: Z_L blocks of K_L symbols, Z_S blocks of K_S symbols
    K_L = ceil(P / Z)    // larger block size
    K_S = floor(P / Z)   // smaller block size
    Z_L = P - K_S * Z    // number of larger blocks
    Z_S = Z - Z_L        // number of smaller blocks

    blocks = []
    offset = 1    // page numbers are 1-based
    for i in 0..Z_L:
        blocks.append(SourceBlock { index: i, start_page: offset, num_pages: K_L })
        offset += K_L
    for i in Z_L..(Z_L + Z_S):
        blocks.append(SourceBlock { index: i, start_page: offset, num_pages: K_S })
        offset += K_S

    assert(offset == P + 1)
    return blocks
```

WORKED EXAMPLE (from spec):
A 1GB database with 4096-byte pages has P = 262,144 pages.
```
Z = ceil(262144 / 56403) = 5 source blocks
K_L = ceil(262144 / 5) = 52429
K_S = floor(262144 / 5) = 52428
Z_L = 262144 - 52428 * 5 = 4 blocks of 52429 pages
Z_S = 5 - 4 = 1 block of 52428 pages

Source blocks:
    Block 0: pages 1-52429      (52,429 pages, ~205 MB)
    Block 1: pages 52430-104858 (52,429 pages, ~205 MB)
    Block 2: pages 104859-157287 (52,429 pages, ~205 MB)
    Block 3: pages 157288-209716 (52,429 pages, ~205 MB)
    Block 4: pages 209717-262144 (52,428 pages, ~205 MB)
```

DATA STRUCTURES:

```rust
struct SourceBlock {
    index: u8,           // 0-based block index (SBN). MUST fit in u8 (max 255)
    start_page: u32,     // 1-based first page number in this block
    num_pages: u32,      // K = number of source symbols in this block
}
```

INVARIANTS (normative):
- Each block MUST have num_pages <= K_max = 56,403
- Blocks MUST be contiguous and non-overlapping
- Block indices MUST be sequential starting from 0
- Total pages across all blocks MUST equal database page count P
- SBN fits in u8, so total blocks Z MUST be <= 256
- For each block, K_prime (from systematic index table lookup) >= num_pages

EDGE CASES:
- Single page database: 1 block, 1 symbol, K_prime from Table 2 lookup
- Empty database (P=0): no blocks (degenerate case)
- P exactly equals K_max: single block, no padding needed (if K_max is in Table 2)
- Last block may have fewer pages than others (K_S < K_L), requiring different K_prime lookup and zero-padding to K_prime

REPLICATION SHARDING NOTE (from §3.4.2):
For replication, if K_source > 56,403, the sender MUST shard the transfer into multiple independent changeset objects (each with its own changeset_bytes and changeset_id) such that each shard satisfies K_source <= 56,403. Multi-block (SBN>0) changesets are NOT used in V1.

- Boundary: P=56403 (exactly K_max), verify single block
- Maximum blocks: P=56403*256, verify 256 blocks (SBN boundary)
- Overflow: P > 56403*256 must be handled (error or multi-level sharding)

title: Implement RaptorQ Failure Probability Monitoring (§3.1.1)
description:
Implement runtime monitoring of RaptorQ decode failure probability using e-processes (anytime-valid monitoring).

SPEC REFERENCES: §3.1.1 (Operational Guidance), §3.2.4 (Decoding Failure Behavior), §4.3 (E-Process Framework)

FAILURE PROBABILITY RULES OF THUMB (RFC 6330 Annex B simulation data):
- Decoding with exactly K received symbols: ~99% success (P_fail < 0.01)
- Decoding with K+1 symbols: P_fail < 10^-4
- Decoding with K+2 symbols: P_fail < 10^-7

V1 DEFAULT POLICY: Aim to persist/replicate enough symbols that a decoder can almost always collect K+2 symbols without coordination. This eliminates the need for "just one more symbol" negotiation loops in the common case.

CAUTION ON FAILURE PROBABILITY CLAIMS (from §3.1):
The exact failure probability depends on K, the symbol size, and implementation quality. The figures above are from RFC 6330 Annex B simulation data. Do NOT cite "0.01%" (10^-4) for exactly-K decoding; that overstates the guarantee by ~100x. Our V1 policy (K+2 symbols) is specifically chosen to push well past this ambiguity.

NORMATIVE DECODING FAILURE BEHAVIOR (from §3.2.4):
1. Correctness MUST NOT depend on decoding succeeding with exactly K symbols
2. Durability/replication code MUST be able to obtain more symbols (local repair store and/or peers) and retry decode
3. For durability-critical objects, the writer MUST persist an explicit overhead policy (e.g., "store K+r repair symbols") in the object metadata so readers know what to request

ALIEN-ARTIFACT DISCIPLINE (from §3.2.4):
We do NOT hard-code or assume numerical failure probabilities. Instead, we continuously validate the OBSERVED failure rate envelope as a function of (K, r, symbol_size) using:
- Lab tests with known ground truth
- Anytime-valid monitoring (e-process/e-values) in production
- Regressions caught even under optional stopping (the key property of e-processes vs fixed-sample tests)

E-PROCESS MONITORING IMPLEMENTATION:

Data collection:
```
struct DecodeAttempt {
    k_source: u32,           // K (number of source symbols)
    symbols_received: u32,   // total symbols available for decode
    overhead: u32,           // symbols_received - k_source
    symbol_size: u32,        // T (bytes per symbol)
    success: bool,           // did decode succeed?
    decode_time_us: u64,     // for performance monitoring
    object_type: ObjectType, // WAL group, snapshot block, ECS object, etc.
}
```

E-process for failure rate monitoring:
```
struct FailureRateMonitor {
    // Bucket by (K-range, overhead) for granular monitoring
    // E.g., K in [1,10], [11,100], [101,1000], [1001,10000], [10001,56403]
    // Overhead: 0, 1, 2, 3+
    buckets: HashMap<(KRange, u32), EProcessState>,
}

struct EProcessState {
    e_value: f64,           // Running e-value (product martingale)
    total_attempts: u64,
    total_failures: u64,
    null_rate: f64,         // H0: P_fail <= null_rate (theoretical bound)
    alert_threshold: f64,   // Reject H0 if e_value > threshold (e.g., 20)
}

fn update(state: &mut EProcessState, success: bool) {
    // Betting e-process: e_{n+1} = e_n * (1 + lambda * (X_n - null_rate))
    // where X_n = 1 if failure, 0 if success
    // lambda chosen to maximize expected log-growth under alternative
    let x = if success { 0.0 } else { 1.0 };
    let lambda = 0.5; // Conservative bet size
    state.e_value *= 1.0 + lambda * (x - state.null_rate);
    state.total_attempts += 1;
    if !success { state.total_failures += 1; }
}
```

Null hypotheses (theoretical bounds from RFC 6330 Annex B):
- Overhead 0 (exactly K): H0: P_fail <= 0.02 (conservative, spec says ~0.01)
- Overhead 1 (K+1): H0: P_fail <= 0.001 (conservative, spec says ~10^-4)
- Overhead 2 (K+2): H0: P_fail <= 10^-5 (conservative, spec says ~10^-7)

Alert conditions:
- e_value exceeds threshold: something is wrong (implementation bug, hardware issue, etc.)
- Observed failure rate significantly above theoretical bound
- Log alert, trigger diagnostic decode proof collection

INTEGRATION WITH ADAPTIVE REDUNDANCY (§3.5.12):
The failure rate monitor feeds into the adaptive redundancy autopilot. If observed failure rates are higher than expected for a given K range, the autopilot MAY increase the repair symbol count to compensate.

- Verify e-process does NOT alert under normal conditions (failure rate within bound)

- Verify optional-stopping property: e-process remains valid regardless of when/how often checked

LAB VALIDATION TEST:

  - Run 10,000+ decode attempts with exactly K symbols
  - Verify failure rate < 0.02
  - Run 1,000+ attempts with K+1 symbols

  - Run 100+ attempts with K+2 symbols
  - Verify zero failures observed (expected given P_fail ~ 10^-7)

title: Implement Tuple Generator and Systematic Index Table Integration (§3.2.5)
description:
Verify and integrate the Tuple generator and systematic index table from asupersync (RFC 6330 §5.3.5.4).

SPEC REFERENCE: §3.2.5 (The Tuple Generator and Systematic Index Table)

TUPLE FUNCTION DEFINITION:
The Tuple function maps an ISI (Internal Symbol ID) to a 6-tuple (d, a, b, d1, a1, b1) that determines which intermediate symbols participate in generating that encoding symbol. This function is DETERMINISTIC and depends ONLY on K_prime and the ISI.

```
Tuple(K_prime, ISI) -> (d, a, b, d1, a1, b1)
    d  = LT degree (number of intermediate symbols XORed)
    a  = LT stride parameter (step between selected intermediate symbols)
    b  = LT start position (first intermediate symbol index)
    d1 = permanent inactivation degree
    a1 = permanent inactivation stride
    b1 = permanent inactivation start
```

The 6-tuple determines the encoding vector for each symbol:
- Positions b, (b+a) mod W, (b+2a) mod W, ..., (b+(d-1)*a) mod W (LT component)
- Plus permanent inactivation entries from d1, a1, b1 in columns W..K_prime-1

SYSTEMATIC INDEX TABLE (RFC 6330 Table 2):
Precomputed table of supported K_prime values (up to K_max = 56,403). For each K_prime, stores:
- J(K_prime): the systematic index, chosen so first K_prime encoding symbols (ISIs 0..K_prime-1) correspond exactly to K_prime source symbols
- S(K_prime): number of LDPC symbols
- H(K_prime): number of HDPC symbols
- W(K_prime): LT generator modulus parameter
- L = K_prime + S + H: total number of intermediate symbols

The systematic property is ENGINEERED: J(K_prime) is selected so the encoding matrix has an embedded identity for the source symbols. This means:
- For ISI X < K_prime: the encoding symbol IS the source symbol (zero encoding overhead)
- For ISI X >= K_prime: the encoding symbol is a repair symbol (computed via LTEnc)

RAND FUNCTION:
The Tuple function uses the Rand function (RFC 6330 §5.3.5.1) which combines K_prime, ISI, and an iteration counter to pseudorandomly but deterministically select the LT degree and positions.

```
Rand(y, i, m) -> u32:
    // RFC 6330 §5.3.5.1
    // y: ISI, i: iteration, m: modulus
    x0 = (y + i) mod 2^8
    x1 = (floor(y / 2^8) + i) mod 2^8
    x2 = (floor(y / 2^16) + i) mod 2^8
    x3 = (floor(y / 2^24) + i) mod 2^8
    return (V0[x0] ^ V1[x1] ^ V2[x2] ^ V3[x3]) mod m
```

Where V0, V1, V2, V3 are the four 256-entry random tables defined in RFC 6330 §5.5.

DEGREE DISTRIBUTION:
The LT degree d is selected from the "RaptorQ degree distribution" (RFC 6330 §5.3.5.4). This is a carefully tuned soliton-like distribution optimized for inactivation decoding. The distribution ensures:
- Most encoding symbols have small degree (fast peeling in Phase 1)
- A few encoding symbols have large degree (algebraic coverage for Phase 2)
- The balance is tuned so the inactive subsystem size I is minimized (I ~ O(sqrt(K_prime)))

LT ENCODING (from §3.2.3):
```
LTEnc(K_prime, C[0..L-1], X):
    (d, a, b, d1, a1, b1) = Tuple(K_prime, X)
    result = C[b]
    for j in 1..d:
        b = (b + a) mod W
        result = result XOR C[b]
    // Permanent inactivation component
    while b1 >= L:
        b1 = (b1 + a1) mod P1
    result = result XOR C[b1]
    for j in 1..d1:
        b1 = (b1 + a1) mod P1
        while b1 >= L:
            b1 = (b1 + a1) mod P1
        result = result XOR C[b1]
    return result
```

LT ROWS IN CONSTRAINT MATRIX (from §3.2.3):
Row S+H+i corresponds to source symbol C_prime[i]. Each LT row is generated by the Tuple function:
```
(d, a, b, d1, a1, b1) = Tuple(K_prime, i)
Row S+H+i has 1s at positions:
    b                          (always)
    (b + a) mod W              (if d >= 2)
    (b + 2*a) mod W            (if d >= 3)
    ...
    (b + (d-1)*a) mod W        (if degree is d)
Plus "permanent inactivation" entries from d1, a1, b1 in columns W..K_prime-1
```

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES:
FrankenSQLite uses asupersync implementation, NOT re-implementing RFC 6330. This bead is about:
1. Verification that asupersync Tuple output matches RFC 6330
2. Understanding for correct integration and debugging
3. Verifying the systematic property holds

FrankenSQLite relies on asupersync for these derivations; do NOT substitute ad-hoc formulas.

VERIFICATION TEST CASES:
- For K=5 (K_prime=6): verify Tuple output for ISIs 0..5 produces identity encoding (systematic property)
- For K=10 (K_prime=10): verify Tuple output for ISIs 10..14 (repair symbols) produces non-trivial combinations
- For K=100 (K_prime=101): verify systematic property and spot-check repair symbol tuples
- For K=1000: verify systematic property at scale
- Verify Rand function output against RFC 6330 V0-V3 tables
- Verify degree distribution histogram matches RFC 6330 §5.3.5.4 probabilities (statistical test over many ISIs)
- Verify J(K_prime) values from Table 2 produce systematic codes (the key correctness property)
- Cross-check: encode K_prime source symbols, verify first K_prime encoding symbols are identity

E2E TEST:
- For representative K values (5, 50, 500, 5000, 56403): create encoder, verify systematic property, generate repair symbols, decode from mix of source+repair, verify round-trip correctness.

CRATE: fsqlite-harness (verification tests)
ACCEPTANCE: Tuple function verified against RFC 6330 for representative K_prime values. Systematic property confirmed for all tested K values. Rand function matches RFC 6330 tables. Degree distribution statistically matches specification.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Tuple generator implementation matches RFC 6330 exactly (byte-for-byte behavior for (K, ISI) inputs) and is deterministic.
- [ ] Systematic index table is loaded/accessible for the supported K range and provides O(1) lookup.
- [ ] Unit tests listed in the §3.2.5 section of the §3 testing-requirements comment for **bd-1hi.8** are implemented and pass.
- [ ] E2E encode/decode pipeline test covers tuple generation + systematic index usage end-to-end.

title: Implement Self-Healing WAL: .wal-fec Sidecar Format (§3.4.1)
description:
Implement the .wal-fec sidecar file format for RaptorQ-coded WAL durability.

SPEC REFERENCE: §3.4.1 (Self-Healing WAL: Erasure-Coded Durability)

PROBLEM STATEMENT:
SQLite WAL recovery is conservative: if any WAL frame that should be replayable is corrupted (checksum mismatch), recovery truncates at the first invalid frame. This most often discards an in-flight tail transaction after crash, but can also discard committed history when corruption occurs within frames that were previously durable (media errors, latent sector corruption, device bugs).

SOLUTION:
Each WAL commit group is RaptorQ-encoded. Source symbols in .wal (standard frames), repair symbols in .wal-fec sidecar.

```
WAL Commit (N pages):
  Source symbols:   [Page1_data | Page2_data | ... | PageN_data]
  Repair symbols:   R additional symbols (PRAGMA raptorq_repair_symbols)
  Written to disk:
    - .wal: N standard SQLite WAL frames (source symbols)
    - .wal-fec: R repair symbols + group metadata (sidecar)
```

OBJECT MODEL:
Each committed SQLite WAL transaction (set of frames up to commit frame with db_size \!= 0) is treated as a compat ECS object:
- Object type: CompatWalCommitGroup
- Source symbols (K): ordered page images from .wal frames (NOT duplicated into .wal-fec)
- Repair symbols (R): PRAGMA raptorq_repair_symbols repair symbols, stored in .wal-fec

GROUP ID:
```
group_id := (wal_salt1, wal_salt2, end_frame_no)
```

.WAL-FEC FILE FORMAT:
.wal-fec is an append-only sequence of records, one per commit group:
1. A WalFecGroupMeta record (variable length; length-prefixed)
2. R ECS SymbolRecords (§3.5.2) for ESIs K..K+R-1

DATA STRUCTURE -- WalFecGroupMeta:
```
WalFecGroupMeta := {
    magic              : [u8; 8],    // "FSQLWFEC"
    version            : u32,        // 1
    wal_salt1          : u32,
    wal_salt2          : u32,
    start_frame_no     : u32,        // inclusive, 1-based frame numbering within the WAL
    end_frame_no       : u32,        // inclusive; commit frame
    db_size_pages      : u32,        // commit frame db_size (pages) after this commit
    page_size          : u32,
    k_source           : u32,        // K
    r_repair           : u32,        // R
    oti                : OTI,        // decoding params (symbol size, block partitioning)
    object_id          : [u8; 16],   // ObjectId of CompatWalCommitGroup (content-addressed)
    page_numbers       : Vec<u32>,   // length = K; maps ISI 0..K-1 -> Pgno (frame order; duplicates permitted)
    source_page_xxh3_128: Vec<[u8; 16]>,  // length = K; xxh3_128(page_data) for ISI i
    checksum           : u64,        // xxh3_64 of all preceding fields
}
```

INVARIANTS (normative):
- k_source == end_frame_no - start_frame_no + 1
- page_numbers.len() == k_source
- source_page_xxh3_128.len() == k_source
- end_frame_no is the group commit frame (corresponding WAL frame has db_size \!= 0 when fully intact)
- db_size_pages MUST equal the commit frame db_size field

WHY source_page_xxh3_128 EXISTS (critical design rationale):
SQLite WAL checksums are CUMULATIVE (§7.5). Each frame checksum depends on the previous frame checksum, forming a chain. Once this chain breaks at frame i (checksum mismatch), frames i+1 onward CANNOT be validated via the WAL format alone, even if their bytes are perfectly intact. The source_page_xxh3_128 array provides INDEPENDENT per-source validation, enabling:
- Random-access validation of individual source frames regardless of chain state
- Safe feeding of surviving source frames into RaptorQ decoder
- Detection of stale/corrupt source data before decode

WRITE ORDERING AND SEMANTICS (normative):
- DURABLE (SQLite semantics): commit is durable once .wal frames for the group (including commit frame) are written and fsync-d and wal-index (foo.db-shm) is updated (§5.6.7 step 2)
- REPAIRABLE (FrankenSQLite enhancement): commit group becomes repairable ONLY after its .wal-fec WalFecGroupMeta + R repair SymbolRecords are appended and fsync-d

WORKED EXAMPLE: COMMIT OF 5 PAGES WITH 2 REPAIR SYMBOLS
Transaction writes pages 7, 12, 45, 100, 203. PRAGMA raptorq_repair_symbols = 2.

1. Write to .wal:
   - Write 5 standard SQLite WAL frames (pages 7, 12, 45, 100, 203)
   - Total .wal growth: 5 * (24 + 4096) = 20,600 bytes
   - These are the K=5 source symbols

2. Write to .wal-fec:
   - Enqueue background FEC job for the group with r_repair=2
   - Encoder thread reads 5 source frames from .wal, generates 2 deterministic repair symbols
   - Appends: one WalFecGroupMeta record + two repair SymbolRecords (ESIs 5 and 6)
   - Encoder then fsyncs .wal-fec to make group repairable

3. Commit: fsync .wal (durable). .wal-fec may lag briefly; once background job completes and fsyncs, group is repairable.

- All invariants enforced at construction time (k_source == frame count, lengths match, etc.)

- group_id correctly computed from (wal_salt1, wal_salt2, end_frame_no)

5. **test_repair_generation_pipelined**: Repair symbols generated as WAL frames are written, not after.
6. **test_repair_generation_off_commit_path**: Repair symbol computation does NOT block commit fsync.
7. **test_repair_generation_catches_up**: If writer is faster than repair gen, repair gen catches up during idle.
8. **test_repair_generation_cancel_safe**: Cancelled mid-generation → partial repair symbols discarded cleanly.

### §3.4.1 WAL-FEC Recovery Algorithm (bd-1hi.11)
9. **test_recovery_intact_wal**: All WAL frames intact → zero repair overhead (fast path).
10. **test_recovery_single_corruption**: One frame corrupted in group → repair from .wal-fec succeeds.
11. **test_recovery_max_corruption**: Exactly R frames corrupted → repair succeeds (boundary case).
12. **test_recovery_exceed_corruption**: R+1 frames corrupted → SQLITE_CORRUPT (graceful failure).
13. **test_recovery_mixed_intact_and_corrupted**: Some groups intact, some need repair. Verify per-group repair.

### §3.4.1 PRAGMA raptorq_repair_symbols (bd-1hi.12)

15. **test_pragma_set_higher**: Increase R → more repair symbols per group.
16. **test_pragma_set_lower**: Decrease R → fewer repair symbols, higher risk.
17. **test_pragma_zero_disables**: R=0 → no .wal-fec sidecar generated.
18. **test_pragma_takes_effect_next_group**: Changed PRAGMA takes effect for next WAL group, not current.

title: §5.7.1-5.7.2 SSI Witness Objects (ECS Schemas) + Hot/Cold Plane Discovery
description:
Define the canonical ECS schemas for all SSI witness objects and implement the two-stage candidate discovery mechanism (hot-plane + cold-plane refinement) that makes SSI cross-process safe (spec lines 8353-8509).

SCOPE: Covers all witness data structures (ReadWitness, WriteWitness, WitnessDelta, WitnessIndexSegment, DependencyEdge, CommitProof, AbortWitness) and the two-tier discovery system: O(1) hot-plane superset via SHM bitsets, optional cold-plane refinement via ECS object decode.

DATA STRUCTURES:
- KeySummary (6 variants): ExactKeys, HashedKeySet, PageBitmap (RoaringBitmap<u32>), CellBitmap (RoaringBitmap<u64>), ByteRangeList, Chunked. Soundness rule: MUST NOT have false negatives for coverage claim.
- ReadWitness: {txn, begin_seq, level, range_prefix, key_summary, emitted_at}
- WriteWitness: same as ReadWitness + write_kind (Intent | Final); Final required before commit validation
- WitnessDelta: {txn, begin_seq, kind, level, range_prefix, participation: Present (union-only CRDT), refinement}
- WitnessIndexSegment: {segment_id, level, range_prefix, readers/writers bitmaps, epochs, covered range}
- DependencyEdge: {kind: RWAntiDependency, from/to TxnToken, key_basis, observed_by, observation_seq}
- CommitProof: {txn, begin/commit_seq, has_in/out_rw, witness/edge/merge refs, abort_policy}; replayable proof for deterministic re-validation
- AbortWitness: {txn, begin_seq, abort_seq, reason, edges_observed}

ALGORITHMS:
- All ECS schemas follow normative encoding: little-endian integers, sorted maps/sets by canonical bytes, canonical roaring encoding for bitmaps
- Hot-plane candidate discovery (Stage 1): HotWitnessIndex bitsets in SHM provide O(1) superset of candidates; query both live epochs (cur and prev) and OR them; map slots to TxnToken; validate txn_epoch matches
- Cold-plane refinement (Stage 2, optional): decode ReadWitness/WriteWitness refinements to confirm actual key intersection and reduce false positives
- No False Negatives theorem (hot plane, active txns): active txn R registering read WitnessKey K is always discoverable because registration updates every configured level bucket, epoch advancement constrains witness_epoch to {cur, cur-1}, and stale bits filtered by (txn_id, txn_epoch) validation
- Scope limitation: hot plane only covers TxnSlot-holding txns; committed readers covered by RecentlyCommittedReadersIndex (section 5.6.2.1)

INVARIANTS:
- ECS encoding MUST be deterministic: same inputs produce identical bytes
- WitnessDelta participation is union-only CRDT (no removals)
- CommitProof contains enough evidence to replay SSI validation
- Hot-plane has no false negatives for active transactions

TEST REQUIREMENTS (9 unit + 1 E2E):
- test_key_summary_canonical_encoding (round-trip all variants), test_read_witness_ecs_deterministic, test_write_witness_kinds (Intent vs Final), test_witness_delta_crdt_merge, test_dependency_edge_canonical, test_commit_proof_replay, test_hot_plane_no_false_negatives, test_hot_plane_epoch_overlap, test_cold_plane_refinement_reduces_fp
- E2E: concurrent write workload verifying CommitProof replayability, write-skew detection, and RaptorQ encode/decode round-trip

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. All witness ECS schemas round-trip deterministically
2. Hot-plane discovery has zero false negatives for active transactions
3. Cold-plane refinement reduces false positives without introducing false negatives
4. CommitProof artifacts sufficient for deterministic re-validation
5. WitnessDelta union-only CRDT semantics preserved
6. Witness objects survive RaptorQ encode/decode

## §5.7.1-5.7.2 SSI Witness Objects (Canonical ECS Schemas) + Hot/Cold Plane Discovery

### What This Implements
The canonical data structures for SSI (Serializable Snapshot Isolation) evidence tracking, plus the two-tier discovery mechanism that makes SSI cross-process safe.

### Spec Content (Lines 8353-8509)

**§5.7.1 Witness Objects — Canonical ECS Schemas (normative):**
All witness structures follow ECS encoding rules:
- integer endianness: little-endian
- maps/sets: sorted by canonical byte representation
- bitmaps: canonical roaring encoding

**Core Types:**
- `KeySummary`: union type — ExactKeys | HashedKeySet | PageBitmap | CellBitmap | ByteRangeList | Chunked
- `ReadWitness`: {txn, begin_seq, level, range_prefix, key_summary, emitted_at}
- `WriteWitness`: {txn, begin_seq, level, range_prefix, key_summary, emitted_at, write_kind: Intent|Final}
- `WitnessDelta`: {txn, begin_seq, kind: Read|Write, level, range_prefix, participation: Present, refinement}
- `WitnessIndexSegment`: {segment_id, level, range_prefix, readers bitmap, writers bitmap, epochs, covered range}
- `DependencyEdge`: {kind: RWAntiDependency, from, to, key_basis, observed_by, observation_seq}
- `CommitProof`: {txn, begin/commit seq, has_in/out_rw, witness refs, edge refs, merge witnesses, abort_policy}
- `AbortWitness`: {txn, begin_seq, abort_seq, reason: SSIPivot|Cancelled|Other, edges_observed}
- `MergeWitness`: (specified in §5.10)

**Soundness rule:** KeySummary MUST NOT have false negatives for its coverage claim. False positives allowed.
**CommitProof meaning:** Replayable proof (not cryptographic) — enough evidence to deterministically re-run SSI validation.

**§5.7.2 Two-Stage Candidate Discovery:**
1. **Hot-plane (O(1)):** SHM HotWitnessIndex bitsets provide superset of candidates
   - Query both live epochs (cur and prev) and OR them
   - Map slots to TxnToken, validate txn_epoch matches
2. **Cold-plane refinement (optional):** Decode ReadWitness/WriteWitness refinements to confirm actual key intersection

**Theorem (No False Negatives, hot plane — active txns only):**
Active txn R registering read WitnessKey K is always discoverable at commit time because:
- Registration updates every configured level bucket
- Epoch advancement constrains witness_epoch ∈ {cur, cur-1}
- Stale bits filtered by (txn_id, txn_epoch) validation

**Scope limitation:** Only covers TxnSlot-holding txns. Committed readers → RecentlyCommittedReadersIndex (§5.6.2.1).

### Unit Tests Required
1. test_key_summary_canonical_encoding: Round-trip each KeySummary variant
2. test_read_witness_ecs_deterministic: Same inputs produce identical ECS bytes
3. test_write_witness_kinds: Intent vs Final distinction
4. test_witness_delta_crdt_merge: Union-only participation semantics
5. test_dependency_edge_canonical: Edge encoding matches spec
6. test_commit_proof_replay: CommitProof contains enough to re-run SSI validation
7. test_hot_plane_no_false_negatives: Active reader always discoverable
8. test_hot_plane_epoch_overlap: Both cur and prev epochs queried
9. test_cold_plane_refinement_reduces_fp: Refinement eliminates spurious edges

### E2E Test
Run concurrent write workload. Verify:
- All CommitProofs are replayable (re-validation yields same decision)
- No false negatives in conflict detection (inject known write-skew, verify abort)
- Witness objects survive RaptorQ encode/decode round-trip

comments.text:
SECTION: §5.7.1 + §5.7.2 (spec lines ~8306-8509)

PURPOSE: Define canonical ECS witness object schemas and the two-stage candidate discovery algorithm.

## §5.7 SSI Algorithm Specification (Overview)
- SSI extends Snapshot Isolation to detect/prevent write skew anomaly
- Default isolation mode for BEGIN CONCURRENT (Layer 2)
- Built on RaptorQ-native witness plane (§5.6.4):
  - Cross-process safe, distributed-ready, self-healing, explainable

### Formal rw-antidependency Definition
- Edge R -rw-> W exists iff:
  1. R and W are CONCURRENT: neither committed before other's snapshot
     (W.commit_seq > R.begin_seq AND R.commit_seq > W.begin_seq)
     Note: snapshot-based concurrency, not wall-clock overlap
  2. Exists WitnessKey K: R read K, W wrote K with commit not visible to R's snapshot

### Witness Plane Integration Contract
- register_read(key: WitnessKey)
- register_write(key: WitnessKey)
- emit_witnesses() -> (read_witnesses, write_witnesses) -- publishes ECS objects + updates hot index

## §5.7.1 Witness Objects (Canonical ECS Schemas)
All are normative; deterministic encoding per ECS rules (§3.5):
- integer endianness: little-endian
- maps/sets: sorted by canonical byte representation
- bitmaps: canonical roaring encoding

### KeySummary (6 variants)
- ExactKeys(keys: Vec<WitnessKey>) -- sorted by canonical bytes
- HashedKeySet(hashes: Vec<KeyHash>) -- sorted ascending
- PageBitmap(pages: RoaringBitmap<u32>) -- page numbers
- CellBitmap(cells: RoaringBitmap<u64>) -- (page<<32) | cell_tag
- ByteRangeList(ranges: Vec<(u32, u16, u16)>) -- sorted
- Chunked(chunks: Vec<KeySummaryChunk>) -- for large sets
- Soundness rule: MUST NOT have false negatives for its coverage claim

### ReadWitness
- txn: TxnToken, begin_seq, level: u8, range_prefix: u32, key_summary: KeySummary, emitted_at: LogicalTime

### WriteWitness
- Same as ReadWitness plus write_kind: { Intent, Final }
- Final is required before commit validation

### WitnessDelta
- txn, begin_seq, kind: {Read, Write}, level, range_prefix
- participation: { Present } -- union-only CRDT (no removals)
- refinement: Option<KeySummary>

### WitnessIndexSegment
- segment_id, level, range_prefix, readers/writers: RoaringBitmap<u64>
- epochs: Option<EpochSnapshot>
- covered_begin_seq, covered_end_seq

### DependencyEdge
- kind: { RWAntiDependency }, from/to: TxnToken
- key_basis: { level, range_prefix, refinement }
- observed_by: TxnToken, observation_seq

### CommitProof
- txn, begin_seq, commit_seq, has_in_rw, has_out_rw
- read_witnesses, write_witnesses, index_segments_used, edges_emitted, merge_witnesses: Vec<ObjectId>
- abort_policy: { AbortPivot, AbortYoungest, Custom }
- Meaning: replayable proof (not cryptographic) -- enough evidence to re-run SSI validation

### AbortWitness
- txn, begin_seq, abort_seq, reason: { SSIPivot, Cancelled, Other }, edges_observed

### MergeWitness -- specified in §5.10

## §5.7.2 Candidate Discovery (Hot Plane) and Refinement (Cold Plane)
Two-stage approach:

### Stage 1: Hot-Plane Candidate Discovery (shared memory)
- HotWitnessIndex bitsets provide superset of candidates in O(1) per bucket
- For incoming edges (R -rw-> T): query reader bitsets for BOTH live epochs (cur and prev), OR them, intersect with active_slots_bitset, map to TxnToken via TxnSlotTable
- For outgoing edges (T -rw-> W): symmetric using writers_for_epoch union

### Stage 2: Cold-Plane Refinement (optional)
- Decode ReadWitness/WriteWitness refinements or WitnessIndexSegments
- Confirm actual key intersection to reduce false positives

### No False Negatives Theorem (hot plane, active transactions only)
- If R is ACTIVE (holds TxnSlot) and registers read K, R is discoverable as reader candidate
- Epoch advancement ensures active txns have witness_epoch in {cur, cur-1}
- Stale bits filtered by (txn_id, txn_epoch) validation
- Scope limitation: once R commits and frees slot, hot-plane evidence becomes stale
  -> RecentlyCommittedReadersIndex (§5.6.2.1) provides coverage for committed readers

### Commit
235fc95 — `feat(fsqlite-mvcc): SSI witness objects + hot/cold plane discovery (bd-1if1)`

### Implementation Summary

**§5.7.1 Canonical ECS Schemas (witness_objects.rs, ~840 lines):**
- `KeySummary` enum (6 variants: ExactKeys, HashedKeySet, PageBitmap, CellBitmap, ByteRangeList, Chunked) with `may_overlap()` no-false-negatives guarantee
- `EcsReadWitness` / `EcsWriteWitness`: Full ECS-level read/write witness types with txn, begin_seq, level, range_prefix, key_summary, emitted_at, write_kind
- `WitnessDelta`: CRDT union-only merge semantics (participation can only become Present, refinement merged by precision)
- `EcsDependencyEdge`: R→W anti-dependency edges with observer tracking
- `EcsCommitProof`: Replayable SSI validation proof with refs to all witness/edge objects + abort policy

description:
SECTION 10 — QUERY PIPELINE (~530 lines)

The SQL processing pipeline from text to execution.

SUBSECTIONS: §10.1 Lexer Detail, §10.2 Parser Detail (hand-written recursive descent + Pratt expression parsing), §10.3 AST Node Types, §10.4 Name Resolution, §10.5 Query Planning, §10.6 Code Generation, §10.7 VDBE Instruction Format, §10.8 Coroutines.
CRATES: fsqlite-parser, fsqlite-ast, fsqlite-planner, fsqlite-vdbe.

## UNIT TEST REQUIREMENTS
- test_lexer_string_literal_escaping: Verify lexer handles embedded single quotes (doubled: 'it''s') and emits the correct token span
- test_lexer_blob_literal_odd_hex: Verify lexer emits Error token for blob literals with odd number of hex digits (X'ABC')
- test_parser_pratt_precedence_eq_vs_lt: Verify `a = b < c` parses as `a = (b < c)` (equality lower precedence than comparison, per §10.2 table)
- test_parser_escape_not_infix: Verify ESCAPE is parsed as part of LIKE/GLOB handler, not as a standalone infix operator
- test_name_resolution_ambiguous_column: Verify ambiguous column reference across multiple FROM tables produces a clear error with source span
- test_planner_covering_index_cost: Verify the planner selects a covering index scan (no table lookup) when all needed columns are in the index
- test_codegen_select_rowid_lookup: Verify SELECT by rowid generates the expected VDBE opcode sequence (OpenRead, SeekRowid, Column, ResultRow)
- test_coroutine_yield_swap: Verify InitCoroutine/Yield/EndCoroutine opcodes correctly swap program counters for CTE evaluation

## E2E TEST
test_e2e_query_pipeline_complex.rs: Execute a complex query with CTEs, window functions, and subqueries against a populated database; verify the pipeline (lex -> parse -> resolve -> plan -> codegen -> execute) produces correct results matching C sqlite3 output.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- [ ] Lexer handles all token types from §10.1 including string/number/blob literals, all ~150 keywords, and operator tokens
- [ ] Parser uses Pratt precedence with all 11 operator levels matching §10.2 exactly (including NOT lower than comparisons)
- [ ] Name resolution handles table aliases, star expansion, and correlated subquery scoping per §10.4
- [ ] Query planner uses beam search join ordering with mxChoice matching C SQLite's computeMxChoice per §10.5
- [ ] VDBE instruction format matches §10.7 (Opcode, p1-p3 as i32, p4 as tagged enum, p5 as u16)

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Query pipeline is complete end-to-end for the specified SQL subset: SQL text -> parser -> AST -> planner -> VDBE bytecode -> execution.
- [ ] Core correctness is proven by unit/property tests and at least one end-to-end harness suite (with EXPLAIN dumps on failures).
- [ ] Logging/tracing exists for opcode-level debugging in tests (env-gated) and produces structured output.
- [ ] Spec coverage audit complete for the embedded §10 extract.
