title: §16 Phase 6: MVCC Concurrent Writers with SSI
description:
## §16 Phase 6: MVCC Concurrent Writers with SSI

### Deliverables
- `crates/fsqlite-mvcc/src/txn.rs`: Transaction type with TxnId, Snapshot, TxnEpoch, write_set, intent_log, page_locks, mode (Serialized/Concurrent), witness-key sets (read_keys/write_keys), SSI state (has_in_rw/has_out_rw)
- `crates/fsqlite-mvcc/src/snapshot.rs`: Snapshot capture (high = commit_seq at BEGIN, schema_epoch at BEGIN), visibility predicate (commit_seq <= snapshot.high)
- `crates/fsqlite-mvcc/src/version_chain.rs`: Page version chains, GF(256) delta encoding via RaptorQ (Section 3.4.4)
- `crates/fsqlite-mvcc/src/lock_table.rs`: Page-level writer exclusion:
  - ShmPageLockTable adapter over SharedPageLockTable in shared memory (§5.6.3) for multi-process Concurrent mode
  - InProcessPageLockTable (sharded HashMap, 64 shards) for unit tests and single-process simulations
- `crates/fsqlite-mvcc/src/witness_plane.rs`: SSI witness plane integration: witness-key registration (register_read/register_write), shared-memory HotWitnessIndex updates, cold-plane witness object emission (ReadWitness, WriteWitness, WitnessDelta) and index-segment compaction hooks
- `crates/fsqlite-mvcc/src/ssi.rs`: SSI validation on top of the witness plane (conservative pivot abort rule with optional refinement + merge), plus DependencyEdge / CommitProof / AbortWitness artifacts for explainability
- `crates/fsqlite-mvcc/src/conflict.rs`: First-committer-wins validation, merge policy ladder (Section 5.10): deterministic rebase via intent logs and structured page patch merge; explicit prohibition of raw byte-disjoint XOR merge for SQLite structured pages (§3.4.5)
- `crates/fsqlite-mvcc/src/gc.rs`: Garbage collection -- horizon computation (min active begin_seq), version chain trimming, witness-plane GC horizons and bucket epoch advance (§5.6.4.8), memory bound enforcement
- `crates/fsqlite-mvcc/src/coordinator.rs`: Write coordinator using asupersync two-phase MPSC channel, commit serialization for WAL append
- `crates/fsqlite-pager/src/cache.rs`: ARC cache with (PageNumber, CommitSeq) keys, MVCC-aware eviction constraints (pinned, dirty, superseded). Lives in fsqlite-pager (L2) because the MvccPager trait is defined there; CommitSeq is imported from fsqlite-types.
- `crates/fsqlite-pager/src/mvcc_pager.rs`: MvccPager trait definition; implementation in fsqlite-mvcc (L3) bridges B-tree layer to MVCC, Cx threading

### Crates Involved
- fsqlite-mvcc (txn, snapshot, version_chain, lock_table, witness_plane, ssi, conflict, gc, coordinator)
- fsqlite-pager (cache, mvcc_pager trait)
- fsqlite-types (CommitSeq import)

### LOC Estimate
~15,000 LOC

### Entry Criteria (Dependencies)
- Phase 5 complete (MVCC sits atop WAL and pager)

### Exit Criteria (Acceptance)
- Serialized mode: Exact C SQLite behavior -- single writer, SERIALIZABLE isolation, BEGIN IMMEDIATE blocks other writers
- Concurrent mode: Two transactions writing to different pages both commit successfully
- Concurrent mode: Two transactions writing to the same page with a non-mergeable conflict, second committer gets SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT
- Concurrent mode: 100 threads each insert 100 rows into separate rowid ranges, all 10,000 rows present after all commits
- Snapshot isolation: Long-running reader (started before writer) does not see writer's changes even after writer commits
- Snapshot isolation: Reader started after writer commits sees all changes
- Merge safety: SQLite structured pages MUST NOT be merged by raw byte-range XOR; include regression test for the B-tree lost-update counterexample (cell move/defrag vs update at old offset) that must abort or resolve semantically (never silent lost update)
- GC: Sustained write load of 1,000 transactions, memory usage bounded by O(active_transactions * pages_per_transaction), not O(total_transactions)
- GC: Version chain length never exceeds active transaction count + 1
- Version chain compression: Pages with small diffs (< 10% changed) use sparse XOR delta encoding, space savings > 80%
- SSI: Write skew pattern (two txns read overlapping data, write disjoint pages based on reads) -- at least one txn aborted under default mode
- SSI: PRAGMA fsqlite.serializable=OFF allows both to commit (SI mode)
- SSI: has_in_rw/has_out_rw flags correctly set for known rw-antidependency patterns
- Rebase merge: Two transactions insert distinct keys into same leaf page -- rebase succeeds, both commit
- Rebase merge: Two transactions update same key -- rebase fails, second committer aborts
- Roaring Bitmap: Visibility checks with 100 in-flight transactions have zero false positives (exact, not probabilistic)
- ARC cache: Sequential scan does not evict frequently-accessed index pages (ARC adaptation test)
- Lab runtime: All above tests run under deterministic scheduling with same results across 100 different seeds
- Mazurkiewicz traces: 3-transaction scenario (T1 writes page A, T2 writes page B, T3 writes both A and B) -- all 6 possible commit orderings verified for correct conflict detection
- E-process monitors: INV-1 through INV-7 monitored continuously during 100-thread stress test, zero violations
- Target: 2,000+ tests

### Risk Areas
This is the hardest phase. Specific risks:
- Snapshot capture must be atomic with respect to concurrent commits. A non-atomic snapshot can miss a commit, violating SI. Mitigation: hold a read lock on active_transactions during snapshot capture.
- GC must not reclaim versions needed by any active transaction. Mitigation: formal proof in Section 5.5, e-process monitoring at runtime.
- Merge ladder correctness (intent replay + structured patches) is subtle: a naive byte-range merge can silently lose writes on B-tree pages. Mitigation: explicit counterexample tests + proptest/DPOR asserting that any accepted merge is observationally equivalent to some serial ordering of the intent ops, and passes integrity_check post-commit.
- ARC cache interaction with MVCC versioning adds complexity to eviction decisions. Mitigation: start with simple LRU, upgrade to ARC once basic MVCC works.

### Test Requirements
1. test_mvcc_serialized_mode: Exact C SQLite behavior -- single writer, SERIALIZABLE, BEGIN IMMEDIATE blocks other writers
2. test_mvcc_concurrent_different_pages: Two transactions writing different pages both commit
3. test_mvcc_concurrent_same_page_conflict: Two transactions writing same page with non-mergeable conflict, second gets SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT
4. test_mvcc_100_threads_100_rows: 100 threads each insert 100 rows into separate rowid ranges, all 10,000 rows present
5. test_snapshot_isolation_long_reader: Long-running reader started before writer does not see writer's changes after commit
6. test_snapshot_isolation_new_reader: Reader started after writer commits sees all changes
7. test_merge_safety_no_xor: Regression test for B-tree lost-update counterexample (cell move/defrag vs update at old offset) -- must abort or resolve semantically, never silent lost update
8. test_gc_memory_bounded: Sustained 1,000 transactions, memory O(active_txns * pages_per_txn) not O(total_txns)
9. test_gc_version_chain_length: Version chain length never exceeds active transaction count + 1
10. test_version_chain_compression: Pages with <10% diff use sparse XOR delta, space savings >80%
11. test_ssi_write_skew_abort: Write skew pattern -- at least one txn aborted under default SSI mode
12. test_ssi_non_serializable_allows: PRAGMA fsqlite.serializable=OFF allows both to commit (SI mode)
13. test_ssi_rw_flags: has_in_rw/has_out_rw flags correctly set for known rw-antidependency patterns
14. test_rebase_merge_distinct_keys: Two transactions insert distinct keys into same leaf page -- rebase succeeds
15. test_rebase_merge_same_key_abort: Two transactions update same key -- rebase fails, second aborts
16. test_roaring_bitmap_visibility: Visibility checks with 100 in-flight transactions have zero false positives
17. test_arc_cache_scan_resistance: Sequential scan does not evict frequently-accessed index pages (ARC adaptation)
18. test_lab_deterministic_seeds: All MVCC tests run under deterministic scheduling, same results across 100 seeds
19. test_mazurkiewicz_3txn_6_orderings: 3-transaction scenario, all 6 commit orderings verified for correct conflict detection
20. test_eprocess_inv1_through_inv7: INV-1 through INV-7 monitored during 100-thread stress test, zero violations

- test_e2e_bd_bca_2_compliance: concrete E2E identifier for structure lint compliance.
End-to-end validation: Open a WAL-mode database, create tables, insert data across multiple concurrent transactions (some conflicting, some not). Verify: conflicting transactions correctly abort with SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT, non-conflicting transactions both commit, snapshot isolation holds for long-running readers, data is persistent across close/reopen. Run under Lab runtime with deterministic scheduling across 100 seeds. Verify Mazurkiewicz trace exploration for 3-transaction scenario covers all distinct orderings. Confirm e-process monitors (INV-1 through INV-7) report zero violations during 100-thread stress.

### Logging Requirements
- INFO: phase-level milestones (MVCC integration) with phase_substep and duration_ms.
- DEBUG: MVCC page-version publish: page, new_version, commit_seq, chain_len.
- WARN: checkpoint lag / GC pressure: gc_horizon, oldest_active_begin_seq, max_chain_len.
- ERROR: durability invariant violation (e.g., commit published without WAL durability).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Serialized mode matches legacy C SQLite behavior (single writer, SERIALIZABLE semantics, BEGIN IMMEDIATE blocks other writers).
- [ ] Concurrent mode supports multiple writers: disjoint-page writes both commit; same-page non-mergeable conflicts abort/return SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT deterministically.

title: §6.1-6.2 ARC Cache Rationale + MVCC-Aware Data Structures
description:
Implements §6.1-6.2 of the FrankenSQLite spec: ARC cache rationale and MVCC-aware data structures for the buffer pool.

SUMMARY: Establishes why ARC (Adaptive Replacement Cache, Megiddo & Modha FAST '03) replaces LRU for database workloads, and defines the MVCC-aware keying scheme where cache entries are indexed by (PageNumber, CommitSeq) instead of PageNumber alone. Covers core data structures (CacheKey, CachedPage, EntryRef, RecencyStore, GhostStore, ArcCache), implementation strategy (slab-allocated intrusive doubly-linked lists for exact ARC, or CAR clock buffers), and concurrency model (Mutex for ARC ops, AtomicU32 ref_count for lock-free read-side pinning).

KEY DATA STRUCTURES AND ALGORITHMS:
- CacheKey: {pgno: PageNumber, commit_seq: CommitSeq} — commit_seq=0 is on-disk baseline; uncommitted pages live in txn write_set, NOT in ARC
- CachedPage: {key, data: PageData, ref_count: AtomicU32, xxh3: Xxh3Hash, byte_size: usize, wal_frame: Option<u32>}
- ArcCache: {t1: RecencyStore, t2: RecencyStore, b1: GhostStore, b2: GhostStore, p: usize, capacity, total_bytes, max_bytes, index: HashMap<CacheKey, EntryRef>}
- RecencyStore<K,V>: T1/T2 lists with front/pop_front/push_back/move_to_back/rotate_front_to_back ops
- GhostStore<K>: B1/B2 metadata-only lists with contains/remove/push_back/pop_front ops
- Implementation: slab-allocated intrusive lists (exact ARC) or CAR clock buffers (Bansal & Modha FAST '04)

ARC ADVANTAGE PATTERNS: (1) Scan-then-point — scan enters T1 only, hot pages stay in T2; (2) Frequency skew (Zipfian) — frequent pages promoted to T2; (3) Loop patterns — ghost hits in B1 adjust p for partial hit rate. Patent US 6,996,676 expired Feb 2024.

NORMATIVE INVARIANTS:
- MUST NOT evict pinned pages (ref_count > 0)
- Eviction MUST NOT perform I/O (no WAL append, no durability I/O — pure memory operation)
- MUST prefer evicting superseded versions (newer committed version exists visible to all active snapshots)
- All ArcCache operations protected by Mutex; CachedPage.ref_count uses atomics for lock-free read-side
- Transaction-private (uncommitted) page images are NOT ARC cache entries

UNIT TEST REQUIREMENTS:
1. test_cache_key_mvcc_awareness: Different (pgno, commit_seq) pairs are different keys
2. test_arc_t1_t2_promotion: First access places in T1, second access promotes to T2
3. test_arc_ghost_hit_b1: B1 hit increases p (favor recency)
4. test_arc_ghost_hit_b2: B2 hit decreases p (favor frequency)
5. test_scan_resistance: Full-table scan does not evict hot working set from T2
6. test_pinned_page_not_evicted: ref_count > 0 prevents eviction
7. test_eviction_no_io: Eviction path performs zero I/O calls
8. test_superseded_version_preferred: Newer committed version causes old version to be evicted first
9. test_memory_accounting: total_bytes tracks correctly across inserts and evictions

E2E TEST: test_e2e_arc_mvcc_integration_smoke — run concurrent transactions reading/writing pages with ARC active; verify ARC never evicts pinned pages and liveness holds (no deadlock from all-pinned preferred list).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
- ARC data structures compile and pass all 9 unit tests
- MVCC keying correctly differentiates page versions by commit_seq
- Eviction respects all three normative constraints (no pinned eviction, no I/O, prefer superseded)
- Memory accounting tracks total_bytes accurately within 1% tolerance
- Concurrent pin/unpin transitions are race-free under stress test

comments.text:
## Merged from P2 bead bd-1lcf (§6.1-6.2 Why ARC + MVCC-Aware Data Structures)

## §6.1 Why ARC, Not LRU

LRU fails catastrophically for DB workloads: a single table scan evicts the entire working set. ARC (Adaptive Replacement Cache, Megiddo & Modha, FAST '03) auto-tunes between recency and frequency. The ARC paper proves 2c-entry directory always contains the c pages LRU(c) would retain. Competitive ratio for deterministic paging is k (cache size), not 2 — ARC's contribution is adaptive self-tuning.

**Patent note:** ARC patent (US 6,996,676 B2) expired Feb 2024 — implementation is legally safe.

**Three canonical advantage patterns:**
1. **Scan-then-point:** Scan touches every page once — enters T1 but never promotes to T2. Hot pages remain in T2 untouched. LRU evicts all hot pages.
2. **Frequency skew (Zipfian 10/90):** LRU can't distinguish 1-access vs 1000-access pages. ARC promotes frequent pages to T2, protecting from recency-only eviction.
3. **Loop patterns:** Working set slightly larger than cache — LRU gets 0% hit rate. ARC detects looping via B1 ghost hits, adjusts p for partial hit rate.

## §6.2 MVCC-Aware ARC Data Structures

Standard ARC keys on page number. Our variant keys on (PageNumber, CommitSeq) because multiple versions coexist.

**CacheKey:** `{ pgno: PageNumber, commit_seq: CommitSeq }` — commit_seq=0 is on-disk baseline. Transaction-private images are NOT ARC entries; they live in owning transaction's write_set.

**CachedPage:** `{ key: CacheKey, data: PageData, ref_count: AtomicU32, xxh3: Xxh3Hash, byte_size: usize, wal_frame: Option<u32> }`

**EntryRef:** Implementation-specific handle into T1/T2. Exact ARC: NodeIdx in slab. CAR: SlotIdx in clock buffer.

**RecencyStore<K,V>:** T1/T2. Ops: membership probe, front/pop_front/push_back/move_to_back/rotate_front_to_back.

**GhostStore<K>:** B1/B2 (metadata-only). Ops: contains/remove/push_back/pop_front.

**ArcCache:** t1/t2 (RecencyStore), b1/b2 (GhostStore), p (adaptive target T1 size), capacity, total_bytes, max_bytes, index (HashMap<CacheKey, EntryRef>).

**Implementation (Extreme Optimization):** DO NOT use LinkedHashMap. Prefer slab-allocated intrusive lists (exact ARC) or CAR clock buffers (Bansal & Modha FAST '04). CAR: sequential memory sweep, CPU prefetcher friendly, eliminates pointer churn. All ops protected by Mutex; ref_count is atomic for lock-free reads.

**Eviction Constraints (normative):**
1. Never evict pinned (ref_count > 0)
2. Eviction is pure memory — MUST NOT append to .wal, MUST NOT perform durability I/O
3. Prefer superseded versions (newer committed version exists, visible to all active snapshots)

comments.text:
## §5.10.6-5.10.8 MVCC History Compression + Intent Footprints/Commutativity + Merge Certificates

### Spec Content (Lines 10441-10613)

**§5.10.6 PageHistory Objects:**
Compressed version chains stored as ECS objects: newest = full image, older = patches (intent logs and/or XOR deltas). This enables bounded storage while maintaining full MVCC history for active snapshots.

**§5.10.7 Intent Footprints and Commutativity (Trace-Normalized Merge):**
Uses Mazurkiewicz trace theory (§4.4) to formalize when intent operations commute:
- Define independence relation I ⊆ IntentOp × IntentOp
- Two ops are independent iff they can be swapped without changing the outcome
- Trace equivalence: two intent logs are equivalent if they produce the same result under any reordering consistent with I
This provides a rigorous foundation for the merge safety ladder (§5.10.4).

**§5.10.8 Merge Certificates (Proof-Carrying Merge):**
Every successful merge produces a MergeWitness (ECS object) containing:
- The original intent logs from both transactions
- The independence relation used
- The merged page image
- A proof that the merge is equivalent to some serial execution
This makes merges auditable and replicable.

### Unit Tests Required
1. test_page_history_compression: Full image + patches correct
2. test_page_history_ecs_round_trip: PageHistory survives ECS encode/decode
3. test_intent_commutativity: All IntentOp pairs tested for independence
4. test_trace_equivalence: Equivalent traces produce same state
5. test_merge_certificate_generation: MergeWitness produced on successful merge
6. test_merge_certificate_replay: MergeWitness sufficient to re-derive merge

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
SECTION: §5.10.5 + §5.10.6 + §5.10.7 + §5.10.8 (spec lines ~10423-10612)

PURPOSE: Implement merge verification proofs, MVCC history compression, trace-normalized commutativity analysis, and merge certificates.

## §5.10.5 What Must Be Proven
Runnable proofs (proptest + DPOR), NOT prose:
- B-tree invariants hold after replay/merge: ordering, cell count bounds, free space, overflow chain
- Patch algebra: apply(p, merge(a,b)) == apply(apply(p,a), b) when mergeable; commutativity for commutative ops
- Determinism: identical (intent_log, base_snapshot) → identical outcome under LabRuntime across seeds
- UpdateExpression determinism: evaluate_rebase_expr(expr, row) deterministic for (expr, row) pair
- Expression safety: expr_is_rebase_safe correctly rejects all non-deterministic/side-effectful expressions

## §5.10.6 MVCC History Compression: PageHistory Objects
- Full page images per version is unacceptable long-term
- Strategy:
  - Newest committed version: full page image (fast reads)
  - Older versions: patches (intent logs and/or structured patches)
  - Hot pages: encode patch chains as ECS PageHistory objects → repairable + remotely fetchable
- This is how MVCC avoids eating memory under real write concurrency

## §5.10.7 Intent Footprints and Commutativity (Trace-Normalized Merge)

### Independence Relation on Intents (normative, trace-monoid formalization)
Two intent ops a, b are independent (a,b) ∈ I_intent iff:
- a.schema_epoch == b.schema_epoch, AND
- a.footprint.structural == NONE AND b.footprint.structural == NONE, AND
- Writes(a) ∩ Writes(b) = ∅, AND
- Writes(a) ∩ Reads(b) = ∅ AND Writes(b) ∩ Reads(a) = ∅

SAFE merges additional restriction:
- Reads(a) AND Reads(b) MUST both be empty
  - UpdateExpression implicit column reads in RebaseExpr (NOT in footprint.reads) → condition satisfied
  - Uniqueness checks re-validated during replay → NOT in footprint.reads

### UpdateExpression Commutativity Refinement
- Two UpdateExpressions on same (table, key) have overlapping Writes at SemanticKeyRef level
- Column-level override: independent iff columns_written(a) ∩ columns_written(b) = ∅
- If any column index overlaps → NOT independent (sub-row granularity conflict)

### Join-Update Exception (normative, REQUIRED for AUTOINCREMENT)
- Some overlapping column updates commute by algebra (not disjointness)
- V1 permits exactly one class: monotone join updates col = max(col, c) on INTEGER
- is_join_max_int_update(col_idx, expr) detects canonical forms:
  - MAX(ColumnRef(col_idx), Literal(Integer(c))) -- either argument order
- Two UpdateExpressions with overlapping ColumnIdx are independent if ALL overlapping columns satisfy is_join_max_int_update
- Deterministic normalization: multiple join-max updates → collapse to single with c = max(c_1, c_2, ...)
  - Justified: max is associative, commutative, idempotent on integers

### UpdateExpression + materialized Update/Delete on same key → NEVER independent

### Canonical Merge Order (normative)
- Sigma_intent: alphabet of intent ops identified by op_digest (Trunc128(BLAKE3('fsqlite:intent:v1' || bytes)))
- Foata normal form layering; within each layer sort by (btree_id, kind, key_digest, op_kind, op_digest)
- This exact order recorded in merge certificate (§5.10.8)

### Mergeable Intent Classes (normative, deliberately narrow)
- Insert/Delete/Update on table B-tree leaf pages for DISTINCT RowId keys (no overflow, no multi-page balance)
- UpdateExpression on table B-tree leaf pages (column-disjointness rule)
- IndexInsert/IndexDelete on index B-tree leaf pages for DISTINCT index keys (no overflow, no balance)
- Any op with structural \!= NONE → non-commutative → abort/retry only

### Key Identity Alignment (REQUIRED)
- StructuredPagePatch.cell_ops.cell_key_digest MUST use same domain-separated semantic key digest as SemanticKeyRef.key_digest
- Merge machinery MUST NOT treat physical offsets as identity

## §5.10.8 Merge Certificates (Proof-Carrying Merge)

### Requirement
- Any commit via merge path MUST produce verifiable MergeCertificate
- Native mode: attached to CommitProof (referenced by marker record)
- Compatibility mode: emitted to evidence ledger, MAY persist to sidecar

### MergeCertificate Schema (normative)
- merge_kind: { rebase, structured_patch, rebase+patch }
- base_commit_seq: u64, schema_epoch: u64
- pages: Vec<PageNumber>
- intent_op_digests: Vec<[u8;16]> -- ops involved
- footprint_digest: [u8;16] -- digest over all IntentFootprints
- normal_form: Vec<[u8;16]> -- op digests in canonical order used
- post_state: { page_hashes: Vec<(PageNumber, [u8;16])>, btree_invariant_hash: [u8;16] }
- verifier_version: u32

### Verification Algorithm (normative)
Given (base snapshot, intents, certificate):

title: §12.17 Time Travel Queries (Native Mode Extension: AS OF COMMIT)
description:
E2E Test:
- test_e2e_bd_cfj0_compliance: concrete E2E identifier for structure lint compliance.

## SUMMARY

Implements Time Travel Queries (S12.17), a FrankenSQLite Native Mode extension that enables reading historical database state via the immutable commit stream (capsules + markers). Syntax uses FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF with either a timestamp string (converted to commit sequence via binary search of marker space) or COMMITSEQ N (direct commit sequence reference). A synthetic read-only snapshot S is created with S.high = target_commit_seq and the query executes using normal MVCC resolution rules: resolve(P, S) returns the newest committed version with version.commit_seq <= S.high. Time travel is strictly read-only; INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL in a time-travel context MUST fail with SQLITE_ERROR. If retention policy has pruned the requested state, the query fails with 'history not retained'. With tiered storage, older capsules may be fetched on demand from remote storage under Cx budgets.

## KEY DATA STRUCTURES / ALGORITHMS

- **Commit Sequence Resolution**: For timestamp-based queries, binary-search commit sequence space using random-access marker reads (S3.5.4.1) to find greatest marker with marker.commit_time_unix_ns <= target_time_unix_ns.
- **Synthetic Read-Only Snapshot**: Create snapshot S with S.high = target_commit_seq. No write capability.
- **MVCC Resolution**: resolve(P, S) returns newest committed version with version.commit_seq <= S.high, using standard S3.6/S5 resolution rules.
- **Timestamp Parsing**: SQLite-compatible datetime rules (same inputs accepted by unixepoch()) converted to target_time_unix_ns.
- **Tiered Storage Fetch**: Older capsules/index segments in remote storage fetched on demand under Cx capability budgets with decode/repair as usual (S3.5.11).
- **Retention Policy Check**: Before executing time-travel query, verify requested commit sequence is within retention bounds.

## NORMATIVE INVARIANTS

1. FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF COMMITSEQ N MUST use exact commit sequence N.
2. FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF timestamp MUST convert to commit sequence via binary search of markers.
3. Time travel queries MUST be read-only; INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL in time-travel context MUST fail with SQLITE_ERROR.
4. Synthetic snapshot MUST use S.high = target_commit_seq for MVCC resolution.
5. resolve(P, S) MUST return newest committed version with version.commit_seq <= S.high.
6. Pruned historical state MUST fail with explicit 'history not retained' error.
7. Tiered storage fetches MUST respect Cx capability budgets.
8. Time-travel queries MUST see a consistent snapshot at the target commit.
9. Multiple tables in the same time-travel query MUST all resolve against the same target commit sequence.

## UNIT TEST REQUIREMENTS

1. test_time_travel_as_of_timestamp -- FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF datetime returns data at that point in time
2. test_time_travel_as_of_commitseq -- FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF COMMITSEQ N uses exact commit sequence
3. test_time_travel_timestamp_to_commitseq_resolution -- Timestamp converted to correct commit sequence via binary search
4. test_time_travel_read_only -- INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE in time-travel context fails with SQLITE_ERROR
5. test_time_travel_ddl_blocked -- DDL in time-travel context fails with SQLITE_ERROR
6. test_time_travel_snapshot_isolation -- Time-travel query sees consistent snapshot at target commit
7. test_time_travel_mvcc_resolution -- resolve(P, S) returns newest committed version with commit_seq <= S.high
8. test_time_travel_pruned_history -- Request for pruned history fails with 'history not retained' error
9. test_time_travel_tiered_storage_fetch -- Older capsules in remote storage are fetched on demand
10. test_time_travel_cx_budget_enforcement -- Remote fetches respect Cx capability budget
11. test_time_travel_multiple_commits -- Query at different commit points returns correct historical state
12. test_time_travel_table_before_creation -- Querying a table before it was created fails gracefully
13. test_time_travel_with_joins -- Time-travel queries work correctly with joins across tables

Verify that DML/DDL in time-travel context is rejected. Test that pruned history returns the correct error. This is a FrankenSQLite-only test (no C sqlite3 comparison since this is a native mode extension).

## §12.17 Time Travel Queries (Native Mode: AS OF COMMIT)

### Spec Content (Lines 14717-14761)

Native mode persists an immutable commit stream (capsules + markers). This enables time travel queries that evaluate reads against a historical commit sequence.

**Syntax (extension):**
```sql
SELECT ... FROM my_table FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF '2023-10-27 10:00:00';
SELECT ... FROM my_table FOR SYSTEM_TIME AS OF COMMITSEQ 1234567;
```

**Semantics (normative):**
1. Determine target_commit_seq:
   - If `AS OF COMMITSEQ N`, then `target_commit_seq := N`.
   - Otherwise parse the time-string using SQLite-compatible datetime rules (same inputs accepted by unixepoch(...)) and convert to target_time_unix_ns. Binary-search commit sequence space using random-access marker reads (§3.5.4.1) for greatest marker with `marker.commit_time_unix_ns <= target_time_unix_ns`, set `target_commit_seq := marker.commit_seq`.
2. Create a synthetic read-only snapshot S with `S.high = target_commit_seq`.
3. Execute query using normal MVCC resolution rules: `resolve(P, S)` returns newest committed version with `version.commit_seq <= S.high` (§3.6, §5).

**Restrictions (V1):**
- Time travel is read-only. Any attempt to execute INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL in a time-travel context MUST fail with SQLITE_ERROR (or more specific SQLite-compatible error code).

**Retention and tiered storage:**
- If retention policy has pruned the requested historical state, time travel MUST fail with explicit error "history not retained".

title: §12.10 BEGIN CONCURRENT + Cross-Database Two-Phase Commit
description:
E2E Test:
- test_e2e_bd_d2m7_compliance: concrete E2E identifier for structure lint compliance.

## SUMMARY

Implements the BEGIN CONCURRENT transaction mode (S12.10) and cross-database two-phase commit (S12.11) as FrankenSQLite extensions. BEGIN CONCURRENT enters MVCC concurrent writer mode with Snapshot Isolation where multiple transactions can write simultaneously to different pages. Page-level conflict detection uses first-committer-wins: if two CONCURRENT transactions modify the same page, the second committer gets SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT. Cross-database atomic WAL transactions use a two-phase commit protocol across attached database WAL files, overcoming standard SQLite's limitation of WAL-mode atomicity only within a single database. The 2PC protocol uses a global commit marker, with crash recovery semantics ensuring either all databases commit or none do.

## KEY DATA STRUCTURES / ALGORITHMS

- **MVCC Snapshot**: On BEGIN CONCURRENT, a read snapshot is established. No global write mutex is acquired; page locks replace it.
- **Page-Level Conflict Detection**: At commit time, check if any page in the write set was modified by another committed transaction since the snapshot was taken. Conflict returns SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT.
- **First-Committer-Wins Rule**: The transaction that commits first succeeds. Conflicting transactions must retry.
- **Two-Phase Commit Protocol**: Phase 1 (Prepare): Write WAL frames to all involved databases, fsync, but do not update WAL-index. Phase 2 (Commit): Write global commit marker, then update each database's WAL-index to make frames visible.
- **Global Commit Marker**: Records participating databases and prepare state in the primary WAL or dedicated coordinator file.
- **Crash Recovery**: Before Phase 1 complete: no effect. After Phase 1 but before Phase 2 marker: roll forward on recovery. During Phase 2: complete remaining WAL-index updates on recovery. Phase 1 failure on any DB: roll back all.
- **Savepoint Integration**: Savepoints within CONCURRENT transactions work normally; ROLLBACK TO reverts to savepoint but keeps CONCURRENT snapshot active.

## NORMATIVE INVARIANTS

1. BEGIN CONCURRENT MUST establish a snapshot and enter MVCC concurrent writer mode without acquiring global write mutex.
2. Multiple concurrent writers MUST be able to hold active transactions simultaneously.
3. Page-level conflict detection: same-page modification by two CONCURRENT transactions MUST result in SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT for the second committer.
4. First-committer-wins: the transaction that commits first succeeds.
5. SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT MUST be distinguishable from SQLITE_BUSY for application retry logic.
6. Cross-database WAL transactions MUST be atomic via two-phase commit.
7. Phase 1 MUST write WAL frames to all databases and fsync before Phase 2.
8. Phase 2 MUST make all frames visible atomically via WAL-index updates.
9. Crash after Phase 1 (all prepared) but before Phase 2 marker MUST roll forward on recovery.
10. Failure during Phase 1 on any database MUST roll back all databases.
11. 2PC MUST handle up to 12 total databases (main + temp + 10 attached via SQLITE_MAX_ATTACHED).
12. Savepoints within CONCURRENT transactions MUST preserve the CONCURRENT snapshot on ROLLBACK TO.
13. Cannot DETACH a database with active transactions.

## UNIT TEST REQUIREMENTS

1. test_begin_concurrent_multiple_writers -- Two connections both BEGIN CONCURRENT; insert into different pages; both commit successfully
2. test_begin_concurrent_page_conflict_busy_snapshot -- Two connections same snapshot; one commits page X; other updates same page X and gets SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT
3. test_begin_concurrent_first_committer_wins -- Three concurrent txns: T1 writes page 5, T2 writes page 5, T3 writes page 10; T2 commits first (ok), T1 gets BUSY_SNAPSHOT, T3 succeeds
4. test_cross_database_two_phase_commit -- ATTACH two databases; INSERT into both; COMMIT; verify both visible; simulate crash after Phase 1 and verify atomicity
5. test_savepoint_within_concurrent -- BEGIN CONCURRENT; INSERT A; SAVEPOINT sp1; INSERT B; ROLLBACK TO sp1; INSERT C; COMMIT; verify A and C visible, B not
6. test_attach_detach_limit -- Attach 10 databases (max); 11th fails; detach one; attach succeeds
7. test_cross_db_2pc_both_committed -- ATTACH aux DB, INSERT into both, COMMIT; verify both show inserts
8. test_cross_db_2pc_crash_after_prepare -- Simulate crash after Phase 1; on recovery, transaction fully committed or fully rolled back
9. test_cross_db_2pc_one_db_fails_prepare -- Simulate disk-full on one DB during prepare; all DBs rolled back
10. test_cross_db_2pc_crash_during_phase2 -- Simulate crash during WAL-index updates; on recovery, complete the commit
11. test_cross_db_2pc_max_attached -- Transaction spanning main + 10 attached databases commits atomically
12. test_cross_db_2pc_wal_mode_required -- Verify 2PC works in WAL mode

- test_e2e_bd_d2m7_compliance: concrete E2E identifier for structure lint compliance.

ATTACH a second database. Perform writes to both under BEGIN CONCURRENT. Inject a failure between prepare and commit phases. Verify: either both DBs reflect the transaction or neither does (atomic 2PC). Test multiple concurrent writers with page-level conflict detection. Verify SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT is returned on conflict. This is partially a FrankenSQLite-only test (CONCURRENT mode), with standard transaction features compared against C sqlite3.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

- All 12 unit tests pass.
- BEGIN CONCURRENT allows multiple simultaneous writers without global write mutex.
- Page-level conflict detection correctly identifies same-page conflicts and returns SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT.
- Cross-database 2PC ensures atomicity across all attached WAL databases.
- Crash recovery correctly handles all failure points (before Phase 1, between phases, during Phase 2).
- Savepoints within CONCURRENT transactions preserve snapshot correctly.
- SQLITE_MAX_ATTACHED limit of 10 is enforced.

comments.text:
# §12.10 BEGIN CONCURRENT + Cross-Database Two-Phase Commit

## Scope

This bead covers the transaction control extensions specified in §12.10 and §12.11: the BEGIN CONCURRENT mode (MVCC concurrent writer entry point) and the requirement for cross-database atomic transactions via two-phase commit across attached WAL files.

## Spec References

- §12.10: "CONCURRENT: FrankenSQLite extension. Enters MVCC concurrent writer mode with Snapshot Isolation. Multiple CONCURRENT transactions can write simultaneously to different pages. Conflict on the same page results in SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT for the second committer."
- §12.10: Savepoints form a stack with RELEASE/ROLLBACK TO semantics
- §12.11: "Maximum 10 attached databases by default (SQLITE_MAX_ATTACHED)"
- §12.11: "Cross-database transactions are atomic only in rollback journal mode (not WAL mode in standard SQLite; FrankenSQLite MUST support cross-database atomic WAL transactions via two-phase commit across attached database WAL files)."
- §2.4 Layer 2: "BEGIN CONCURRENT: New non-standard syntax (matching SQLite's experimental BEGIN CONCURRENT branch). Uses page-level MVCC with SSI"
- §5.4: Global write mutex for Serialized mode; Concurrent mode uses page locks instead

## Requirements

### BEGIN CONCURRENT Mode
1. Parse and accept `BEGIN CONCURRENT [TRANSACTION]` syntax
2. On BEGIN CONCURRENT: establish a snapshot, enter MVCC concurrent writer mode (no global write mutex acquisition)
3. Multiple concurrent writers MUST be able to hold active transactions simultaneously
4. Page-level conflict detection: if two CONCURRENT transactions modify the same page, the second committer gets SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT
5. First-committer-wins rule: the transaction that commits first succeeds; the other must retry

### SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT Handling
6. When a CONCURRENT writer attempts to commit and finds a page conflict, return SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT (not SQLITE_BUSY)
7. The application-level retry loop can distinguish SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT from SQLITE_BUSY and decide whether to retry or abort

### Savepoint Interaction with CONCURRENT
8. Savepoints within a CONCURRENT transaction work normally (stack semantics)
9. ROLLBACK TO within CONCURRENT reverts to savepoint but keeps the CONCURRENT snapshot active
10. RELEASE within CONCURRENT commits savepoint work into the transaction's write set

### Cross-Database Two-Phase Commit
11. When a transaction spans multiple ATTACHed databases (all in WAL mode), COMMIT MUST be atomic across all databases
12. Implement two-phase commit protocol: Phase 1 (prepare) writes WAL frames to all involved databases; Phase 2 (commit) makes all visible atomically
13. If any database fails during Phase 1, roll back all databases
14. SQLITE_MAX_ATTACHED = 10: maximum number of attached databases (configurable)

### ATTACH/DETACH Constraints
15. ATTACH adds a new schema namespace; DETACH removes it
16. Cannot DETACH a database with active transactions
17. The main database is always named "main", temp is always "temp"

## Unit Test Specifications

### Test 1: `test_begin_concurrent_multiple_writers`
Open two connections. Both execute BEGIN CONCURRENT. Conn1 inserts into table A (page X). Conn2 inserts into table B (page Y, different page). Both COMMIT successfully -- no conflict because different pages.

### Test 2: `test_begin_concurrent_page_conflict_busy_snapshot`
Open two connections. Both execute BEGIN CONCURRENT with the same snapshot. Conn1 updates row on page X, commits. Conn2 updates different row on same page X, attempts commit. Verify Conn2 gets SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT.

### Test 3: `test_begin_concurrent_first_committer_wins`
Three concurrent transactions all reading the same snapshot. T1 writes page 5, T2 writes page 5, T3 writes page 10. T2 commits first (succeeds). T1 commits second (SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT on page 5). T3 commits third (succeeds, no conflict on page 10).

### Test 4: `test_cross_database_two_phase_commit`
ATTACH two databases. Begin transaction. INSERT into main.t1 and aux.t2. COMMIT. Verify both inserts are visible. Then begin another transaction, INSERT into both, simulate crash after Phase 1 prepare on main but before Phase 2 on aux. On recovery, verify either both or neither are committed (atomicity).

### Test 5: `test_savepoint_within_concurrent`
BEGIN CONCURRENT. INSERT row A. SAVEPOINT sp1. INSERT row B. ROLLBACK TO sp1. INSERT row C. COMMIT. Verify rows A and C are visible but B is not.

### Test 6: `test_attach_detach_limit`
Attach 10 databases (the maximum). Attempt to attach an 11th. Verify it fails with appropriate error. Detach one, then attach succeeds.

## Missing Detail (Audit Fix): Cross-Database Two-Phase Commit Protocol Detail

### Problem
The bead covers the high-level requirement for cross-database 2PC but lacks the protocol mechanics -- the specific phases, failure modes, and how this differs from standard SQLite.

### Spec Content (§12.11 lines 14617-14623 + §18 WAL Multiplexing lines 17847-17851)

**Standard SQLite limitation:** Cross-database transactions are atomic ONLY in rollback journal mode in standard SQLite. In WAL mode, standard SQLite does NOT guarantee atomicity across attached databases -- each database has its own WAL file, and a crash between writing one WAL and the other leaves databases inconsistent.

**FrankenSQLite requirement (normative):** FrankenSQLite MUST support cross-database atomic WAL transactions via two-phase commit across attached database WAL files.

**Two-Phase Commit Protocol for Cross-Database WAL Transactions:**

**Phase 1 -- Prepare:**
1. For each attached database touched by the transaction, prepare WAL frames (dirty pages serialized into WAL frame format)
2. Write WAL frames to each database's WAL file BUT do not update the WAL-index to make them visible
3. Ensure all frames are fsynced to stable storage
4. A global commit marker (in the primary WAL or a dedicated coordinator file) records which databases are participating and their prepare state

**Phase 2 -- Commit (make visible):**
1. Write the global commit marker indicating all databases are prepared
2. Update each database's WAL-index to make the new frames visible to readers
3. If all WAL-index updates succeed, the transaction is committed

**Crash Recovery Semantics:**
- Crash before Phase 1 completes: No WAL frames visible, no effect (automatic rollback)
- Crash after Phase 1 (all prepared) but before Phase 2 marker: On recovery, roll forward -- the prepared frames exist in all WAL files; write the commit marker and complete Phase 2
- Crash during Phase 2 (partial visibility): On recovery, detect the commit marker and complete any remaining WAL-index updates
- If any database fails during Phase 1 (e.g., disk full on one WAL): Roll back all databases -- discard uncommitted WAL frames from all involved databases

**WAL Multiplexing interaction (§18):** When WAL multiplexing is enabled (WAL frames sharded across multiple files), commit requires atomic append to all WAL files touched by the transaction. 2PC across WAL files uses a global commit marker in the primary WAL. Crash recovery replays prepared-but-uncommitted entries using this global commit marker.

**Constraint:** Maximum 10 attached databases by default (`SQLITE_MAX_ATTACHED`). The 2PC protocol must handle up to 12 total databases (main + temp + 10 attached).

## Test Requirements
- test_cross_db_2pc_both_committed: ATTACH aux DB, INSERT into both, COMMIT; verify both databases show the inserts
- test_cross_db_2pc_crash_after_prepare: Simulate crash after Phase 1 prepare on all databases; on recovery, transaction either fully committed or fully rolled back
- test_cross_db_2pc_one_db_fails_prepare: Simulate disk-full on one database during prepare; all databases rolled back
- test_cross_db_2pc_crash_during_phase2: Simulate crash during WAL-index updates; on recovery, complete the commit
- test_cross_db_2pc_max_attached: Transaction spanning main + 10 attached databases commits atomically
- test_cross_db_2pc_wal_mode_required: Verify 2PC works in WAL mode (not just rollback journal mode)

title: MemoryVfs: remove SQLite-style lock escalation (no serialized writers)
description:
## Problem

`crates/fsqlite-vfs/src/memory.rs` implemented SQLite-style file lock escalation (Shared -> Reserved -> Pending -> Exclusive) and returned Busy based on other handles.

That reintroduces file-level writer serialization, which violates FrankenSQLite's core design: concurrent writers are coordinated via MVCC at the page level, not by SQLite's file-lock protocol. In this project, MemoryVfs file locking should be a minimal stub.

## Fix

- Make `MemoryFile::lock` / `MemoryFile::unlock` minimal stubs (local bookkeeping only; no cross-handle coordination; never Busy).
- Make `check_reserved_lock` always return false for MemoryVfs.
- Update/replace any tests that assumed SQLite-style contention.

## Done When

- MemoryVfs lock/unlock no longer blocks other writers at the file level.
- `cargo check --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo fmt --check` are green.

title: §1.3 Asupersync-Only Runtime Enforcement (No Tokio CI Gate)
description:
## SUMMARY

Establish CI-enforced verification that the FrankenSQLite workspace uses asupersync as its sole async runtime, with zero tokio/async-std/smol dependencies. Per spec §1.3: "No tokio. All async I/O uses asupersync exclusively." Asupersync provides the async runtime, RaptorQ codec, Cx capability contexts, structured concurrency (Scope + macros), lab runtime (deterministic scheduling, cancellation injection, chaos), oracles/e-process monitors, deadline monitoring, and trace/TLA export. This bead gates CI to reject any introduction of alternative async runtimes and verifies that all I/O-performing trait methods accept the `&Cx` capability parameter.

## KEY DATA STRUCTURES / ALGORITHMS

- **Cx (Capability Context)**: Asupersync's capability token (§9) threaded through all I/O-performing methods. Provides cancellation, deadline monitoring, and structured concurrency guarantees. Every VFS, pager, and MVCC trait method that performs I/O MUST accept `&Cx` as a parameter.
- **Lab Runtime**: `LabRuntime::new(seed)` — asupersync's deterministic test runtime providing reproducible scheduling, cancellation injection at await points, and chaos mode (random delays, fault injection). Used for all async tests in the workspace.
- **Dependency audit**: CI script (cargo-deny or custom) that parses `Cargo.lock` to detect direct or transitive dependencies on `tokio`, `async-std`, `smol`, or `futures-executor`. Any match fails the build with an actionable diagnostic.
- **Structured concurrency (Scope)**: Asupersync's `Scope` + macros ensure all spawned tasks are joined before the scope exits. Replaces tokio's unstructured `tokio::spawn`.

## NORMATIVE INVARIANTS

1. **INV-NO-TOKIO**: Zero workspace crates may depend on `tokio`, `async-std`, `smol`, or `futures-executor` as direct dependencies. Transitive dependencies from external crates MAY pull in tokio types but MUST NOT instantiate or use their runtime (§1.3).
2. **INV-CX-THREADING**: Every trait method that performs I/O (VFS, pager, MVCC, replication) MUST accept `&Cx` as a parameter (§9). Methods that do not perform I/O SHOULD NOT require `&Cx`.
3. **INV-LAB-DETERMINISM**: All async tests MUST be runnable under `LabRuntime` with a fixed seed, producing deterministic execution order. Non-deterministic scheduling is confined to production runtime only.
4. **INV-NO-TOKIO-MACROS**: Zero occurrences of `#[tokio::main]`, `#[tokio::test]`, `#[async_std::main]`, or equivalent macros in any workspace source file.

## UNIT TEST REQUIREMENTS

- **test_no_tokio_in_cargo_lock**: Parse `Cargo.lock` and assert that no entry has `name = "tokio"` (or `async-std`, `smol`, `futures-executor`) as a direct dependency of any workspace crate. If a transitive dep pulls tokio, verify it is behind a non-default feature gate not activated by any workspace crate.
- **test_no_tokio_macros_in_source**: Scan all `.rs` files in `crates/` for `#[tokio::main]`, `#[tokio::test]`, `#[async_std::main]`. Assert zero matches. Prevents accidental use of alternative runtime test harnesses.
- **test_cx_parameter_on_vfs_trait**: Compile-time verification (via trait bounds or a dedicated test that instantiates a mock VFS) that all VFS read/write/lock methods require `&Cx`. A missing `Cx` parameter must cause a compile error.
- **test_lab_runtime_deterministic**: Run a small async workload (3 tasks, 10 yields each) under `LabRuntime::new(42)` twice. Assert identical execution traces (task interleaving order). Confirms deterministic scheduling.
- **test_lab_cancellation_injection**: Run an async operation under LabRuntime with cancellation injection enabled. Assert the operation observes cancellation at an await point and returns a cancellation error (not a hang or panic).

## E2E TEST

- **test_e2e_no_tokio_dependency_gate**: Run the full dependency audit script as it would run in CI. Temporarily add a `tokio = "1"` dependency to a test crate's Cargo.toml, run the audit, and verify it fails with a clear diagnostic message identifying the offending crate and dependency chain. Then remove the temporary dependency and verify the audit passes.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

- [ ] CI script (cargo-deny rule or custom) rejects any direct tokio dependency in workspace crates, with clear error message showing the dependency chain
- [ ] All VFS, pager, and MVCC trait methods verified to accept `&Cx` parameter (compile-time enforcement)
- [ ] LabRuntime smoke test passes with deterministic seed (same seed => same execution order)
- [ ] Zero `#[tokio::main]` or `#[tokio::test]` macros anywhere in the workspace source
- [ ] Dependency audit runs in < 5 seconds and is integrated into the CI pipeline
close_reason: 6 CI gate tests: cargo metadata dep scan, macro source scan (runtime-assembled patterns to avoid self-detection), Cargo.lock scan, workspace Cargo.toml scan, VfsFile Cx parameter compile-time check, E2E summary. All pass, clippy clean, fmt clean.

title: §13.6 COLLATE Interaction: BINARY/NOCASE/RTRIM + Custom Collation Registration
description:
## SUMMARY
Implement SQLite collation interaction with built-in functions and support for custom collation registration. Three built-in collations must be provided: BINARY (memcmp byte comparison), NOCASE (ASCII case-insensitive comparison), and RTRIM (ignores trailing spaces before comparison). Functions affected by collation (min/max scalar and aggregate) must use SQLite's comparison rules respecting the active collation. Functions NOT affected by collation (instr, replace, LIKE, GLOB) implement their own byte/character and case-folding rules. Collation selection follows SQLite's precedence: explicit COLLATE clause > column schema collation > default BINARY. Custom collations are registered via the database connection API.

## KEY DATA STRUCTURES / ALGORITHMS
- Collation trait: fn compare(&self, a: &[u8], b: &[u8]) -> Ordering. Each collation is a named implementation of this trait.
- CollationRegistry: maps collation name (case-insensitive) -> Collation trait object. Pre-populated with BINARY, NOCASE, RTRIM.
- BINARY collation: delegates to memcmp (byte-by-byte comparison).
- NOCASE collation: case-insensitive for ASCII letters (A-Z folded to a-z), byte-level comparison otherwise. Does NOT handle Unicode case folding (that requires the ICU extension).
- RTRIM collation: strips trailing spaces (0x20) from both operands before BINARY comparison.
- Collation selection algorithm (when operands have different collations):
  1. Explicit COLLATE clause wins. If multiple explicit collations, leftmost wins.
  2. Column collation from schema (CREATE TABLE ... COLLATE NOCASE).
  3. Default: BINARY.
- Functions using collation: scalar min/max and aggregate min/max use the collation-aware comparison for determining minimum/maximum.
- Functions ignoring collation: instr, replace use byte/character matching; LIKE uses its own case-folding (case-insensitive for ASCII); GLOB uses its own case-sensitive matching.
- Custom collation registration API: db.create_collation("name", MyCollation::new()). Must be available before any query references the collation.

## NORMATIVE INVARIANTS
1. BINARY collation uses memcmp (byte-by-byte unsigned comparison).
2. NOCASE folds only ASCII A-Z to a-z; non-ASCII bytes are compared as-is.
3. RTRIM strips only space characters (0x20), not tabs or other whitespace.
4. Collation selection precedence: explicit COLLATE > schema COLLATE > BINARY default.
5. When multiple explicit COLLATE clauses conflict, the leftmost wins.
6. min/max (both scalar and aggregate) respect the active collation for comparisons.
7. instr, replace, LIKE, GLOB do NOT use collation; they have their own comparison rules.
8. LIKE is case-insensitive for ASCII by default (no collation involvement).
9. GLOB is always case-sensitive (no collation involvement).
10. Custom collations must be registered before use; referencing an unregistered collation is an error.
11. Collation names are case-insensitive (BINARY = binary = Binary).

## UNIT TEST REQUIREMENTS
1. test_binary_collation_basic: 'ABC' < 'abc' under BINARY (uppercase bytes are less)
2. test_binary_collation_memcmp: comparison is byte-by-byte, not character-aware
3. test_nocase_collation_equal: 'ABC' = 'abc' under NOCASE
4. test_nocase_collation_ascii_only: 'Ä' != 'ä' under NOCASE (non-ASCII not folded)
5. test_rtrim_collation_equal: 'hello' = 'hello   ' under RTRIM
6. test_rtrim_collation_tabs_not_stripped: 'hello\t' != 'hello' under RTRIM (only 0x20 stripped)
7. test_collation_selection_explicit: SELECT 'a' < 'B' COLLATE NOCASE uses NOCASE
8. test_collation_selection_leftmost: when two explicit COLLATE conflict, leftmost wins
9. test_collation_selection_schema: column defined with COLLATE NOCASE uses NOCASE by default
10. test_collation_selection_default: without any COLLATE, BINARY is used
11. test_min_respects_collation: min('ABC', 'abc') differs under BINARY vs NOCASE
12. test_max_respects_collation: max with NOCASE collation compares case-insensitively
13. test_aggregate_min_collation: SELECT min(col) with col COLLATE NOCASE
14. test_aggregate_max_collation: SELECT max(col) with col COLLATE NOCASE
15. test_instr_ignores_collation: instr always uses byte matching regardless of column collation
16. test_replace_ignores_collation: replace is byte-exact regardless of collation
17. test_like_ignores_collation: LIKE uses its own ASCII case-folding, not column collation
18. test_glob_ignores_collation: GLOB is always case-sensitive regardless of collation
19. test_order_by_collation: ORDER BY col COLLATE NOCASE sorts case-insensitively
20. test_group_by_collation: GROUP BY col COLLATE NOCASE groups 'ABC' and 'abc' together
21. test_distinct_collation: SELECT DISTINCT col COLLATE NOCASE deduplicates case-insensitively
22. test_custom_collation_registration: register a custom collation (e.g., reverse) and use it
23. test_custom_collation_in_order_by: ORDER BY with custom collation produces expected order
24. test_custom_collation_in_index: CREATE INDEX with custom collation works
25. test_unregistered_collation_error: referencing unregistered collation name raises error
26. test_collation_name_case_insensitive: COLLATE BINARY = COLLATE binary = COLLATE Binary

## E2E TEST
Create tables with columns using different collations (BINARY, NOCASE, RTRIM). Insert data with mixed case, trailing spaces, and Unicode characters. Test ORDER BY, GROUP BY, DISTINCT, min/max, comparisons (=, <, >, IN, BETWEEN) under each collation. Register a custom collation and verify it works in ORDER BY, WHERE, and INDEX creation. Verify that instr/replace/LIKE/GLOB ignore collation. Compare all results against C sqlite3.

## ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. BINARY, NOCASE, RTRIM collations are built-in and produce correct comparison results.
2. Collation selection precedence (explicit > schema > default BINARY) is correctly implemented.
3. min/max respect collation; instr/replace/LIKE/GLOB do not.
4. Custom collations can be registered and used in ORDER BY, WHERE, GROUP BY, DISTINCT, and indexes.
5. Collation names are case-insensitive.
6. Unregistered collation reference produces an error.
7. All results match C sqlite3. sqllogictest collation tests pass.

title: WASM 2.10: Bundler compatibility matrix — Vite, webpack, esbuild, Turbopack testing and documentation

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
# WASM 2.10: Bundler Compatibility Matrix — Vite, webpack, esbuild, Rollup, Turbopack

## Problem
WASM + Workers don't "just work" with all bundlers. Each bundler handles `new URL('./file.wasm', import.meta.url)`, Worker instantiation, and WASM imports differently. Users will hit confusing build errors if we don't test and document bundler-specific configuration.

## Known Bundler Issues
1. **Vite**: Works well with `?url` suffix for WASM, needs `optimizeDeps.exclude` for WASM packages
2. **webpack 5**: Needs `experiments.asyncWebAssembly = true`, Worker via `new Worker(new URL(...), { type: 'module' })`
3. **esbuild**: No native WASM support — needs explicit loader config
4. **Rollup**: Needs @rollup/plugin-wasm, Worker via separate entry point
5. **Turbopack (Next.js)**: Early WASM support, may need fallback to webpack

## Deliverables

### 1. Bundler Test Matrix (CI)
```
packages/tests-bundler/
├── vite/                    # Vite project using @frankensqlite/sdk
│   ├── vite.config.ts
│   ├── src/main.ts
│   └── test.spec.ts         # Playwright: verify app works
├── webpack/                 # webpack 5 project
│   ├── webpack.config.js
│   ├── src/index.ts
│   └── test.spec.ts
├── esbuild/                 # esbuild project
│   ├── build.mjs
│   ├── src/index.ts
│   └── test.spec.ts
├── turbopack/               # Next.js with Turbopack
│   ├── next.config.js
│   ├── app/page.tsx
│   └── test.spec.ts
└── playwright.config.ts     # Shared Playwright config
```

### 2. Documentation: Bundler Config Guide
For each bundler, document the minimum config needed:

```typescript
// Vite config
export default {
  optimizeDeps: { exclude: ['@frankensqlite/core'] },
  server: {
    headers: {
      'Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy': 'same-origin',
      'Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy': 'require-corp',
    },
  },
};

// webpack 5 config
module.exports = {
  experiments: { asyncWebAssembly: true },
  module: {
    rules: [{ test: /\.wasm$/, type: 'webassembly/async' }],
  },
  devServer: {
    headers: {
      'Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy': 'same-origin',
      'Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy': 'require-corp',
    },
  },
};
```

### 3. CI Job
```yaml
bundler-compat:
  strategy:
    matrix:
      bundler: [vite, webpack, esbuild, turbopack]
  steps:
    - name: Build and test with ${{ matrix.bundler }}
      run: |
        cd packages/tests-bundler/${{ matrix.bundler }}
        npm ci
        npm run build
        npx playwright test
```

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Vite, webpack 5, esbuild, Turbopack all build and run @frankensqlite/sdk
2. Each bundler project builds in CI
3. Playwright tests verify WASM loads and basic query works in each bundler's output
4. Documentation page for each bundler with copy-paste config
5. Known limitations documented (e.g., esbuild Worker limitations)

title: emit_expr ignores column refs in table-backed WHERE clauses (emits NULL)
close_reason: Fixed in commit c664162: ScanCtx threading through emit_expr for cursor-aware expression codegen. All WHERE clause column references now correctly emit Opcode::Column instead of Null.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## Bug: emit_expr ignores column references in table-backed WHERE clauses

**File:** `crates/fsqlite-vdbe/src/codegen.rs`, line 1624-1627

**Root cause:** `emit_expr()` does not handle `Expr::Column` — it falls through to the
catch-all arm which emits `Opcode::Null`. This means any WHERE clause expression
involving column references (other than the specially-handled `Eq` case in
`emit_where_filter`) evaluates columns as NULL, breaking:
- Comparison operators (>, <, >=, <=, !=)
- OR predicates
- IS NULL / IS NOT NULL
- LIKE patterns
- BETWEEN / IN operators
- Any compound predicate that isn't a simple `col = literal`

**Symptoms:**
- `SELECT a FROM t WHERE a > 2` returns 0 rows
- `SELECT a FROM t WHERE a = 1 OR a = 3` returns 0 rows
- `SELECT a FROM t WHERE b IS NULL` returns ALL rows (NULL IS NULL = true)
- `SELECT b FROM t WHERE b LIKE 't%'` returns 0 rows

**Fix:** Add cursor-aware expression emission. Either:
1. Add `emit_expr_with_cursor(b, expr, reg, cursor, table)` that handles
   `Expr::Column` by emitting `Opcode::Column(cursor, col_idx, reg)`, OR
2. Refactor `emit_where_filter` to thread cursor context through to `emit_expr`

The `emit_where_filter` fallback (line 1366-1372) correctly evaluates the expression
and tests truthiness with `IfNot` — the only issue is that `emit_expr` can't resolve
column references.

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## Resolution: bd-f6pn — emit_expr column reference fix verified

The core fix was already implemented in commit c664162 ("feat(vdbe): thread ScanCtx through emit_expr for cursor-aware expression codegen"):

1. ScanCtx struct carries cursor + table context through expression emission
2. emit_expr handles Expr::Column when ScanCtx is provided, emitting Opcode::Column
3. emit_where_filter catch-all creates ScanCtx and passes it for non-Eq/non-And WHERE predicates
4. emit_column_reads creates ScanCtx for non-column expressions in SELECT list
5. All helpers (emit_binary_op, emit_comparison, emit_is_comparison, emit_case_expr) propagate ctx

What I fixed: Updated outdated test test_codegen_select_non_column_expr_with_from_rejected to
test_codegen_select_non_column_expr_with_from_accepted since emit_column_reads now handles
non-column expressions via ScanCtx. Test verifies Add opcode is emitted for SELECT 1+2 FROM t.

Verification: 168 VDBE tests pass, 64 fsqlite lib tests pass, clippy+fmt clean.
All symptoms from the bug report are resolved.

title: EPIC: RaptorQ Self-Healing WAL (.wal-fec sidecar, compat mode)
description:
Implement the spec §3.4.1 self-healing WAL design.

Core requirement:
- Standard SQLite .wal frames remain untouched (compatibility).
- A sidecar .wal-fec stores group metadata + deterministic repair symbols.

Spec essentials (self-contained):
- Commit group = frames up to commit frame (db_size != 0).
- group_id := (wal_salt1, wal_salt2, end_frame_no).
- .wal-fec is append-only: WalFecGroupMeta record + R SymbolRecords for ESIs K..K+R-1.
- Recovery: validate surviving sources using per-source xxh3_128 hashes stored in WalFecGroupMeta, then decode if |sources|+|repairs|>=K.

Non-negotiable perf:
- Encoding MUST NOT happen in WAL write critical section (pipelined background job by default).

This epic is closed only when writer/reader/recovery/tests are implemented.
close_reason: All WAL-FEC sidecar implementation/dependency lanes are closed; self-healing WAL epic complete

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## Epic Notes: Self-Healing WAL (.wal-fec)

### Compatibility Thesis
- SQLite `.wal` stays byte-for-byte compatible.
- All fountain-code data lives in a sidecar `.wal-fec`.

### Data Model (Spec §3.4.1)
- We treat each commit group as a source block:
  - frames `[start_frame_no..end_frame_no]` where `end_frame_no` is a commit frame (`db_size != 0`).
- Group identity:
  - `group_id := (wal_salt1, wal_salt2, end_frame_no)`

### `.wal-fec` Append-Only Layout
For each commit group append:
1. `WalFecGroupMeta` (k/r/oti/page list + per-source hashes + checksum)
2. `R` repair SymbolRecords for ESIs `K..K+R-1` (deterministically generated)

### Recovery Algorithm (High Level)
1. Find relevant group meta records (by salts + end_frame_no).
2. Validate surviving systematic sources using meta’s per-source `xxh3_128(page_bytes)` hashes.
3. Treat invalid sources as erasures.
4. If `|valid_sources| + |valid_repairs| >= K_source`, decode.
5. If decode succeeds: reconstruct missing frames/pages and continue normal WAL recovery.
6. If decode fails: emit explicit diagnostic + (lab/debug) DecodeProof.

### Performance Non-Negotiable
Repair symbol generation must not sit on the WAL write critical section.
Default behavior is pipelined background generation.

### Dependencies
- Depends on overhead policy (`bd-26ge`) for choosing R.
- Uses asupersync codec via §4 integration (`bd-3go`).

### Acceptance
Closed only when:
- writer path produces `.wal-fec`
- recovery consumes it
- tests demonstrate success within budget and explainable failure beyond budget

title: WASM 6.1: SharedArrayBuffer page lock table for cross-Worker page-level locking

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
# Task 6.1: SharedArrayBuffer Page Lock Table

## What
Implement page-level locking across Workers using SharedArrayBuffer and Atomics. This is the core primitive that enables concurrent writers.

## Design
```
SharedArrayBuffer layout (per database):
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Header (64 bytes)                             │
│   [0..4]   magic: 0x46534C4B ("FSLK")       │
│   [4..8]   version: 1                        │
│   [8..16]  max_pages: u64                    │
│   [16..24] active_writers: atomic u64        │
│   [24..32] next_txn_id: atomic u64           │
│   [32..64] reserved                          │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Lock Table (8 bytes per page)                 │
│   [0..4]   lock_state: atomic u32            │
│             0 = free                          │
│             1..0x7FFF_FFFF = shared readers   │
│             0x8000_0000 = exclusive writer    │
│   [4..8]   owner_txn_id: atomic u32          │
├──────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Version Counters (8 bytes per page)           │
│   [0..4]   current_version: atomic u32       │
│   [4..8]   last_writer_txn: atomic u32       │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

## Atomics Usage
```rust
// In Rust (via wasm-bindgen Atomics)
fn try_lock_page_exclusive(page: u32) -> bool {
    let offset = HEADER_SIZE + page as usize * 8;
    let expected = 0u32; // Free
    let desired = 0x8000_0000u32; // Exclusive
    Atomics::compare_exchange(sab, offset, expected, desired) == expected
}

fn try_lock_page_shared(page: u32) -> bool {
    loop {
        let current = Atomics::load(sab, offset);
        if current & 0x8000_0000 != 0 { return false; } // Exclusive held
        let desired = current + 1;
        if Atomics::compare_exchange(sab, offset, current, desired) == current {
            return true;
        }
    }
}
```

## COOP/COEP Requirement
SharedArrayBuffer requires:
```
Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp
Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin
```
These headers must be set by the server. Task 6.5 handles the fallback when these are unavailable.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Correct CAS-based locking with Atomics
- No deadlocks (page locks acquired in page-number order)
- Shared reader count tracks correctly
- Exclusive writer blocks shared readers and other writers
- Lock table size scales to max_pages

comments.author: Dicklesworthstone
comments.text:
## TECHNICAL FEASIBILITY NOTES (audit, 2026-03-02)

### COOP/COEP Header Requirement is a MAJOR deployment constraint
SharedArrayBuffer requires these HTTP headers on the serving page:
```
Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp
Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin
```
This is NOT optional and has significant implications:
1. **CDNs**: Most CDN-served content (images, fonts, scripts) must serve `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: cross-origin` or be fetched with CORS
2. **Third-party scripts**: Google Analytics, Stripe, Intercom, etc. may break under COEP
3. **Iframe embeds**: Same-origin restrictions affect iframe communication
4. **Legacy browsers**: Safari added SAB support in 15.2 but with restrictions

### Atomics.waitAsync() vs Atomics.wait()
The bead shows `Atomics::compare_exchange` which is fine, but if we need to BLOCK waiting for a lock:
- `Atomics.wait()` is ONLY available in Workers (not main thread)
- `Atomics.waitAsync()` is available on main thread but returns a Promise
- Our architecture (Workers only) is correct for using `Atomics.wait()`

### Rust wasm-bindgen Atomics access
wasm-bindgen doesn't have direct SharedArrayBuffer Atomics bindings. We'd need:
1. **js-sys**: `js_sys::Atomics::*` functions
2. **wasm-bindgen raw**: Access via `wasm_bindgen::JsValue` + manual FFI
3. **Custom JS glue**: TypeScript helper functions imported via wasm-bindgen extern

Option 1 (js-sys) is preferred. Verify: `js_sys::Atomics::compare_exchange()`, `js_sys::Atomics::load()`, `js_sys::Atomics::store()` exist.

### SAB Size Calculation
With the proposed layout (header + 8B/page lock + 8B/page version):
- 1000 pages: 64 + 8000 + 8000 = ~16KB
- 10,000 pages: 64 + 80,000 + 80,000 = ~160KB
- 100,000 pages: ~1.6MB

This is reasonable. But the max_pages needs to be pre-allocated (SAB cannot be resized). Consider using a growable approach or a page-table-of-page-tables indirection.

title: Epic: The Bloodstream (Incremental View Maintenance via Differential Dataflow)
description:
**Goal:** Dissolve the query-polling boundary between the DB and the application by pushing algebraic deltas of materialized views directly to clients in O(Δ) time, guaranteeing exactly-once semantics.
**Background & Justification:** Currently, clients repeatedly poll the database for updated views, wasting massive CPU/IO. Shipping a differential delta (+1 or -1 row) is virtually free. By integrating Timely Dataflow concepts into `fsqlite-vdbe`, we compute view differentials at commit time.
**Constraints:** 
- Must preserve SSI isolation and exact `CommitSeq` serializability.
- Must not block the MVCC write coordinator.
- View updates must complete within the `group_commit` budget (<5ms).
**Primary failure risk + countermeasure:**
- Risk: Delta computation slows down write commit, or subscribers lose sync.
- Countermeasure: Budgeted mode. If differential graph execution exceeds 1ms, gracefully degrade to sending an invalidation signal (forcing a client re-poll). Subscribers must be able to gracefully recover via a new snapshot.
**Adoption wedge & Ergonomics:** 
- Opt-in via `PRAGMA fsqlite_differential_views = ON`. 
- New PRAGMA `fsqlite_differential_status` to see active subscriptions, emission rates, and fallback counts.
- **Snapshot + Stream Sync:** Clients subscribing to a view receive an atomic initial payload at `CommitSeq(N)`, and the stream guarantees deltas begin exactly at `N+1`.

title: Replace MemDatabase snapshots with MVCC version tokens
description:
## Goal

Replace any MemDatabase snapshot cloning with MVCC version tokens, so snapshot reads reference MVCC state without copying whole databases.

## Scope

- Snapshot identity represented as a lightweight version token
- Readers resolve visible page versions via MVCC using that token
- Remove clone-based snapshotting from the hot path
acceptance_criteria:
Acceptance Criteria

- Snapshot reads no longer require cloning the entire database state.
- Tests demonstrate: writer commits, reader on older token sees old state, new reader sees new state (no panics, deterministic behavior).
close_reason: MemDatabase snapshots already use lightweight MemDbVersionToken (undo-log index). Removed unused Clone impl, added #[must_use]. 177 VDBE + 685 core tests pass.

Audited the full MemDatabase snapshot chain:
- `Connection.snapshot()` (connection.rs:710) captures `MemDbVersionToken` (undo-log length)
- `Connection.restore_snapshot()` (connection.rs:719) calls `MemDatabase.rollback_to(token)`

- `Clone for MemDatabase` existed but was NEVER called in production code

### Changes
1. **Removed `Clone for MemDatabase`** (engine.rs:645-654) — prevents future accidental O(n) table cloning. The undo-log path (`MemDbVersionToken`) is the only correct snapshot mechanism.

3. **Added documentation** explaining the MVCC-style undo-log approach and referencing bd-g6eo.

- `DbSnapshot` stores lightweight `MemDbVersionToken` + schema vector
- `TransactionHandle.savepoint/rollback_to_savepoint` manages MVCC-layer savepoints

title: §9 Cx Parameter Enforcement + Sealed Trait Pattern Validation
description:
## SUMMARY
Cross-cutting enforcement bead for §9 (Trait Hierarchy):

1. **Cx Everywhere Rule:** any trait method that touches I/O, acquires locks, or could block MUST accept `&Cx` as its first parameter.
2. **Sealed Trait Pattern:** internal-only traits MUST be sealed to prevent downstream implementations that could violate MVCC safety invariants; user-extension traits MUST remain implementable.

This bead exists to make these rules mechanically checkable (tests + audits) so they cannot regress silently.

## Scope

### Cx Everywhere
- MUST take `&Cx`: VFS I/O, pager operations, cursor operations, checkpoint/writer I/O, coordinator IPC, and any other potentially-blocking path.
- MUST NOT take `&Cx`: pure computation only (example: `CollationFunction::compare`; CPU-only `ScalarFunction::call`).

### Sealed Traits
Open extension points (user-implementable; MUST NOT be sealed):
- `Vfs`, `VfsFile`
- `ScalarFunction`, `AggregateFunction`, `WindowFunction`
- `VirtualTable`, `VirtualTableCursor`
- `CollationFunction`, `Authorizer`

Internal-only (MUST be sealed):
- `MvccPager`
- `BtreeCursorOps`
- `CheckpointPageWriter`

### Test Mocks (Required)
The defining crate for each sealed trait MUST export test mocks usable cross-crate:
- `MockMvccPager`
- `MockBtreeCursor` (implements `BtreeCursorOps`)
- `MockCheckpointPageWriter`

## Unit Test Requirements

- `test_cx_param_audit_vfs_traits`: every I/O method on `Vfs`/`VfsFile` takes `&Cx`.
- `test_cx_param_audit_mvcc_pager_trait`: `begin/get_page/write_page/allocate_page/free_page/commit/rollback` all take `&Cx`.
- `test_cx_param_audit_btree_cursor_ops_trait`: all cursor ops take `&Cx`.
- `test_cx_param_audit_checkpoint_page_writer_trait`: `write_page/sync` take `&Cx`.
- `test_pure_compute_exclusion_collation_compare_no_cx`: `CollationFunction::compare` does not take `&Cx`.
- `test_pure_compute_exclusion_scalar_call_cpu_only_no_cx`: CPU-only `ScalarFunction::call` does not take `&Cx`.
- `test_sealed_mvcc_pager_compile_fail`: downstream impl attempt fails due to sealed trait.
- `test_sealed_btree_cursor_ops_compile_fail`: downstream impl attempt fails.
- `test_sealed_checkpoint_page_writer_compile_fail`: downstream impl attempt fails.
- `test_open_vfs_external_impl_compiles`: downstream crate/module can implement `Vfs`/`VfsFile` (compile-pass).
- `test_open_function_traits_external_impl_compiles`: downstream can implement `ScalarFunction`/`AggregateFunction`/`WindowFunction` (compile-pass).
- `test_mock_exports_available`: mocks are exported and usable from other crates' tests.

## E2E Test

- `test_e2e_bd_ggxs_cx_and_sealed_enforcement_workspace_pass`:
  - Run the signature audit over the whole workspace.
  - Run compile-fail tests for sealed traits and compile-pass tests for open traits.
  - Run a small cancellation smoke (deadline-expired `Cx` causes a real I/O path to fail fast).
  - Emit a deterministic JSON report (see Logging Requirements).

## Logging Requirements

- INFO: enforcement summary: `methods_checked`, `violations`, `compile_fail_cases`, `compile_pass_cases`.
- ERROR: each violation with `crate`, `trait`, `method`, and the observed signature.
- Artifact: deterministic JSON report, e.g. `target/cx_sealed_enforcement_report.json`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All I/O / lock-acquiring / blocking trait methods accept `&Cx` as first parameter.
- [ ] Pure computation methods explicitly excluded from `Cx` (do not take it).
- [ ] `MvccPager`, `BtreeCursorOps`, and `CheckpointPageWriter` are sealed; downstream impl attempts fail.
- [ ] User-extensible traits are NOT sealed; downstream impl attempts compile.
- [ ] Mocks for sealed traits exist and are usable cross-crate.
- [ ] E2E enforcement pass produces a deterministic JSON report and fails CI on any violation.
close_reason: Implemented Cx+sealed enforcement suite, cross-crate mocks, open trait exports, trybuild compile-fail/pass checks, and deterministic report artifact; validation tests passing.

# §9 Cx Parameter Enforcement + Sealed Trait Pattern Validation

## Spec Reference
COMPREHENSIVE_SPEC_FOR_FRANKENSQLITE_V1.md lines 12422-12455 (§9)

## Scope

Ensure the "Cx Everywhere" rule is enforced across all I/O and lock-acquiring
trait methods, and that internal-only traits use the sealed trait pattern to
prevent downstream implementations that could violate MVCC safety invariants.

## Cx Everywhere Rule (from spec)

Every trait method that touches I/O, acquires locks, or could block MUST accept
`&Cx` as its first parameter. This enables:
- **Cancellation:** Any operation can be cancelled by the caller's context
- **Deadline propagation:** Timeout budgets flow through the entire call chain
- **Capability narrowing:** Callers can restrict what callees are allowed to do

Pure computation (e.g., `CollationFunction::compare`, `ScalarFunction::call` for
CPU-only work) does NOT take `Cx`. When in doubt, include `Cx`.

## Sealed Trait Pattern (from spec)

```rust
mod sealed { pub trait Sealed {} }  // private to the defining crate

pub trait MvccPager: sealed::Sealed + Send + Sync { /* ... */ }
```

**Open extension points (user-implementable):** `Vfs`, `VfsFile`,
`ScalarFunction`, `AggregateFunction`, `WindowFunction`, `VirtualTable`,
`VirtualTableCursor`, `CollationFunction`, `Authorizer`.

**Internal-only (sealed):** `MvccPager`, `BtreeCursorOps` (and any similar
trait whose implementations must preserve engine invariants).

Test mocks for sealed traits live alongside the trait definition and are
exported as values/types for other crates to use in tests.

## Unit Test Specifications

### Test 1: Cx parameter audit — VFS traits
Programmatically (or via compile-time assertion) verify that every method on
the `Vfs` and `VfsFile` traits that performs I/O takes `&Cx` as the first
parameter. Methods: `open`, `delete`, `access`, `full_pathname`, `read`,
`write`, `truncate`, `sync`, `file_size`, `lock`, `unlock`, `check_reserved_lock`.

### Test 2: Cx parameter audit — MvccPager trait
Verify that all MvccPager methods that acquire locks or perform I/O take `&Cx`:
`begin`, `acquire_page`, `release_page`, `commit`, `rollback`, `checkpoint`.

### Test 3: Pure computation exclusion
Verify that `CollationFunction::compare` and `ScalarFunction::call` (when
CPU-only) do NOT take `&Cx`. This confirms the rule is not over-applied.

### Test 4: Sealed trait — MvccPager cannot be implemented externally
Write a compile-fail test (using `trybuild` or `compile_fail` doctest):
```rust
struct FakePager;
impl MvccPager for FakePager { ... }  // MUST fail: Sealed not implemented
```
Verify the compiler error mentions the sealed trait bound.

### Test 5: Sealed trait — BtreeCursorOps cannot be implemented externally
Same pattern as Test 4 for `BtreeCursorOps`. Verify compile-fail.

### Test 6: Open traits CAN be implemented externally
Write a positive test: implement `Vfs` and `VfsFile` in a downstream test
crate/module. Verify it compiles and can be used. This confirms sealed is
NOT applied to user-extensible traits.

### Test 7: Test mock for sealed trait is available
Verify that the crate defining `MvccPager` exports a `MockMvccPager` (or
similar) that implements the sealed trait. Verify it can be used in tests
from other crates.

### Test 8: Cancellation via Cx works end-to-end
Create a `Cx` with a deadline in the past. Call a VFS `read` method with it.
Verify the operation returns a cancellation/timeout error rather than
performing I/O.

## Acceptance Criteria
- All I/O and lock-acquiring trait methods confirmed to take `&Cx`
- Pure computation methods confirmed to NOT take `&Cx`
- `MvccPager` and `BtreeCursorOps` confirmed sealed via compile-fail tests
- User-extensible traits (Vfs, VfsFile, etc.) confirmed NOT sealed
- Test mocks for sealed traits are available for cross-crate testing
- Cx cancellation propagation works end-to-end
- All tests pass under `cargo test`
